ad-hoc.hook: AD HOC: Latin for 'for this' — for this one purpose only.
ad-hoc.story: Ad hoc. Made for one particular purpose only, not planned in advance. One monsoon night, water rushed into the ground floor of a small-town hospital. There was no plan for this, so nurses, cleaners and patients' relatives formed an ad hoc team on the spot, passing beds and medicine boxes up the stairs, hand to hand. By morning the job was done, and the team simply melted away. Ad hoc is Latin for "for this": for this one job only. So, what do you call a team put together on the spot for a single task?... Ad hoc.
ad-hoc.example: Without a written schedule, the volunteers at the book fair relied on ad hoc arrangements, deciding each morning who would staff which stall.

gre.s: Rather than developing a coherent policy, the ministry responded to each crisis in a purely ____ fashion, devising quick fixes that were abandoned once the emergency passed.
gre.clue: Rather than developing a coherent policy

allow.hook: GRE trick: ALLOW can mean ADMIT — 'he allowed that he was wrong.'
allow.story: Allow. To permit, and also to admit that something is true. Jake and his grandfather argued all through dinner about whose generation had it harder. Grandfather spoke of walking to school through knee-deep mud; Jake spoke of city traffic. At last the old man put down his tea. "I will allow that your traffic is worse than my mud." Jake grinned and allowed that the mud sounded terrible too. When you allow a point into the argument, you admit it is true. So, what verb means to admit that the other side has a point?... Allow.
allow.example: The referee later allowed that the goal might have been offside, though he insisted he had no clear view at the time.

gre.s: Even her harshest critics would ____ that her research was meticulous, though they continued to dispute the conclusions she drew from it.
gre.clue: though they continued to dispute the conclusions

appropriate.hook: Two pronunciations: ap-PRO-pree-it means SUITABLE; ap-PRO-pree-ate means to TAKE as your PROPERTY.
appropriate.story: Appropriate. As an adjective, suitable for the situation. As a verb, to take something for your own use, often without permission. Ryan spent a month painting a poster for his university's spring festival. A week later, a senior student hung it in the hall with his own name at the bottom. Ryan felt his face burn. The senior had appropriated his work, and it was hardly appropriate behaviour. Inside appropriate hides the root of property, meaning your own: to appropriate is to make something your property. So, what verb means to take someone else's work as your own?... Appropriate.
appropriate.example: During the war, the army appropriated several private villas in the hills and turned them into field hospitals.

gre.s: Critics accused the fashion house of choosing to ____ traditional Jamdani motifs for its new collection without ever crediting the weavers who had developed them over centuries.
gre.clue: without ever crediting the weavers

august.hook: GRE trick: au-GUST, like Emperor AUGUSTUS, majestic.
august.story: August. Respected and impressive; majestic. On convocation day, an eighty-year-old professor walked onto the stage in his black gown, white-haired and perfectly upright. Two thousand graduates rose to their feet, and even the noisy photographers fell silent. Emily felt a shiver of pride just to be in that august hall, before such an august figure. Think of Augustus, the Roman emperor whose very title meant the revered one; an august person carries that same grandeur. So, what word describes a presence so dignified that a whole hall stands in silence?... August.
august.example: The journal, founded in 1887, is one of the most august publications in the field, and acceptance there can make a young chemist's career.

gre.s: The young scholar felt intimidated in the ____ company of Nobel laureates and former heads of state, and barely dared to speak during the entire dinner.
gre.clue: Nobel laureates and former heads of state

base.hook: GRE trick: BASE means LOW morally, like the bottom of a building.
base.story: Base. Shamefully dishonourable and selfish, without moral decency. During a flood in a river town, one shopkeeper locked away his rice and sold it to hungry families at three times the normal price. When a relief volunteer begged him to be fair, he only raised the price again. The villagers were disgusted. Of all the things they saw that year, his greed was the most base. Picture the lowest floor of a building: a base act sinks to the very bottom of human behaviour. So, what word describes cheating desperate people for profit?... Base.
base.example: Spreading false rumors about a rival candidate's family was a base tactic, and even his own supporters were ashamed of it.

gre.s: Investigators concluded that the official had acted from the most ____ motives, since he had accepted bribes to approve a dam he knew was unsafe.
gre.clue: accepted bribes to approve a dam he knew was unsafe

champion.hook: GRE trick: to CHAMPION a cause means to fight FOR it.
champion.story: Champion. To publicly support or fight for a cause. When the council planned to fill in an old pond in a quiet town to build a market, a retired schoolteacher named Margaret refused to stay quiet. She wrote to newspapers, gathered her former students, and spoke at every public meeting. When the plan was finally dropped, Margaret hugged the children who had marched with her. She had championed the pond. The trick: a sports champion wins for himself, but when you champion a cause, you fight for something beyond yourself. So, what verb means to stand up publicly for a cause?... Champion.
champion.example: The young librarian championed a reading program for street children in Kamalapur, persuading local businesses to donate books and snacks.

gre.s: Though she was initially skeptical of renewable energy, the senator went on to ____ it more vigorously than any of her colleagues, sponsoring dozens of bills to expand solar power.
gre.clue: sponsoring dozens of bills to expand solar power

contemporary.story: Contemporary. Belonging to the same period as someone else; also, of the present day. In nineteen thirty, the Indian poet Tagore sat with Albert Einstein near Berlin and talked about truth and reality. Hannah read about it for her history class and was amazed. The poet she grew up reciting and the scientist from her physics book were contemporaries, alive at the same time. Today the word can also mean modern, as in contemporary art. Con means with, and tempus means time: with the same time. So, what word describes two people who lived in the same era?... Contemporary.
contemporary.example: Shakespeare and Cervantes were contemporary writers, and the two men died within days of each other in the spring of 1616.

gre.s: Historians prefer ____ accounts of the battle, written by eyewitnesses, to the romanticized versions that poets composed a full century later.
gre.clue: written by eyewitnesses

content.hook: CON-TENT (stress on TENT): happy in your little tent.
content.story: Content. Peacefully satisfied. Tom rows a wooden boat on a wide river. Each evening he sits outside his tin-roofed house with a cup of sweet tea, watching the sky turn orange over the water. When a visitor from the city asked whether he wanted more from life, Tom smiled, and shook his head. "I have enough." He was truly content. Content is the root of contentment; do not mix it up with the content of a book, which is what the book contains. So, what word describes someone peacefully satisfied with what they have?... Content.
content.example: After years of chasing promotions in Dhaka, Kamal was finally content to run a small guesthouse among the tea gardens of Srimangal.

gre.s: Unlike her restless siblings, who constantly chased new ventures, she was ____ with the quiet life of a village schoolteacher and never sought promotion.
gre.clue: Unlike her restless siblings, who constantly chased new ventures

conventional.hook: CONVENTIONAL: what everyone agreed on at the CONVENTION.
conventional.story: Conventional. Following accepted customs and standards; traditional. At a family dinner, Ethan's parents discussed his future: doctor, engineer, or a government job. Safe, respected, conventional. Then Ethan quietly said he wanted to photograph tigers in the mangrove forests. The table went silent, and his mother slowly put down her spoon. A convention is a meeting where people come to an agreement, so the conventional path is the one everyone has already agreed on. So, what word describes the safe, traditional path that everyone expects you to take?... Conventional.
conventional.example: The architect rejected the conventional glass tower and designed an office block wrapped in screens of living bamboo.

gre.s: Defying ____ wisdom, which held that the disease was inherited, the researcher argued that it was caused by an environmental toxin.
gre.clue: which held that the disease was inherited

discount.hook: GRE trick: DISCOUNT means to ignore, not just lower the price.
discount.story: Discount. To regard something as unimportant or untrustworthy, and set it aside. When a neighbour told Lily's grandmother that bitter gourd juice could replace her insulin, Lily felt a flash of worry. But the doctor gently discounted the advice and kept her grandmother on her medicine. After that, Lily learned to discount the miracle cures forwarded in family chats. The trick: in a shop, a discount cuts the price; in an argument, discounting a claim cuts its value to almost nothing. So, what verb means to dismiss a claim as not worth trusting?... Discount.
discount.example: Coach Habib discounted the injury rumors and named his striker in the starting eleven for the final.

gre.s: Scientists were quick to ____ the anonymous report, since its author offered no data and had a long history of fabricating results.
gre.clue: had a long history of fabricating results

documentary.story: Documentary. Based on real documents and records. For years, Nathan's family argued over who owned a small plot of land in the countryside. Every uncle had a story, but stories proved nothing. Then Nathan opened his great-grandfather's old tin trunk and found the deed, the paper brown and brittle, the seal still clear. His aunt pressed a hand to her mouth. At last there was documentary proof. The word has document right inside it: documentary evidence is evidence written down on paper. So, what kind of evidence rests on written records rather than memory?... Documentary.
documentary.example: No documentary proof of the land sale survived the fire, so the court had to rely on the testimony of elderly villagers.

gre.s: The historian's claims rest on solid ____ evidence, including letters, ledgers, and court records from the period.
gre.clue: including letters, ledgers, and court records

economy.hook: GRE trick: ECONOMY of words means using no more words than needed.
economy.story: Economy. Using money, effort or words carefully, without waste. Olivia's mother runs a family of five on one small salary. She buys vegetables in season, measures cooking oil by the spoon, and turns last night's leftovers into breakfast. Nothing is ever wasted. Years later, Olivia writes her essays the same way, with an economy of words that her teacher praises. Think of economy class on a plane: no extra space, nothing wasted. So, what word means careful use of money, effort or words, with nothing wasted?... Economy.
economy.example: With remarkable economy of movement, the old carpenter smoothed the plank in a few strokes while his apprentice watched in silence.

gre.s: Her prose is admired for its remarkable ____: she never uses three words where one will do, and every sentence seems to earn its place.
gre.clue: she never uses three words where one will do

elementary.story: Elementary. Basic; belonging to the simplest beginning stages. On the first day of his GRE quant course, Kevin felt almost insulted. The teacher started with fractions, percentages and the area of a triangle, things he had learned in class six. Then his first practice test came back, and he had missed four elementary questions. He stopped complaining and started practising. Elementary comes from element, the basic building block of everything. So, what word describes the simplest, most basic ideas a subject begins with?... Elementary.
elementary.example: The first experiment in the chemistry lab was elementary, just timing how quickly salt dissolves in warm and cold water.

gre.s: Although the textbook advertises itself as an advanced treatment of the subject, its exercises are so ____ that a first-year student could finish them in an afternoon.
gre.clue: a first-year student could finish them in an afternoon

entitled.hook: ENTITLED: acts like he holds a royal TITLE.
entitled.story: Entitled. Feeling owed special treatment you have not earned. At the university canteen, students waited in a long line for lunch. A boy in designer sunglasses walked straight to the front and said, "Do you know who my father is?" The cashier calmly pointed to the back of the line, and a few students quietly cheered. He was entitled, acting as if rules were only for other people. Picture him wearing an invisible royal title: an entitled person behaves like a lord without ever earning the crown. So, what word describes someone who expects privileges they never earned?... Entitled.
entitled.example: The entitled customer at the Gulshan restaurant demanded a free dessert simply because he had waited five minutes for his table.

gre.s: The coach was frustrated by the star player's ____ attitude, as he expected special privileges while skipping the practices everyone else attended.
gre.clue: expected special privileges

facility.hook: GRE trick: FACILITY means ease — she has a facility for languages.
facility.story: Facility. A natural ease or skill in doing something. Grace's little brother has never had a single music lesson, yet he can hear a song once on the radio and play it on the harmonium straight away. His fingers find the notes as if they already knew them. When he finishes, the whole family claps and cheers. Everyone notices his facility with melody. Facility shares its Latin root with facile and facilitate, all from the word for easy, so a facility is a skill that comes easily. So, what word means a natural ease at doing something?... Facility.
facility.example: Rafsan's facility with numbers made him the person everyone called whenever the family's tax forms had to be filled in.

gre.s: Despite her obvious ____ with languages, which allowed her to pick up conversational Italian in a matter of weeks, she struggled for years with basic arithmetic.
gre.clue: pick up conversational Italian in a matter of weeks

frank.hook: FRANK: Frank always tells it straight.
frank.story: Frank. Open, honest and direct. Daniel nervously handed his first short story to his mentor, hoping for praise. She read it, put down her tea, and said, "The opening is dull, and the ending is borrowed. But the third page is brilliant. Build from there." It stung, yet Daniel walked home grateful. She had been frank with him, and her frank words helped more than any polite ones. The trick: the old French word franc meant free, so frank speech is free of disguise. So, what word describes feedback that is open, honest and direct?... Frank.
frank.example: In a frank interview, the retired captain admitted that his team had been badly unprepared for the tour of Australia.

gre.s: Rather than offering the vague reassurances his patients expected, the doctor was always ____, telling them plainly what their prognosis was even when the news was grim.
gre.clue: telling them plainly what their prognosis was

minute.hook: MINUTE (my-NOOT): as tiny as a MINI thing.
minute.story: Minute. Extremely small; also, precise and detailed. In a weaving village near the city, Sophie watched an old weaver lift threads one by one, working a minute flower into the cloth. Each petal was smaller than a grain of rice. One sari can take him months of such minute work, and Sophie could hardly breathe as she watched. Unlike the minute on a clock, this minute is about size, and it shares its root with diminish and minuscule, both about smallness. So, what word describes detail so tiny you must lean close to see it?... Minute.
minute.example: Engineers found that a minute crack in a turbine blade, thinner than a hair, had caused the entire engine to fail.

gre.s: Although the changes to the manuscript appeared ____, they altered the meaning of several key passages in ways that scholars still debate.
gre.clue: they altered the meaning of several key passages

noble.hook: NOBLE: like a NOBEL Prize-worthy character.
noble.story: Noble. Having high moral qualities; also, aristocratic. A rickshaw puller in the city found a bag under his seat holding a small fortune. He had rent to pay and a daughter who needed school fees. Still, he spent the whole day searching until he found the owner, returned every note, and refused a reward. People who read the story felt their throats tighten. It was noble, nobler than any title. The trick: noble is the opposite of base; base sinks low, noble rises high. So, what word describes an act of high moral character, like returning money you badly need?... Noble.
noble.example: Giving up his own scholarship so that his younger sister could study abroad was a noble sacrifice, though Nayeem never spoke of it.

gre.s: Although she could easily have kept the reward for herself, she made the ____ choice to donate it to the families of the miners who had died.
gre.clue: Although she could easily have kept the reward for herself

plastic.hook: GRE trick: PLASTIC means moldable, like clay — not just the material.
plastic.story: Plastic. Easily shaped or moulded; flexible and adaptable. Rachel's little son moved from a small town to the big city at four. Within months he was chattering in a new accent, picking up words from cousins and cartoons. Rachel worried, but her neighbour, a doctor, smiled and said, "A child's brain is plastic. It reshapes itself as it learns." The word comes from a Greek verb meaning to mould, which is also how the material plastic got its name. Think of soft clay in a potter's hands. So, what word describes something that can be easily shaped and reshaped?... Plastic.
plastic.example: Young children's accents are remarkably plastic, so a girl who moves from Sylhet to London at five may soon sound entirely British.

gre.s: Contrary to the old belief that the adult brain is fixed, researchers now regard it as remarkably ____, capable of forming new connections throughout life.
gre.clue: capable of forming new connections throughout life

prime.hook: GRE trick: to PRIME is to PREPARE, like priming a wall before painting.
prime.story: Prime. To prepare someone or something for action. In the last week before Megan's GRE, her tutor taught her nothing new. Instead, every morning at nine, the exact hour of her real test, he handed her a timed practice set, so her mind would wake up sharp at that time. He was priming her for the big day. It is just like a house painter priming a wall with a base coat before the real colour goes on. So, what verb means to get someone ready for action?... Prime.
prime.example: Before the debate, the team captain primed each speaker with the opposing side's strongest arguments and the best replies to them.

gre.s: Before the negotiations began, the lawyer took care to ____ her client, rehearsing every likely question so that nothing would catch him off guard.
gre.clue: rehearsing every likely question so that nothing would catch him off guard

radical.story: Radical. Favouring drastic change; also, relating to the very roots of something. For years, a riverside village fought floods with small fixes: sandbags, higher plinths, new drains. Every monsoon, the water won. Then a young engineer named Marcus made a radical proposal: build homes on floating platforms that rise with the water. The elders stared at him in disbelief. Radical comes from the Latin radix, meaning root, so radical change goes all the way down to the roots. So, what word describes change that is drastic and fundamental?... Radical.
radical.example: Moving the whole newsroom from print to online publishing in a single year was a radical step for the century-old newspaper.

gre.s: Rather than tinkering with the existing curriculum, the new principal proposed a ____ overhaul that would reshape every course from the ground up.
gre.clue: reshape every course from the ground up

reflect.hook: REFLECT: like a mirror, turning thoughts back on yourself.
reflect.story: Reflect. To think carefully about something; also, to show or express it. After failing her first GRE practice test, Jessica looked at the score, and did not rush into another one. She sat by her hostel window with the report and reflected. Which questions had she rushed? Which words had she only guessed? Three months later, her final score reflected all that patient work. Think of a mirror: it reflects your face, and when you reflect, you turn your thoughts back on yourself. So, what verb means to think deeply, or to show something clearly?... Reflect.
reflect.example: Rising rents in Dhanmondi reflect the growing demand for apartments near the city's best schools.

gre.s: The novel's bleak tone may ____ the author's own despair during the war years, a period she described in her letters as the darkest of her life.
gre.clue: a period she described in her letters as the darkest of her life

remarkable.story: Remarkable. Unusual enough to be noticed and admired; exceptional. Chloe's neighbour sold vegetables at the city market for thirty years, waking before dawn in every season. Alone, she raised four children and sent all four to university. On the day her youngest became a doctor, the whole lane came out to congratulate her, and Chloe cried a little too. Everyone agreed her life was remarkable. The word is simply remark plus able: something remarkable is worth remarking on. So, what word describes an achievement so exceptional that people cannot stop talking about it?... Remarkable.
remarkable.example: The rescued hawk made a remarkable recovery, flying again only three weeks after the vet set its broken wing.

gre.s: What makes the novel ____ is not its plot, which is entirely conventional, but its narrator, who speaks in a voice unlike any other in modern fiction.
gre.clue: a voice unlike any other in modern fiction

remote.hook: REMOTE: far away like a REMOTE village, or a remote chance.
remote.story: Remote. Far away and distant; also, slight or faint, as in a remote chance. Tyler's grandparents live on a remote sandbar island in the middle of a great river, reachable only by boat. One stormy evening, Tyler asked the old boatman whether the ferry would still run. The boatman looked at the black sky and the churning water. "Only a remote chance, son." Think of a remote control: it works from far away, and a remote chance is just as far from happening. So, what word means far away, or so slight it hardly exists?... Remote.
remote.example: The odds that the asteroid will strike Earth are remote, but astronomers plan to keep tracking it for the next fifty years.

gre.s: Although the doctors admitted there was a ____ chance that the experimental treatment would succeed, they warned the family not to raise their hopes.
gre.clue: warned the family not to raise their hopes

slight.hook: GRE trick: SLIGHT as a verb means to snub someone.
slight.story: Slight. As an adjective, small or minor. As a verb, to insult someone by ignoring them; as a noun, the insult itself. At a cousin's wedding by the sea, the host greeted every guest with hugs. When Ava's mother reached the gate, he looked past her and turned to the next guest. She smiled politely, but Ava saw her hands tremble. It was no slight mistake; it was a slight. The trick: to slight someone is to treat them as slight, too small to notice. So, what verb means to insult someone by treating them as not worth noticing?... Slight.
slight.example: The novelist took it as a slight when her name was left off the festival poster, even though she was its keynote speaker.

gre.s: The ambassador was offended by what she regarded as a deliberate ____: she had been seated at the far end of the table, away from every other head of delegation.
gre.clue: seated at the far end of the table, away from every other head of delegation

sound.hook: GRE trick: SOUND means solid and valid — a sound argument.
sound.story: Sound. Based on valid reasoning; also, in good condition and reliable. When Brian told his parents he wanted to study in Germany, his father frowned. Then Brian laid out his plan: savings for the first year, a partial scholarship, a part-time job already arranged, and a clear career goal. His father read it twice, then nodded. "Your reasoning is sound." Think of the phrase safe and sound: a sound argument is whole and solid, with no cracks in it. So, what word describes reasoning that is solid and reliable?... Sound.
sound.example: The judge found the engineer's analysis sound and ordered the builder to repair the cracked pillars at his own expense.

gre.s: Although the argument's conclusion was surprising, its reasoning was ____, resting on well-established data and careful logic.
gre.clue: resting on well-established data and careful logic

stem-from.hook: STEM FROM: like a plant's STEM growing from its root.
stem-from.story: Stem from. To come from, or to be caused by. Abby's little sister would never go near the pond behind their village home, even on the hottest days. One evening their mother explained that the fear stemmed from an old accident: at three, the girl had slipped off a boat and been pulled out just in time. Now Abby understood, and she held her sister's hand a little tighter. Picture a plant: its stem grows from hidden roots, just as a problem can stem from a hidden cause. So, what phrase means to originate from something?... Stem from.
stem-from.example: Many of the river's pollution problems stem from tanneries upstream that dump untreated waste directly into the water.

gre.s: Most of the town's current troubles ____ a single decision made decades ago: closing the factory that once employed half its residents.
gre.clue: a single decision made decades ago

suspect.hook: GRE trick: SUSPECT as an adjective means questionable.
suspect.story: Suspect. Not to be trusted; of doubtful quality. A website promised Justin a full scholarship abroad if he paid a five hundred dollar fee within twenty-four hours. The page was full of spelling mistakes, gave no office address, and listed a phone number nobody answered. His professor took one look and said, "This offer is suspect." Justin realised how close he had come to paying. Usually a suspect is a person the police doubt; here the word describes anything that deserves the same doubt. So, what word describes an offer or a claim that cannot be trusted?... Suspect.
suspect.example: Curators considered the painting's signature suspect, since the artist had always signed with his initials and never with his full name.

gre.s: The study's conclusions are ____, since it was funded by the very company whose product it praises and its raw data have never been released.
gre.clue: funded by the very company whose product it praises

universal.story: Universal. Done by or relating to everyone; true in all cases. At the start of each school year, children across the country, in city schools and on river islands alike, receive brand-new free textbooks. Mike still remembers the smell of fresh paper and ink the morning his daughter came home hugging hers. The goal behind it is universal education: every child, with no exceptions. Universal comes from universe, everything that exists, so a universal rule leaves no one out. So, what word describes something that applies to everyone, everywhere?... Universal.
universal.example: Gravity is universal, so the same force that pulls a mango from its branch also keeps the moon circling Earth.

gre.s: The proposal enjoyed nearly ____ support within the committee: of its forty members, only one voted against it.
gre.clue: only one voted against it

wanting.hook: GRE trick: FOUND WANTING means found lacking, not desiring.
wanting.story: Wanting. Lacking; not good enough. Andrew spent weeks on his first research paper and handed it in proudly. It came back with one line in red ink: "The analysis is wanting." For a moment he thought his professor simply wanted more of it. Then he understood that his analysis fell short, and he opened his laptop again. In older English, want meant lack, as in the saying "for want of a nail, the shoe was lost." So, what word describes work that is lacking, not good enough?... Wanting.
wanting.example: Judged against modern safety codes, the old stadium's fire exits are sadly wanting, so the city has closed the upper stands.

gre.s: The proposal was praised for its ambition, but on close examination its financial projections were found ____, resting on assumptions that no serious economist would accept.
gre.clue: resting on assumptions that no serious economist would accept

abstract.hook: ABSTRACT: pulled away (abs-tract) from the physical world.
abstract.story: Abstract. Existing as an idea rather than as a physical thing. On Memorial Day, little Leo stood with his father at the war memorial. He tugged his father's hand. "Dad, where is freedom? Can I touch it?" His father knelt beside him. "You can touch this stone, but freedom is abstract. You feel it in your heart." Abstract comes from Latin for pulled away, the same pull as in tractor: an abstract idea is pulled away from solid things. So, what word describes something like freedom or justice, which exists only as an idea?... Abstract.
abstract.example: Mahbub found economics too abstract until a summer job at his uncle's rice mill showed him supply and demand in action.

gre.s: The professor's lectures were so ____ that students begged for concrete examples, unable to connect her elegant theories to anything in the real world.
gre.clue: students begged for concrete examples

accessible.story: Accessible. Easy to reach or use; also, easy to understand. For two years, Natalie, who uses a wheelchair, could only look up at her university library from the bottom of its steep steps. Friends carried books down to her. This winter, a ramp and a lift were finally built. On the first morning she rolled in by herself and smiled at the shelves. The library was accessible at last. The word holds access inside it: what is accessible gives easy access. So, what word describes a place, or an idea, that is easy to reach?... Accessible.
accessible.example: Shahana's science podcast makes genetics accessible to teenagers by explaining each idea through a simple kitchen experiment.

gre.s: Unlike his dense earlier treatises, which only specialists could follow, the philosopher's final book is remarkably ____, written in plain prose for a general audience.
gre.clue: written in plain prose for a general audience

advocate.hook: ADVOCATE: in Bangladesh, a lawyer is literally called an 'advocate', someone who speaks FOR you.
advocate.story: Advocate. A person who publicly supports a cause; as a verb, to argue for it in public. Maria works in a garment factory outside the city. Every morning she watched mothers leave crying babies with neighbours. She became an advocate for a factory daycare. She collected two hundred signatures and spoke at every meeting, her voice shaking but steady. A year later, the daycare opened. Advocate shares its root with voice and vocal; in many countries, lawyers are called advocates because they speak for you. So, what do you call someone who speaks out publicly for a cause?... Advocate.
advocate.example: As an advocate of cycle lanes, the young city planner rode to every council meeting on her battered bicycle.

gre.s: A longtime ____ of renewable energy, the senator surprised no one when she championed the solar subsidy bill.
gre.clue: surprised no one when she championed

aesthetic.hook: AESTHETIC: think 'A STYLISH thing', all about beauty.
aesthetic.story: Aesthetic. Having to do with beauty and how we appreciate it. In a narrow workshop in the old city, Joe paints peacocks, rivers and film stars on rickshaw panels. A rickshaw runs just as well without them. The paintings exist for one reason: the aesthetic pleasure of everyone who watches them pass. Joe says he is giving the street something beautiful. The trick: aesthetic and anaesthetic share a Greek root about feeling; an anaesthetic stops all feeling, while aesthetic is about feeling beauty. So, what word describes anything to do with beauty and its appreciation?... Aesthetic.
aesthetic.example: The museum chose the old textile mill for aesthetic reasons as well as practical ones, admiring its brick arches and tall windows.

gre.s: Although the bridge is structurally sound, critics fault its ____ shortcomings, calling it the ugliest structure in the city.
gre.clue: calling it the ugliest structure in the city

cease.story: Cease. To stop happening, or to stop doing something. For three days the monsoon rain drummed on the tin roof of Lucy's village house in the hills. Clothes would not dry, the courtyard became a pond, and the whole family stayed indoors. On the fourth morning, Lucy woke to a strange silence. The rain had ceased. She ran barefoot into the wet courtyard, where the air smelled of mud and mango leaves. Think of a ceasefire: the moment the guns cease firing. So, what verb means to come to an end, or simply stop?... Cease.
cease.example: The factory ceased production in 2019, and its empty sheds now shelter stray dogs and the occasional film crew.

gre.s: The two factions agreed to ____ hostilities during the festival, but the fragile truce collapsed only days after the celebrations ended.
gre.clue: the fragile truce

cluster.hook: CLUSTER: like a bunch of grapes clustered together.
cluster.story: Cluster. A group of similar things close together; as a verb, to gather in a group. When the admission results went up on the notice board at the university, hundreds of students clustered around it, shoulder to shoulder, phones held high. Sam squeezed through the cluster, ran a finger down the list, and stopped at his own name. His friends cheered, and the cluster around him only grew. Picture lychees in June, hanging in a tight cluster from a single branch. So, what word means a tight group of similar things, or to gather into one?... Cluster.
cluster.example: On cold winter mornings in Rangpur, rickshaw pullers cluster around the tea stalls, warming their hands on clay cups.

gre.s: Rather than being evenly distributed across the country, the new technology firms tend to ____ in a few urban centers, where investors and skilled engineers are concentrated.
gre.clue: Rather than being evenly distributed across the country

coin.hook: GRE trick: to COIN a word is to MINT a brand-new one, like a new coin.
coin.story: Coin. To invent a new word or expression. One afternoon, rain began to fall while the sun was still shining. Ben's five-year-old sister pressed her face to the window and shouted, "Look, sun-rain!" The whole family laughed, but the word stuck. Now her uncles say sun-rain too, and Ben tells her proudly that she coined it. The trick: a mint stamps out a brand-new coin that passes from hand to hand, and when you coin a word, you stamp out a new one that people pass along. So, what verb means to invent a brand-new expression?... Coin.
coin.example: Richard Owen, the anatomist who coined the word dinosaur, built it from Greek roots meaning terrible lizard.

gre.s: Rather than borrow an existing term, the psychologist decided to ____ a new one, since no word in the language captured the phenomenon she had discovered.
gre.clue: no word in the language captured the phenomenon

compelling.hook: COMPELLING: it COMPELS, or forces, you to pay attention.
compelling.story: Compelling. So interesting or convincing that you cannot ignore it. Alex promised himself just one chapter of a mystery novel before bed. Then the power went out, so he kept reading by the light of his phone, the fan silent. When he turned the last page, the call to dawn prayer was drifting through the window. He had not slept at all. The story was simply too compelling. Compelling comes from compel, to force: a compelling story forces you to keep going. So, what word describes a story or argument you simply cannot put down?... Compelling.
compelling.example: The defense lawyer offered a compelling alibi, backed by bus tickets and a shopkeeper who remembered serving her client that night.

gre.s: Although the evidence for the hypothesis was once considered thin, the new fossil discoveries make a ____ case for it.
gre.clue: Although the evidence for the hypothesis was once considered thin

comply.story: Comply. To act according to a rule, request or command. At the GRE test centre in the city, the officer asked every candidate to remove watches, empty pockets and lock phones away. Emma complied at once and placed her things in a locker. The young man behind her argued for ten minutes about his lucky watch and nearly missed his slot. Emma sat down calm and ready. Comply comes from the same Latin root as complete: you complete, or fill out, what is asked of you. So, what verb means to follow a rule or request?... Comply.
comply.example: Passengers who refused to comply with the mask rule were politely asked to leave the train at the next station.

gre.s: Companies that refuse to ____ with the new environmental regulations will face heavy fines and possible closure.
gre.clue: will face heavy fines and possible closure

compound.hook: GRE trick: COMPOUND interest grows; a COMPOUNDED problem grows worse.
compound.story: Compound. To make a problem worse. Ten-year-old Danny broke his mother's favourite glass bowl, a gift from her own mother. He hid the pieces under his bed and said the cat had done it. When his mother found the pieces, it was the lie that hurt her more than the bowl. By lying, Danny had compounded his mistake. That night he confessed, and she held him close. Think of compound interest, which grows on top of itself; a compounded problem grows worse on top of itself. So, what verb means to make a bad situation even worse?... Compound.
compound.example: A dropped catch in the final over compounded the bowler's misery, and his team lost the match by a single run.

gre.s: The governor's initial delay in ordering an evacuation was a serious error, but her subsequent refusal to admit it served only to ____ the damage to her reputation.
gre.clue: her subsequent refusal to admit it

compromise.hook: GRE trick: COMPROMISE also means to WEAKEN — a compromised password.
compromise.story: Compromise. To settle a disagreement by each side giving something up; also, to weaken or put at risk. Chris's parents could not agree on a winter trip. His father longed for the sea at the long sandy beach; his mother dreamed of the green tea gardens in the hills. After a long evening of debate, they reached a compromise: tea gardens this year, the sea next year. The trick: a compromise between people is healthy, but a compromised password or a compromised bridge has been weakened. So, what word means meeting halfway, with each side giving a little?... Compromise.
compromise.example: Sharing your password with a friend can compromise the security of every account linked to your email address.

gre.s: Engineers warned that cutting corners on materials would ____ the structural integrity of the bridge, putting thousands of commuters at risk.
gre.clue: putting thousands of commuters at risk

consensus.story: Consensus. Broad agreement shared by most or all of a group. In a northern village, families gathered under a huge banyan tree to decide where the new tube well should go. Some wanted it by the market, others near the mosque. Then an old woman pointed out that children walked the farthest for water, so it should stand beside the primary school. One by one, heads nodded. By sunset there was consensus. Consensus and consent share a Latin root: a consensus is when nearly everyone gives consent. So, what word means broad agreement across a whole group?... Consensus.
consensus.example: After two long evenings of debate, the residents of the Mirpur building reached a consensus to paint the stairwell bright yellow.

gre.s: Although a few dissenters remain, the scientific ____ is that human activity is the primary driver of recent warming.
gre.clue: Although a few dissenters remain

conviction.story: Conviction. A firmly held belief; also, an official ruling that someone is guilty. Fifty years ago, in a river village, Laura's grandmother decided her daughters would go to school. Neighbours whispered that girls belonged in the kitchen. She simply walked them to school every morning. Her conviction never wavered, and today two of those daughters are teachers. Conviction and convince share a Latin root: a conviction is something you are convinced of, and a court's conviction means the judge is convinced of guilt. So, what word means a belief held so firmly that nothing shakes it?... Conviction.
conviction.example: The old ferry captain told his passengers with quiet conviction that the storm would pass before they reached Barisal.

gre.s: Though the young activist spoke softly, she argued with such ____ that even her skeptical audience could not doubt she believed every word.
gre.clue: could not doubt she believed every word

divorced.hook: GRE trick: DIVORCED FROM reality means disconnected from it.
divorced.story: Divorced. Cut off from something, with no real link to it. Josh showed his sister his new GRE timetable: twelve hours of study a day, starting at five every morning. She raised an eyebrow. "Josh, you work full time, and you have never woken up before eight." He looked again, and laughed at himself. The plan was completely divorced from reality. The trick: a divorced couple no longer share a home, and an idea divorced from reality no longer shares anything with the real world. So, what word describes a plan cut off from real life?... Divorced.
divorced.example: Raised in a gated compound with a driver and a cook, the diplomat's children grew up divorced from ordinary life in the city.

gre.s: Critics charged that the economist's elegant models were ____ from reality, ignoring how actual consumers behave.
gre.clue: ignoring how actual consumers behave

elaborate.hook: E-LABOR-ATE: lots of LABOR went into it.
elaborate.story: Elaborate. As an adjective, detailed and complicated. As a verb, to explain in more detail. The night before her wedding, Isabella sat for four hours while an artist covered her hands in henna: peacocks, vines, tiny paisleys, even the groom's name hidden inside a leaf. Her cousins crowded close. "How do you plan something so elaborate?" one asked. The artist smiled and elaborated, sketching each step on paper. Inside elaborate hides labour, and its Latin source really means to work something out with effort. So, what word describes a design that is highly detailed and complex?... Elaborate.
elaborate.example: The thief's elaborate plan involved a fake delivery van, two disguises, and a tunnel dug under the jeweller's back wall.

gre.s: Far from the simple sketch the client had requested, the architect produced a highly ____ design, crowded with ornament and dozens of interlocking spaces.
gre.clue: Far from the simple sketch the client had requested

inform.hook: GRE trick: experience INFORMS art means it SHAPES it from within.
inform.story: Inform. To tell someone facts; also, to shape or influence something from within. Aaron grew up on a sandbar island in a great river, where the river swallowed his family's land twice before he turned twelve. Today he is a filmmaker in the city. Every film he makes is informed by that childhood: the roar of the water, the fear of loss, the courage of starting again. His memories inform each scene he shoots. Inform literally means to give form to, so your experiences can inform your work by giving it shape. So, what verb means to shape something deeply from within?... Inform.
inform.example: Her childhood among the weavers of Tangail informs every pattern the designer creates, from silk scarves to hotel carpets.

gre.s: Her years as a war correspondent continue to ____ her fiction: nearly every novel she writes returns to scenes of conflict and displacement.
gre.clue: nearly every novel she writes returns to scenes of conflict and displacement

intimate.hook: GRE trick: as a verb, INTIMATE means to hint, like whispering an intimate secret.
intimate.story: Intimate. To suggest something indirectly; to hint. Two days before the final exam, the chemistry teacher, Miss Parker, closed her book and smiled. "I will not tell you what is on the paper. But if I were you, I would read chapter seven twice." Nobody needed more. She had intimated exactly where to look, and Rebecca spent the whole night on chapter seven. As a verb, intimate comes from the Latin for innermost: you let an inner thought slip out quietly. So, what verb means to hint at something without saying it directly?... Intimate.
intimate.example: The landlord intimated that the rent might rise next year, though he refused to name a figure.

gre.s: Though she never stated it outright, the minister seemed to ____ that the government would soon change its policy.
gre.clue: Though she never stated it outright

keen.hook: KEEN: a KEEN knife is sharp; a keen student is eager.
keen.story: Keen. Sharp and highly developed; also, eager. At dawn on the great river, the old fisherman Walter stood still in his boat, watching the grey water. His grandson saw nothing. Then Walter pointed to a faint silver flicker far away. "Look. Cast there." The net came up shining with fish. The boy stared at his grandfather, amazed by his keen eyes, and became keen to learn everything he knew. The trick: a keen knife is sharp, a keen eye is sharp, and a keen student is sharp with eagerness. So, what word describes senses that are sharp and highly developed?... Keen.
keen.example: A keen sense of smell lets trained airport dogs detect explosives hidden inside sealed suitcases.

gre.s: Her ____ eye for detail made her an invaluable editor; she routinely caught errors that had slipped past three previous readers.
gre.clue: caught errors that had slipped past three previous readers

liability.hook: LIABILITY: something you're LIABLE for, a burden.
liability.story: Liability. Something that holds you back; also, legal responsibility. In his neighbourhood team in the city, Carter could hit sixes over the mango tree, but he dropped every catch that came his way. In the final, he dropped three. His captain put an arm around him. "Your bat wins matches, but in the field you are a liability. Let us practise catching." The trick: an accountant writes assets on one side and liabilities on the other; an asset lifts you up, a liability pulls you down. So, what word means a weakness that holds a person or team back?... Liability.
liability.example: In the summer heat, the team's ageing goalkeeper became a liability, too tired by the second half to dive for anything.

gre.s: His reckless remarks to the press, once dismissed as charming, had become a serious ____ for the campaign, costing it the support of several key donors.
gre.clue: costing it the support of several key donors

modest.hook: MODEST: MODERATE, not boastful, not extreme.
modest.story: Modest. Humble about your achievements; also, moderate or small in size. When Owen came first in the board exam results, reporters crowded into his family's modest two-room house. They asked how he had done it. He looked at the floor, then pointed at his mother. "She woke up with me every morning. Write about her." Everyone loved how modest he was. Modest and moderate share a Latin root meaning measure: a modest person keeps praise within measure, and a modest house is of measured size. So, what word describes someone humble about success?... Modest.
modest.example: The bakery started with a modest budget of fifty thousand taka and one secondhand oven in a Mohammadpur garage.

gre.s: Despite the company's grand promises of transformation, the new policy produced only ____ gains, raising productivity by barely two percent.
gre.clue: raising productivity by barely two percent

partial.hook: PARTIAL: takes PART of one side, or is only a PART.
partial.story: Partial. Biased in favour of one side; also, incomplete. At a winter rice-cake contest at their village home, Grandmother was the only judge. Her eldest grandson made perfect steamed rice cakes. Her six-year-old granddaughter made lumpy ones dripping with date molasses. Grandmother gave first prize to the little one, who clapped her sticky hands, and nobody was surprised. Everyone knew she was partial to her baby. The trick: a partial judge takes part with one side, while a partial payment is only part of the whole. So, what word describes a judge who favours one side?... Partial.
partial.example: A historian who is partial to one dynasty may quietly ignore records that show its rulers in a poor light.

gre.s: Because the judge's brother was a shareholder in the company, critics argued that she would inevitably be ____ in its favor and should withdraw from the case.
gre.clue: the judge's brother was a shareholder

passive.hook: PASSIVE: lets everything PASS by without acting.
passive.story: Passive. Letting things happen without acting or resisting. For a month, Luke watched GRE vocabulary videos every night, nodding along, never once testing himself. When he took a practice quiz, he could barely recall ten words. His tutor explained that passive watching feels like learning but leaves little behind. So Luke began writing sentences and quizzing himself aloud, and the words finally stuck. Picture a passive person standing still while life passes by, never reaching out to act. So, what word describes someone who just lets things happen without taking action?... Passive.
passive.example: A passive investor simply buys a fund that tracks the whole market and then leaves it alone for decades.

gre.s: Far from being ____ spectators of the reforms, the village women organized committees, petitioned officials, and ultimately shaped how the new laws were enforced.
gre.clue: the village women organized committees, petitioned officials

patent.hook: GRE trick: PATENT (adj.) means obvious — a patent lie is obvious to everyone.
patent.story: Patent. Obvious and clearly visible. Little Noah swore he had not touched the sweets in the fridge. He said it with great seriousness, while syrup dripped from his chin and his fingers stuck together. His grandmother wiped his face and asked him again. It was a patent lie, plain to everyone in the room. Patent comes from the Latin for lying open, and that is also why an inventor's patent is an open public record. So, what word describes a lie so obvious that everyone can see through it?... Patent.
patent.example: The company's claim that its biscuits were sugar-free was a patent lie, since sugar appeared second on the ingredients list.

gre.s: The witness's claim was ____ false, contradicted by video footage that showed him miles away at the time.
gre.clue: contradicted by video footage

provincial.hook: PROVINCIAL: from a small PROVINCE, never seen the world.
provincial.story: Provincial. Narrow-minded and unsophisticated. Henry's uncle lives in the richest part of the city and believes nothing good exists outside it. Village food is dirty, he says, and regional accents are only for jokes. Then he spent a week in Henry's mother's village far to the north. A farmer's daughter there quoted poets he had never read, and her mother cooked the best meal of his life. His views had been provincial, even though he lived in the capital. A province is a region far from the centre, and provincial thinking stays stuck in one small corner. So, what word describes narrow-minded, unworldly views?... Provincial.
provincial.example: Living abroad cured Sabrina of her provincial belief that no cuisine in the world could match her mother's cooking.

gre.s: Critics dismissed the novelist's early work as ____, concerned only with the petty gossip of her small hometown.
gre.clue: concerned only with the petty gossip of her small hometown

rational.story: Rational. Guided by clear thinking rather than emotion. While Amy's mother was frying fish, the pan of oil suddenly caught fire. Amy's brother grabbed a jug of water, but their mother stopped him. Water would make burning oil explode. Instead, she calmly turned off the gas and slid a metal lid over the pan. The flames died at once. Her rational mind had saved the kitchen. Rational shares its Latin root with ratio and reason: a rational person reasons before acting. So, what word describes someone guided by clear thinking instead of panic?... Rational.
rational.example: Faced with a sudden fire alarm, the rational response is to leave calmly by the stairs, not to rush for the lift.

gre.s: Although investors like to think of themselves as ____, studies show that their decisions are frequently driven by fear and herd behavior.
gre.clue: frequently driven by fear and herd behavior

resolve.hook: RESOLVE: a RESOLUTION you stick to.
resolve.story: Resolve. Firm determination; as a verb, to decide firmly. As a child, Kate nearly drowned in a pond and never went near water again. At twenty-five, watching her niece splash in the river, she resolved to learn. Every dawn for two months she went to the village pond with a teacher. She swallowed water, shivered, and came back the next day. Her resolve never broke. Then one morning, she swam across. Think of a resolution you make for the new year; resolve is the strength to keep it. So, what word means firm determination to do something?... Resolve.
resolve.example: Rumana's resolve never wavered during the long rehabilitation, and she was back on the hockey field within a year of her injury.

gre.s: Repeated setbacks only strengthened the climbers' ____: after each failed attempt on the summit, they returned the following season eager to try again.
gre.clue: eager to try again

sophisticated.hook: SOPHISTICATED: from SOPHIA, wisdom; refined and advanced.
sophisticated.story: Sophisticated. Highly developed and complex; also, refined and worldly. Adam's grandmother pointed to a palm tree near their pond, where weaver birds hung their nests. Each one was woven from strips of grass into a hanging bottle with a long tunnel for a door, which keeps snakes out. Adam stared, amazed that a small bird could build something so sophisticated. Sophisticated comes from the Greek sophia, wisdom, which also appears in philosophy. Think of a sophisticated design as one packed with the wisdom of long experience. So, what word describes something highly developed and complex?... Sophisticated.
sophisticated.example: Ancient Egyptian farmers developed a sophisticated network of canals and basins to spread the Nile's floodwater across their fields.

gre.s: The fraud was so ____, involving dozens of shell companies across several countries, that investigators needed years to untangle it.
gre.clue: involving dozens of shell companies across several countries

subtle.hook: SUBTLE: silent 'b', just as subtle as the word itself.
subtle.story: Subtle. So delicate or slight that it is hard to notice. Mia's uncle is a tea taster in the hills. He slurps a spoonful from a small cup, rolls it on his tongue, and says which hillside it came from and whether it was picked after rain. To Mia, every cup tastes the same. But he notices subtle differences in smell and colour that she cannot sense at all. Subtle hides a silent b, a letter so subtle that most people never notice it. So, what word describes a difference so delicate that only an expert can detect it?... Subtle.
subtle.example: A skilled tea taster can detect subtle differences between leaves picked in the same Sylhet garden only a week apart.

gre.s: The difference between the two dialects is ____, detectable only to native speakers who have lived in both regions.
gre.clue: detectable only to native speakers

utterly.hook: UTTERLY: so complete you can't UTTER anything more.
utterly.story: Utterly. Completely and absolutely. Peter took the overnight ferry from the city to reach home for the holiday. The deck was packed, the engine roared all night, and he slept sitting on his bag. When he finally reached his mother's gate at dawn, he was utterly exhausted. Then she came running out, and he forgot every bit of it. Utter comes from an old English word for outer, so utterly means all the way to the outermost edge. So, what word means completely, to the very limit?... Utterly.
utterly.example: The old map proved utterly useless, since the river had shifted its course nearly a mile since it was drawn.

gre.s: The expedition's plan, which had seemed flawless on paper, proved ____ unworkable: not a single stage could be carried out once the team reached the frozen pass.
gre.clue: not a single stage could be carried out

yield.hook: YIELD has two meanings: PRODUCE (a crop yields rice) and GIVE WAY (a yield sign).
yield.story: Yield. To produce or provide; also, to give way under pressure. For forty years, George farmed his land near the coast the old way. When salt water crept into his fields, his daughter brought home new salt-tolerant rice seeds. He refused at first. After weeks of her patient arguing, he finally yielded. That winter his fields yielded almost twice as much rice, and he admitted she was right. The trick: a field yields a crop, and a yield sign on the road tells you to give way. So, what verb means both to produce and to give way?... Yield.
yield.example: The survey of three thousand households yielded surprising data on how much families spend on mobile phone credit.

gre.s: Researchers hoped the new irrigation method would ____ larger harvests, but in its first season the farms brought in less rice than ever.
gre.clue: but in its first season the farms brought in less rice than ever

accord.story: Accord. Agreement or harmony; also, a formal treaty, or to grant something. For years, two neighbouring families quarrelled over a mango tree growing right on the wall between their homes. Every summer brought shouting about whose mangoes were whose. At last the elders sat down together and reached an accord: each family keeps the fruit on its own side, and the first basket of the season is shared. Now the families live in accord. Accord holds the Latin cor, heart: hearts brought together. So, what word means a peaceful agreement between two sides?... Accord.
accord.example: Under the new accord, the two universities will let their students take courses at either campus without paying extra fees.

gre.s: After decades of hostility, the two neighboring states finally reached a historic ____ on sharing the river's waters, though skeptics doubted it would survive the next drought.
gre.clue: though skeptics doubted it would survive the next drought

adverse.hook: ADVERSE: like an ADVERSARY, working against you.
adverse.story: Adverse. Harmful or unfavourable. Kyle had saved for months to visit a coral island with his friends. The night before, the coast guard announced adverse weather: high winds and rough seas, with all ships cancelled. Standing at the jetty, watching grey waves crash, Kyle let go of the trip. Adverse conditions had won, but everyone was safe. Adverse shares its root with adversary: adverse weather is your opponent. Do not confuse it with averse, which means unwilling. So, what word describes conditions that work against you?... Adverse.
adverse.example: Doctors warned that staying up past midnight before every exam can have adverse effects on both memory and mood.

gre.s: The drug trial was halted early because several participants suffered ____ reactions, including severe rashes and dangerously high fevers.
gre.clue: including severe rashes and dangerously high fevers

arbitrary.hook: ARBITRARY: like an ARBITER who decides by flipping a coin.
arbitrary.story: Arbitrary. Based on random choice or personal whim, not reason. Jenna's landlord in the city made new rules whenever he felt like it. One month he banned guests after nine. The next, he banned drying clothes on the roof. Then he raised the rent twice in one year, with no reason except his mood. Jenna and her flatmates never knew what tomorrow's rule would be. Every decision was arbitrary. The word comes from arbiter, a judge free to decide however he pleased. So, what word describes a rule made by whim rather than reason?... Arbitrary.
arbitrary.example: The border between the two provinces looks arbitrary on the map, a straight line drawn by colonial officials who never visited the region.

gre.s: Employees resented the new promotion policy, which seemed entirely ____, rewarding some workers and passing over others for no discernible reason.
gre.clue: for no discernible reason

attribute.hook: ATTRIBUTE: give TRIBUTE (credit) to the cause.
attribute.story: Attribute. To regard something as caused by a particular thing; as a noun, a quality or feature. At ninety, Ella's grandmother still walks to the market every morning. When neighbours ask her secret, she holds up three fingers. She attributes her long life to a morning walk, a little rice, and never holding a grudge. Ella thinks her real attribute is her cheerfulness. Attribute and tribute share a Latin root meaning to assign or give: when you attribute something, you assign the credit to its cause. So, what verb means to credit an effect to a cause?... Attribute.
attribute.example: Doctors attribute this year's sharp rise in dengue cases to an unusually long and wet monsoon season.

gre.s: Although the coach was quick to ____ the team's victory to his new training regimen, most observers credited the opposing goalkeeper's uncharacteristic blunders.
gre.clue: most observers credited the opposing goalkeeper's uncharacteristic blunders

auxiliary.story: Auxiliary. Serving as extra or backup help. Halfway through Sarah's wedding reception at a community centre, the power went out. The music stopped, the fans fell silent, and three hundred guests sat in the dark. Sarah's father held his breath. Then, with a roar from the back of the building, the auxiliary generator came to life. The lights blazed, and the guests cheered. Think of the aux cable in a car: aux is short for auxiliary, an extra input beside the main one. So, what word describes a backup source of help?... Auxiliary.
auxiliary.example: When the main ferry broke down, the company sent two auxiliary boats so that passengers would not miss the Eid rush home.

gre.s: Although the main pump handles routine cooling, engineers installed ____ pumps that switch on automatically whenever demand exceeds its capacity.
gre.clue: whenever demand exceeds its capacity

competent.story: Competent. Having enough skill or knowledge to do something well. When the ceiling fan in Evan's flat began to spark, his father called a young electrician from the lane. He was not famous, and he arrived on a bicycle. But within twenty minutes he found the burnt wire, replaced it, tested every switch, and charged a fair price. The young man was competent. Competent means fully able, not necessarily brilliant; it shares a Latin root with compete, as if able to hold your own. So, what word describes someone with enough skill to do the job well?... Competent.
competent.example: Nasrin is a competent driver, but she still asks her brother to take the wheel on the busy Dhaka-Chattogram highway.

gre.s: Although not brilliant, the new manager proved thoroughly ____, handling every crisis calmly and efficiently.
gre.clue: handling every crisis calmly and efficiently

credible.hook: CREDIBLE: has CREDIT, so you can believe it.
credible.story: Credible. Believable enough to be trusted. One evening, a message spread through Ashley's family group: a cyclone would hit the city that very night. Her aunt began packing bags in a panic. Ashley calmly checked the official bulletin from the Meteorological Department, which said the storm would stay far out at sea. That source was credible; the forwarded message was not. Her aunt sat down and unpacked. Credible comes from the Latin for believe, like credit and credentials. So, what word describes a source you can trust?... Credible.
credible.example: For a threat of punishment to work, a parent must make it credible, so empty warnings soon lose their effect.

gre.s: The jury found the witness's account ____, since it matched the physical evidence in every detail.
gre.clue: it matched the physical evidence in every detail

curb.hook: CURB: the street CURB keeps cars from going too far.
curb.story: Curb. To restrain something or keep it in check. Paul used to drink six cups of tea a day, each with three spoons of sugar. After his doctor warned him about diabetes, his daughter Molly stuck a chart on the fridge. Each week, one spoon less. Paul grumbled, but slowly he curbed his sweet tooth. By winter, he took his tea with no sugar at all. Think of the curb at the side of a road: it stops cars from going too far, just as you curb a habit. So, what verb means to hold something back?... Curb.
curb.example: The central bank raised interest rates to curb inflation, which had pushed the price of onions to a record high.

gre.s: Hoping to ____ the spread of the disease, health officials closed schools and banned large gatherings for a month, despite protests from businesses.
gre.clue: closed schools and banned large gatherings

deliberate.hook: DELIBERATE: done with LIBERTY of choice, on purpose.
deliberate.story: Deliberate. Done on purpose; as a verb, to think carefully before deciding. In the last over of a tense match, the young bowler Connor walked back slowly to his mark. He was deliberating: a fast ball, or a slow one? The crowd roared. Then he bowled a deliberate slower ball. The batsman swung far too early, and the stumps flew. Deliberate comes from the Latin libra, a pair of scales: to deliberate is to weigh your options carefully. So, what word describes an act done with clear intention?... Deliberate.
deliberate.example: The professor's long pause before answering was deliberate, a way of making the students think harder about their own question.

gre.s: Investigators concluded that the fire was not an accident but a ____ act, pointing to traces of fuel poured near every exit.
gre.clue: pointing to traces of fuel poured near every exit

eclipse.hook: ECLIPSE: like the moon blocking out the sun.
eclipse.story: Eclipse. To overshadow; to surpass and make something seem less important. At every family gathering, Kayla always sang first, and everyone praised her. Then one holiday, her nine-year-old cousin Lily sang an old folk song in a voice so clear that the whole room fell silent. Kayla felt a sting, then a rush of pride. Her little cousin's talent had eclipsed her own. In a solar eclipse, the moon slides in front of the sun and hides its light; when one person eclipses another, they outshine them. So, what verb means to outshine and overshadow?... Eclipse.
eclipse.example: The huge success of her second album soon eclipsed her debut, which few listeners now remember.

gre.s: Although the novelist was celebrated in her lifetime, her reputation came to ____ that of her more famous brother only after both had died.
gre.clue: her more famous brother

exotic.hook: EXOTIC: EXternal, from the outside world.
exotic.story: Exotic. Coming from a distant foreign country; strikingly unusual. The first time Jason saw a dragon fruit in a city supermarket, he stopped and stared. Its skin was hot pink with green flames, and inside the white flesh was dotted with tiny black seeds. It looked truly exotic. Today, farmers across the country grow dragon fruit, and it is sold from carts beside the road. Exotic comes from the Greek exo, meaning outside: something exotic comes from the outside world. So, what word describes something strikingly unusual, from far away?... Exotic.
exotic.example: Pet shops in Katabon sell exotic birds from Africa and South America, though some of them are smuggled into the country illegally.

gre.s: The botanist travelled to remote islands in search of ____ plants that had never been described in any European catalogue.
gre.clue: had never been described in any European catalogue

foil.hook: FOIL: wrap the plan in FOIL so it can't work.
foil.story: Foil. To stop a plan from succeeding; also, a person who contrasts with another. Brooke's friends spent a week planning a surprise party for her birthday. The balloons were up, the cake was hidden, and everyone was crouched behind the sofa. Then her six-year-old nephew ran to the door and shouted, "Come quickly, everyone is hiding!" One sentence foiled the whole plan. Picture a plan wrapped up in foil so it cannot breathe. A foil is also a character whose contrast makes another shine. So, what verb means to stop a plan from working?... Foil.
foil.example: A sudden thunderstorm foiled the climbers' plan to reach the summit before noon, forcing them back to the lower camp.

gre.s: An alert bank clerk managed to ____ the robbery by quietly pressing a silent alarm, and the police arrived before the gang could reach the vault.
gre.clue: by quietly pressing a silent alarm

fringe.hook: FRINGE: the edge of a scarf, far from the center.
fringe.story: Fringe. The outer edge; also, views far outside the mainstream. At a corner diner, Caleb's uncle insists every evening that the moon landing was faked. The other men sip their tea, roll their eyes, and talk about cricket instead. Caleb knows his uncle is a kind man, but his ideas sit on the fringe, believed by very few. Picture the fringe of a scarf, those loose threads hanging at the far edge, far from the centre of the cloth. So, what word describes views far from the mainstream?... Fringe.
fringe.example: The party began as a fringe movement meeting in a single tea shop, yet within a decade it had won seats in parliament.

gre.s: Once dismissed as a ____ theory held by only a handful of eccentrics, the idea has since gained wide acceptance among mainstream scientists.
gre.clue: held by only a handful of eccentrics

inclined.hook: INCLINED: LEANING toward something, like an inclined plane.
inclined.story: Inclined. Having a tendency or willingness to do something. On cold January mornings up north, Zoe is never inclined to leave her heavy quilt. The fog presses on the windows, and the floor feels like ice. But one morning, the smell of steamed rice cakes and date molasses drifted in from the kitchen. Suddenly she felt very inclined to get up, and she ran out in her socks. Think of an inclined road that leans in one direction: an inclined person leans toward doing something. So, what word means leaning toward doing something?... Inclined.
inclined.example: After the long train ride, few of the tourists were inclined to climb the hundred steps up to the old temple.

gre.s: Having been burned by investments before, she was not ____ to trust the salesman's promises of guaranteed returns.
gre.clue: Having been burned by investments before

naive.hook: NAIVE: like a NATIVE newcomer who doesn't know the city's tricks.
naive.story: Naive. Showing a lack of experience or judgment. Hailey saw a new smartphone advertised on a Facebook page for half its usual price. The seller wanted full payment in advance, and he sounded so friendly. She sent the money. A week later, the parcel arrived, and inside was a single bar of soap. Her elder brother did not scold her. He just said she had been naive. Naive and native come from the same Latin root meaning born: a naive person is as unworldly as a newborn. So, what word describes someone too trusting because of inexperience?... Naive.
naive.example: It was naive of the startup founders to assume that investors would fund them without first seeing any sales figures.

gre.s: Only a ____ observer would take the company's promises at face value, since it has broken nearly every pledge it has made in the past decade.
gre.clue: since it has broken nearly every pledge it has made in the past decade

obscure.story: Obscure. Not well known, or hard to understand; as a verb, to hide or make unclear. Browsing the second-hand bookstalls downtown, Eli found a thin poetry book with a cracked spine. Dust and water stains had obscured the poet's name. He had never heard of her, and neither had the seller. But that night the poems made him cry. He promised himself he would find out who this obscure poet was. Obscure comes from the Latin for dark: something obscure stays in the shadows. So, what word describes a writer almost nobody knows?... Obscure.
obscure.example: The prizewinning novel first appeared from an obscure press in Rajshahi that had never sold more than a few hundred copies of any title.

gre.s: Once an ____ figure known only to a few specialists, the painter is now celebrated in major museums around the world.
gre.clue: known only to a few specialists

profound.hook: PROFOUND: as deep as the ocean FOUNDATION.
profound.story: Profound. Very great or intense; also, showing deep insight. When Mason failed his first university exam, he went home to his village, ashamed. His grandfather took him down to the river at sunset. "Look," he said. "The river never runs straight, yet it always reaches the sea." Mason stood silent for a long time. Those simple words had a profound effect on him. Profound shares a Latin root with foundation, from the word for bottom: a profound idea reaches deep down. So, what word describes words of deep insight?... Profound.
profound.example: The simple question of why the night sky is dark turned out to have profound implications for our picture of the universe.

gre.s: Although the lecture was delivered in simple language, its insights were ____, forcing listeners to reconsider assumptions they had held all their lives.
gre.clue: forcing listeners to reconsider assumptions they had held all their lives

render.hook: RENDER: RENDERS it into a new state.
render.story: Render. To cause someone or something to become; also, to give or provide. Julia opened the email in her dorm room and read the first line three times. A full scholarship. She tried to call her mother, but the news had rendered her speechless, and she could only laugh and cry into the phone. Her mother understood anyway. Render comes from a Latin word meaning to give back: a doctor renders help, and news can render you speechless, giving you back in a new state. So, what verb means to cause someone to become something?... Render.
render.example: Local fishermen rendered vital help to the coast guard, guiding rescue boats through channels that did not appear on any chart.

gre.s: Throughout the crisis, volunteers continued to ____ assistance to stranded travelers, offering food, shelter, and free rides to the nearest town.
gre.clue: offering food, shelter, and free rides to the nearest town

retiring.hook: GRE trick: RETIRING means shy — she RETIRES to her room when guests come.
retiring.story: Retiring. Shy and quiet, preferring to stay out of sight. At every family wedding, while cousins danced and aunts gossiped, Claire slipped quietly up to the rooftop with a cup of tea. Relatives called her the quiet one. Then one winter, her paintings of mangrove forests filled a city gallery, and the family learned what she had been doing all those years. Their retiring Claire had a voice after all. A retiring person retires from the crowd, the way a worker retires from the office. So, what word describes someone shy who keeps out of the spotlight?... Retiring.
retiring.example: The retiring mathematician declined every invitation to speak about her famous proof and went on quietly teaching first-year calculus.

gre.s: Though her paintings were bold and flamboyant, the artist herself was ____, avoiding interviews and rarely appearing even at her own exhibitions.
gre.clue: avoiding interviews and rarely appearing even at her own exhibitions

rhetoric.hook: RHETORIC: a RHETORICAL question doesn't need an answer — it's just for effect.
rhetoric.story: Rhetoric. The art of persuasive speaking; also, language that sounds impressive but is insincere. Before a local election, a candidate's microphone boomed through Derek's small town. Smooth new roads, a modern hospital, a job for every young person. Crowds clapped and garlands piled up. Five years later, the main road still flooded every monsoon, and Derek's mother still travelled two hours to see a doctor. It had all been rhetoric. A rhetor was a public speaker in ancient Greece, and a rhetorical question is asked only for effect. So, what word means fine speech without real substance?... Rhetoric.
rhetoric.example: Behind the minister's rhetoric about a digital revolution, most village schools still had no computers and no reliable electricity.

gre.s: Voters had grown weary of the candidate's ____, noting that years of grand speeches had produced not a single new road or school.
gre.clue: years of grand speeches had produced not a single new road or school

robust.hook: ROBUST: like a ROBOT, strong and hard to break.
robust.story: Robust. Strong, sturdy and healthy. Ian's grandfather is seventy-eight, yet every morning he walks to his rice field, carries sacks on his shoulder, and swims in the pond before lunch. When Ian, at twenty, grew tired halfway through the field, the old man took the sack from him. "City boy," he said fondly. Ian was amazed at how robust he still was. Robust comes from the Latin robur, meaning oak: a robust person stands as firm as an oak tree. So, what word describes someone strong, sturdy and full of health?... Robust.
robust.example: Bamboo scaffolding is surprisingly robust, and Dhaka builders still use it to put up apartment towers many storeys high.

gre.s: Far from being fragile, the economy proved surprisingly ____, recovering within months from a shock that analysts had expected to last years.
gre.clue: Far from being fragile

skirt.hook: GRE trick: to SKIRT means to go around the edge, like a skirt's hem.
skirt.story: Skirt. To go around the edge of something; also, to avoid dealing with an issue. At a family dinner, Madison's aunt leaned over and asked, for the fifth time that year, when she planned to marry. Madison smiled and said, "Auntie, your mango pickle is amazing. How do you make it?" Her aunt began explaining at once. Madison had skirted the question again. A skirt runs around the edge, and when you skirt an issue, you go around it without ever going through it. So, what verb means to dodge a topic?... Skirt.
skirt.example: The new history textbook skirts the controversy over the war's causes, offering a list of dates instead of an explanation.

gre.s: Rather than addressing the scandal directly, the spokesperson tried to ____ the issue by talking at length about the company's charitable work.
gre.clue: Rather than addressing the scandal directly

sober.hook: GRE trick: SOBER means serious and realistic, not just alcohol-free.
sober.story: Sober. Serious, sensible and realistic; also, not drunk. Ethan and his friends were thrilled about their idea for a food delivery business. They talked of millions of customers and new branches in every city. Then his elder sister, an accountant, read their plan. She did not mock them.
