entrenched.hook: EN-TRENCHED: dug deep into a TRENCH, impossible to move.
entrenched.story: Entrenched. So firmly fixed that it is very hard to remove. Dowry has been illegal in the country for decades. Yet in some villages, families still quietly hand over cash, furniture and motorbikes at weddings. When a young teacher named Rachel refused to let her brother's future in-laws pay one, her own relatives were shocked. The custom is deeply entrenched. Picture soldiers dug into a trench: an entrenched habit is dug in so deep that it will not move. So, what word describes a custom so firmly fixed that it is hard to remove?... Entrenched.
entrenched.example: The rivalry between the two neighbouring football clubs is so entrenched that grandfathers still argue about a match played in 1975.

gre.s: Reformers found it difficult to challenge the ____ bureaucracy, whose habits and privileges had been established over generations.
gre.clue: established over generations

erratic.hook: ERRATIC: full of ERRORS, all over the place.
erratic.story: Erratic. Not regular or predictable. One hot summer in Rick's village, the electricity followed no pattern at all. Some evenings it stayed on for hours; other days it vanished at noon, came back for ten minutes, then vanished again. Rick kept a charged lamp beside his books, never knowing when the fan would stop. The supply was erratic. Erratic comes from the Latin for wandering, the same root as error: erratic things wander off course. So, what word describes something irregular and impossible to predict?... Erratic.
erratic.example: The old office printer was maddeningly erratic, working perfectly for an hour and then jamming on every second page.

gre.s: The athlete's performances have been so ____ this season, brilliant one week and dismal the next, that even her coaches cannot predict how she will do.
gre.clue: brilliant one week and dismal the next

exhaustive.hook: EXHAUSTIVE: covers so much it EXHAUSTS the topic.
exhaustive.story: Exhaustive. Thorough and complete, covering every part. Before buying a second-hand car, Russell's father spent an entire Friday inspecting it. He checked the engine, the brakes, every tyre, the papers, and the rust under the doors, then drove it on a highway, a muddy lane and a crowded market road. Russell counted twelve pages of notes. When his father finished, there was nothing left to check. His inspection was exhaustive. An exhaustive search exhausts every possibility. So, what word describes a check so thorough it covers every single part?... Exhaustive.
exhaustive.example: Before writing her thesis on Bengali folk songs, Tahmina compiled an exhaustive list of every recording held in the national archive.

gre.s: The committee's ____ report, which examined every expenditure over a ten-year period, left no question about where the funds had gone.
gre.clue: examined every expenditure over a ten-year period

foreseeable.hook: FORE-SEE-able: can be SEEN BEFORE it happens.
foreseeable.story: Foreseeable. Possible to see coming or to predict. A developer built a row of houses right on the bank of the great river, with no embankment and no drainage. Engineers warned him; old fishermen warned him. In the very first monsoon, the river swallowed three houses. Nobody was hurt, but the owners lost everything. Everyone said the damage was foreseeable. The word is built simply: fore, meaning before, plus see, plus able. Something foreseeable is able to be seen before it happens. So, what word describes trouble that could easily have been predicted?... Foreseeable.
foreseeable.example: Given how little the twins had studied, their poor marks in the board exams were perfectly foreseeable.

gre.s: The collapse was entirely ____, since engineers had warned for years that the dam could not withstand a major flood.
gre.clue: engineers had warned for years

fruitful.hook: FRUITFUL: a tree full of FRUIT.
fruitful.story: Fruitful. Producing good or helpful results. Sadie dreaded the monthly meeting of her village women's savings group, which usually ended in arguments. This time, they agreed to buy two sewing machines, chose who would train first, and set a date to sell their clothes at the Friday market. Walking home, Sadie hummed all the way. The meeting had been fruitful. Picture a mango tree heavy with fruit: a fruitful effort produces plenty, while a fruitless one produces nothing. So, what word describes a meeting that produces good results?... Fruitful.
fruitful.example: The partnership between the two chemists proved fruitful, producing a dozen papers and two patents within three years.

gre.s: After decades of ____ research that yielded dozens of important discoveries, the laboratory was closed for lack of funding.
gre.clue: that yielded dozens of important discoveries

incidental.story: Incidental. Of minor importance; happening alongside something bigger. Nina's office sent her to another city for a three-day training. The training was the main purpose. Along the way she spent a little on rickshaw fares, tea and a phone card. Her manager told her to list these incidental expenses on one line at the end of her report. Next to the training, they were incidental, small costs riding along with the main trip. Think of a small incident at the side of the main road. So, what word describes a minor thing that comes along with the main one?... Incidental.
incidental.example: For the mountaineers, the stunning photographs were incidental, since their real goal was to measure how fast the glacier was shrinking.

gre.s: The lawyer argued that the photograph was merely ____ to the case, a minor detail that had no bearing on the central question of who signed the contract.
gre.clue: a minor detail that had no bearing on the central question

indispensable.hook: IN-DISPENSABLE: can NOT be dispensed with.
indispensable.story: Indispensable. So necessary that you cannot manage without it. In Mitchell's big family, Grandma is the one who knows everything: where the spare keys hang, which medicine each person takes, how much salt the dal needs, and whose birthday is next week. When she went to visit her sister for ten days, the house fell into chaos. Nobody could find anything. Everyone agreed she was indispensable. In means not, so indispensable means not able to be dispensed with, impossible to do without. So, what word describes someone a household simply cannot manage without?... Indispensable.
indispensable.example: On long treks through the Bandarban hills, sturdy boots and plenty of drinking water are indispensable.

gre.s: Once considered a luxury, reliable internet access has become ____ for students, who now need it to submit almost every assignment.
gre.clue: who now need it to submit almost every assignment

inhibit.hook: INHIBIT: keeps you IN, holding you back.
inhibit.story: Inhibit. To hold back, restrain or prevent. Timmy knew every answer in English class, but the fear of mistakes inhibited him from speaking. Every time he tried, his throat went tight. His teacher, Miss Nash, started a small conversation club after school where nobody was ever marked wrong. Week by week, his voice grew steady, and one day he cracked a joke in English. Fear had inhibited him; kindness set him free. Inhibit comes from the Latin for hold in, as if your words are held inside. So, what verb means to hold someone back from acting freely?... Inhibit.
inhibit.example: Cold temperatures inhibit the growth of bacteria, which is why leftover rice should go into the fridge quickly.

gre.s: Researchers hope the new compound will ____ the growth of tumors without damaging healthy tissue.
gre.clue: without damaging healthy tissue

negligent.hook: NEGLIGENT: someone who NEGLECTS their duty.
negligent.story: Negligent. Failing to give the care that duty requires. For months, the tenants of an old city building begged their landlord to fix a broken stair railing. He promised, collected the rent, and did nothing. Then one rainy evening, an elderly tenant slipped and broke her wrist. Her son, Keith, took photos of the railing to the local councillor, and the landlord was made to pay. Everyone agreed he had been negligent. A negligent person neglects their duty; the two words share a root. So, what word describes someone who fails to take proper care?... Negligent.
negligent.example: The hospital was found negligent after a nurse gave a patient the wrong medicine despite clear labels on every bottle.

gre.s: The court ruled that the landlord had been ____, since he had ignored repeated warnings about the building's faulty wiring.
gre.clue: ignored repeated warnings

oblivious.story: Oblivious. Completely unaware of something, often what is close by. Felix was so absorbed in his vocabulary app at the central station that he did not hear the announcement, did not notice the crowd boarding, and did not see his train to the coast slide away. When he finally looked up, the platform was empty. He had learned forty words and missed his train. He had been completely oblivious. Oblivious is related to oblivion, the state of forgetting: an oblivious person has forgotten the world around them. So, what word describes someone totally unaware of what is happening nearby?... Oblivious.
oblivious.example: Lost in a chess problem, Professor Haque was oblivious to the rain blowing through the open window onto his notes.

gre.s: Engrossed in her phone, the pedestrian remained completely ____ to the truck bearing down on her until a stranger grabbed her arm and pulled her back.
gre.clue: until a stranger grabbed her arm and pulled her back

overt.hook: OVERT: right OVER the surface, out in the open.
overt.story: Overt. Done openly, where anyone can see it. When Laura's grandfather was young, men in his village rarely showed affection in public. But the day his granddaughter won a national science prize, he walked onto the school stage and hugged her in front of everyone, tears on his cheeks. His pride was overt, there for the whole school to see. Overt is the opposite of covert, which means hidden. Overt comes from the French word for open, so picture an open door. So, what word describes something done openly, not secretly?... Overt.
overt.example: The referee somehow ignored an overt shove in the penalty area, and the whole stadium erupted in boos.

gre.s: Though the two nations avoided ____ hostilities, never firing a shot, they waged a fierce secret war through spies and proxies.
gre.clue: they waged a fierce secret war through spies and proxies

penetrating.hook: PENETRATING: goes straight through to the truth.
penetrating.story: Penetrating. Showing deep, sharp insight; piercing. In his scholarship interview, Isaiah gave a polished answer about his strengths, rehearsed many times. The interviewer, an old engineer, looked at him for a long moment and asked one quiet question: "And what did you learn from the project that failed?" It cut straight through the script. Isaiah put down his notes and answered honestly. It was a penetrating question. To penetrate is to pierce through; a penetrating question pierces right to the truth. So, what word describes a question that cuts to the heart of a matter?... Penetrating.
penetrating.example: Her penetrating questions during the seminar forced the visiting economist to admit the weak points in his model.

gre.s: Unlike most reviews, which merely summarized the plot, her ____ critique exposed the novel's hidden assumptions about class, insights that even the author later acknowledged.
gre.clue: Unlike most reviews, which merely summarized the plot

perseverance.story: Perseverance. Steady effort that keeps going in spite of setbacks. Harry, a farmer's son, failed the civil service exam on his first try. He studied for another year and failed again, by only a few marks. His friends took other jobs. Harry bought new notebooks and sat for it a third time. When the results came, his mother read his name twice before she believed it. He had succeeded through perseverance. Listen for severe inside it: perseverance means pushing on through severe times. So, what word names steady effort despite repeated setbacks?... Perseverance.
perseverance.example: Learning the sitar demands years of perseverance, since even simple melodies can take months to sound right.

gre.s: The team's eventual success owed less to brilliance than to sheer ____: they repeated the failed experiment hundreds of times before obtaining a usable result.
gre.clue: they repeated the failed experiment hundreds of times

phony.hook: PHONY: like a fake PHONE call from a 'bank'.
phony.story: Phony. Fake, not genuine; also, a person who pretends. At the big bus terminal, a man in a crisp white coat sold bottles of oil he promised would cure diabetes, baldness and back pain. Framed certificates hung behind him. Shaun, a pharmacy student, looked closely and his heart sank: the seal was printed crooked, and the university did not exist. The certificates were phony, and so was the man. Phony sounds like phone, so picture a phony phone call from a fake bank asking for your password. So, what word describes something fake pretending to be real?... Phony.
phony.example: The phony job agency in Motijheel collected registration fees from hundreds of graduates and then vanished overnight.

gre.s: Investigators discovered that the charity was ____: the orphanage featured in its glossy brochures did not exist, and the donations had gone straight into the founder's bank account.
gre.clue: the orphanage featured in its glossy brochures did not exist

pious.story: Pious. Deeply religious; sometimes, showily religious. Every dawn, old Ruth rises for prayer, and every holy season she quietly sends rice to the families on her lane without telling anyone. Her neighbours consider her truly pious. But the word has a sharper second sense. When a businessman donates to a church only in front of cameras, people may call it a pious show, goodness worn for display. Pious shares a root with piety, which means devotion. So, what word describes a person deeply devoted to their faith?... Pious.
pious.example: Her pious uncle spent the holy month in prayer and quiet study, refusing every invitation to travel or celebrate.

gre.s: Voters grew weary of the senator's ____ sermons about honesty, especially once it emerged that he had lied repeatedly about his own finances.
gre.clue: once it emerged that he had lied repeatedly about his own finances

pristine.hook: PRISTINE: PRIS-TEEN, as fresh and new as a teen.
pristine.story: Pristine. In its original, perfect condition; completely clean. When Rhea first visited a coral island as a little girl, the beach was pristine: white sand, clear blue water, and not a single plastic bottle in sight. She ran into the waves shouting with joy. Twenty years later she returned with her own daughter and found wrappers drifting in the shallows. She spent the morning picking them up. Pristine comes from the Latin for former or original: pristine means just as it was at first. So, what word describes a place untouched and perfectly clean?... Pristine.
pristine.example: The museum's copy of the first edition is still pristine, its pages crisp and white after more than two centuries.

gre.s: Conservationists are fighting to protect one of the last ____ forests on the continent, a wilderness never touched by logging or roads.
gre.clue: never touched by logging or roads

prowess.story: Prowess. Outstanding skill, especially in a particular activity. For two seasons, quiet Jared sat on the bench of his village football team. Then, in the final against the neighbouring union, he came on as a substitute, dribbled past four defenders, and curled the ball into the top corner. The crowd fell silent, then roared, and carried him home on their shoulders. Everyone talked about his prowess. Prowess sounds like pro: it is the skill of a professional, whether in sport, study or craft. So, what word means outstanding skill at something?... Prowess.
prowess.example: The mechanic's prowess with old engines kept the village rice mill running long after spare parts had disappeared from the market.

gre.s: Despite her undoubted ____ as a chess player, she lost the championship because she could not cope with the pressure of the final game.
gre.clue: Despite her undoubted

relish.hook: RELISH: like a delicious RELISH sauce you savor.
relish.story: Relish. To enjoy greatly; great enjoyment. After a year of bread and pasta in Germany, Seth came home. His mother set down a plate of fish in mustard sauce, still steaming. Seth closed his eyes at the first bite and ate slowly, savouring every mouthful. He relished it, and his mother watched with a quiet relish of her own. Relish is also a tangy sauce, like a chutney, that makes food taste better: to relish something is to taste it with joy. So, what verb means to enjoy something greatly?... Relish.
relish.example: The retired judge relished long afternoons in the university library, reading the history books he never had time for while working.

gre.s: Far from dreading the debate, the candidate seemed to ____ the chance to confront her opponent in front of a national audience.
gre.clue: Far from dreading the debate

slander.hook: SLANDER is SPOKEN; LIBEL is written.
slander.story: Slander. False spoken statements that damage someone's reputation. After losing a club election, Rodney told everyone in the canteen that the winner, Felicia, had bought votes. None of it was true, but people began to whisper when she passed. Felicia felt her face burn in every class. Finally, the club's adviser checked the ballots, cleared her name, and made Rodney apologise in front of everyone. His words had been slander. Remember: slander is spoken, while libel is written; both are false and damaging. So, what word names false spoken words that ruin a reputation?... Slander.
slander.example: Accusing a colleague of theft in front of the whole department, with no evidence at all, could expose you to a charge of slander.

gre.s: Unable to defeat his opponent on the issues, the candidate chose to ____ her instead, spreading false rumors that she had embezzled campaign funds.
gre.clue: spreading false rumors that she had embezzled campaign funds

vigilant.hook: VIGILANT: keeping a VIGIL all night, watching.
vigilant.story: Vigilant. Keeping careful watch for possible danger. During the monsoon, when the river near their village rises, Jenna's father barely sleeps. Every few hours he walks to the embankment with a torch, checking the water against a mark on a bamboo pole, ready to wake the neighbours. One night the water climbed fast, and his warning gave everyone time to move the cattle. He was vigilant. A vigil is a night spent awake and watching; a vigilant person keeps that same watch. So, what word describes someone carefully watching for danger?... Vigilant.
vigilant.example: Parents in flood-prone villages stay vigilant throughout the monsoon, keeping small children well away from the swollen river.

gre.s: Security guards were told to remain ____ throughout the night, since thieves had already struck the warehouse twice in the small hours.
gre.clue: since thieves had already struck the warehouse twice

abound.hook: A-BOUND-less supply: so much that there's no boundary.
abound.story: Abound. To exist in very large numbers. Every June, Sheila's grandmother phones with the same instruction: "Bring empty bags." In the orchards around her house, mangoes abound. Branches bend almost to the ground, every basket on the veranda overflows, and neighbours leave mangoes at each other's doors. Sheila fills her bags and still cannot carry them all. Abound shares a root with abundant, from the Latin for overflowing, like a wave spilling over. When things abound, there is more than anyone needs. So, what verb means to exist in huge numbers?... Abound.
abound.example: Hidden jokes abound in the cartoonist's drawings, so careful readers find something new on every page.

gre.s: Far from being scarce, allusions to the ancient epic ____ in the poet's later work, surfacing in nearly every stanza.
gre.clue: Far from being scarce

apathy.story: Apathy. A state of not caring or feeling any interest. Marty spent a month organising his university's blood donation camp. He printed posters, booked doctors, and borrowed tables from the canteen. On the day, only nine students came, while hundreds walked past scrolling their phones. Marty packed up quietly. It was not anger that hurt him; it was apathy. The Greek a means without, and pathos means feeling: apathy is life without feeling. Its opposite is passion, or simply care. So, what word names a complete lack of interest or concern?... Apathy.
apathy.example: Years of broken promises had bred deep apathy among residents, who no longer bothered to report potholes to the city corporation.

gre.s: Organizers were dismayed by the public's ____; despite months of campaigning, only a handful of people attended the rally.
gre.clue: only a handful of people attended the rally

ardent.story: Ardent. Very enthusiastic or passionate. Every Friday morning, Rita's grandfather walks two kilometres to watch the village boys play cricket. He has not missed a match in thirty years. He knows every boy's batting style and shouts advice from the boundary until his voice is hoarse. When the youngest batsman hit his first six, the old man threw his cap into the air. He is the club's most ardent fan. Ardent comes from the Latin for burning, the same root as ardour: an ardent fan burns with enthusiasm. So, what word describes someone burning with passion?... Ardent.
ardent.example: An ardent reader of detective stories, Nusrat had finished every Feluda book before she turned twelve.

gre.s: Even her most ____ admirers, who had defended every one of her earlier films against hostile reviewers, conceded that her latest effort was a disappointment.
gre.clue: who had defended every one of her earlier films

aversion.hook: AVERSION: you AVERT (turn away) your eyes from it.
aversion.story: Aversion. A strong dislike. Aaron loves almost every dish except bitter gourd. Since childhood, the sight of bitter gourd on his plate has made him turn his face away. His mother tried frying it crisp, mixing it with potatoes, even hiding it in the dal. Somehow Aaron found it every time. Now he is thirty, and his aversion has not changed at all. Aversion comes from avert, to turn away: when you have an aversion to something, you turn away from it. So, what word names a strong dislike that makes you turn away?... Aversion.
aversion.example: Despite his aversion to early mornings, the new intern reached the lab by six every day to feed the mice.

gre.s: The novelist's lifelong ____ to publicity explains why, despite her enormous commercial success, she has given almost no interviews.
gre.clue: she has given almost no interviews

coercion.story: Coercion. Making people obey by threatening or pressuring them. A garment worker named Tracy was told by her supervisor that unless she signed a paper giving up her overtime pay, she would lose her job. With rent due and a child at home, she signed. Later, a labour court ruled the signature worthless, because it had been obtained through coercion. Think of coercion as force with a threat instead of a fist: to coerce someone is to force them to act against their will. So, what word names getting someone to obey through threats?... Coercion.
coercion.example: Election observers reported widespread coercion, with villagers warned that they would lose their land if they voted the wrong way.

gre.s: The court threw out the confession, ruling that it had been obtained not through voluntary cooperation but through ____, since the suspect had been threatened with violence.
gre.clue: the suspect had been threatened with violence

diffuse.hook: DIFFUSE: like perfume DIFFUSING through a room — spread thin.
diffuse.story: Diffuse. Spread out over a wide area; also, wordy and unfocused. Scott's first essay tried to cover climate change, cricket, his grandfather and artificial intelligence, all in five hundred words. It wandered everywhere and landed nowhere. His teacher returned it with one comment: "Too diffuse. Choose one idea." Scott started again. As a verb, diffuse means to spread out, like a drop of ink slowly spreading through water. Do not confuse it with defuse, which means to calm a tense situation. So, what word describes writing so spread out that it has no clear focus?... Diffuse.
diffuse.example: The light from the paper lantern was soft and diffuse, filling the room without casting a single sharp shadow.

gre.s: Critics complained that the documentary was too ____, touching on dozens of topics without exploring any of them in depth.
gre.clue: touching on dozens of topics without exploring any of them in depth

discrepancy.story: Discrepancy. A difference between things that should match. At the end of the month, Brittany checked the debating club's accounts. Her ledger said the club had four thousand two hundred dollars, but the bank held only three thousand eight hundred. Her stomach dropped. She went over every page with the treasurer until midnight and finally found it: a donation written in the book but never actually deposited. The discrepancy was explained, and Brittany could breathe again. Discrepancy comes from the Latin for sounding different, like two instruments out of tune. So, what word names a mismatch between numbers that should agree?... Discrepancy.
discrepancy.example: A small discrepancy between the two lab reports, one listing the sample at 37 degrees and the other at 39, delayed the whole study.

gre.s: Investigators grew suspicious when they noticed a ____ between the company's public earnings reports and the figures it had submitted to tax authorities.
gre.clue: grew suspicious when they noticed

disparate.hook: DISPARATE: DIS + PARITY. No parity, no equality; completely different.
disparate.story: Disparate. Completely different from one another; hard to compare. Andy's GRE study group looked unlikely at first: a shy software engineer, a loud young doctor, a quiet painter, a retired army officer, and a teenage cricketer. They shared no age, no job, and no taste in music. Yet every Saturday they met in a small café, argued, and cheered each other's scores for months. Such disparate people became close friends. Do not confuse disparate with desperate; listen instead for apart: disparate things are worlds apart. So, what word describes things fundamentally different from each other?... Disparate.
disparate.example: The museum's new gallery pairs disparate objects, such as a Mughal coin beside a plastic toy, to show how trade shaped daily life.

gre.s: The anthology gathers such ____ voices, from medieval mystics to modern rappers, that readers may wonder what unites them.
gre.clue: from medieval mystics to modern rappers

eradicate.hook: E-RADIC-ATE: pull out by the ROOTS (radix).
eradicate.story: Eradicate. To wipe something out so that none of it remains. In the early nineteen seventies, smallpox still haunted villages across the Ganges delta. Health workers went house by house, vaccinating families and tracing every case. In nineteen seventy-five, a little girl on a river island became the last person in the world known to catch the deadliest natural form of the disease. She recovered, and smallpox was later eradicated worldwide. Eradicate comes from the Latin for root: to eradicate is to pull something out by its roots. So, what verb means to destroy something completely?... Eradicate.
eradicate.example: The school launched a campaign to eradicate bullying, training older students to step in whenever they saw it happen.

gre.s: Public health officials hoped not merely to control the disease but to ____ it entirely, so that no new cases would ever appear again.
gre.clue: so that no new cases would ever appear again

evoke.hook: E-VOKE: call (voke, voice) OUT a memory.
evoke.story: Evoke. To bring a feeling, memory or image to mind. Fiona had lived in Toronto for years. One snowy evening, in a small corner grocery, she smelled fresh samosas frying and heard an old love song on the radio. Suddenly she was nine again, sitting beside her grandmother on a rainy afternoon. She stood still, eyes wet. The smell and the song evoked her childhood. E means out, and voc means voice or call, so to evoke is to call a memory out. So, what verb means to bring a memory or feeling to mind?... Evoke.
evoke.example: The composer used slow, rising strings to evoke the vast emptiness of the desert at night.

gre.s: For many people, the smell of rain on dry earth seems to ____ childhood memories more powerfully than any photograph ever could.
gre.clue: more powerfully than any photograph ever could

extant.story: Extant. Still in existence. Seth's grandfather, an old scholar, collects hand-copied manuscripts of songs and stories. Many such books were lost to floods, insects and fire. One afternoon, he unwrapped a red cloth and showed Seth a cracked little book two centuries old. "Only three copies are still extant," he whispered. Seth held his breath. Extant sounds close to extinct, but it means the opposite: extinct things are gone, while extant things survive. So, what word describes something that still exists today?... Extant.
extant.example: The oldest extant recording of the folk song was made on a fragile wax cylinder, and it crackles badly.

gre.s: Although the playwright is known to have written more than forty comedies, only three are ____ today; the rest perished when the theater's archives burned.
gre.clue: the rest perished

fathom.hook: FATHOM: measuring deep water — and deep ideas.
fathom.story: Fathom. To understand something after much thought. Molly's grandmother could not fathom why anyone would pay eight dollars for a cup of coffee. She turned the receipt over twice, as if the reason might be printed on the back, then asked whether the cup came free. A fathom is also a sailor's measure of depth, about six feet: to fathom something is to reach the bottom of it. We often use it with not, as in I cannot fathom it. So, what verb means to finally understand something puzzling?... Fathom.
fathom.example: Rumi could not fathom how his younger sister had solved the puzzle in two minutes when it had taken him all evening.

gre.s: Even after decades of study, physicists struggle to ____ the strange behavior of particles at the quantum level, which seems to defy every intuition about cause and effect.
gre.clue: which seems to defy every intuition about cause and effect

fret.hook: FRET: FRETTING like fingers on guitar FRETS, never still.
fret.story: Fret. To worry anxiously. The night before her visa interview, Kayla could not sleep. What if they asked about her funding? What if she forgot her bank statement? She checked her folder five times and paced the room until three in the morning. Finally her mother brought her warm milk and said, "Do not fret. You have prepared well." Kayla smiled and lay down. Fret also means to wear away, like water slowly fretting a stone, which is exactly what worry does to you. So, what verb means to worry anxiously, again and again?... Fret.
fret.example: Coach Rahman told his players not to fret over the lost first set, since the match was far from decided.

gre.s: Although her doctors assured her that every test result was normal, she continued to ____ about her health, waking at night convinced that something was wrong.
gre.clue: waking at night convinced that something was wrong

hamper.hook: HAMPER: like carrying a heavy laundry HAMPER while trying to run.
hamper.story: Hamper. To slow down or get in the way of progress. Lenny's online classes were going well until load-shedding returned. Every hour the power cut out, his router died, and he missed ten minutes of the lecture. His notes filled with gaps. The power cuts badly hampered his studies. At last his uncle lent him a small battery backup, and Lenny cheered when the router stayed on. Picture trying to run while carrying a heavy laundry hamper: whatever hampers you slows you down. So, what verb means to hinder progress?... Hamper.
hamper.example: A sprained ankle hampered the striker for most of the season, and he managed only two goals.

gre.s: Language barriers continue to ____ cooperation between the two research teams, slowing what could otherwise be rapid progress.
gre.clue: slowing what could otherwise be rapid progress

impulsive.story: Impulsive. Doing things suddenly, without stopping to think. Randy walked into a shopping mall to buy socks. He walked out with a guitar, a gaming chair and a lamp shaped like a puppy, and no money left for the month. None of it was planned; each purchase simply felt right in the moment. That night he ate plain rice and counted his coins. Randy is impulsive. An impulse is a sudden push, and an impulsive person is pushed by every passing wish. Its opposite is deliberate. So, what word describes someone who acts suddenly without thinking?... Impulsive.
impulsive.example: In an impulsive moment, Sabrina dyed her hair bright green the night before her cousin's wedding.

gre.s: Known for weighing every option for months, the cautious director surprised her board with an uncharacteristically ____ decision, announcing the merger the very afternoon it was proposed.
gre.clue: announcing the merger the very afternoon it was proposed

interchangeable.story: Interchangeable. Able to be used in place of each other equally well. When Danny's phone charger broke the night before a trip, he grabbed his sister's from her desk, and it fit perfectly. Their chargers were interchangeable. In English, too, big and large are usually interchangeable. But careful: on the GRE, many words that look similar are not interchangeable. Complacent and confident, for example, mean very different things. Break the word apart: inter means between, so interchangeable things can be changed between one another. So, what word describes two things that can swap places equally well?... Interchangeable.
interchangeable.example: On a well-run assembly line the parts are fully interchangeable, so any bolt fits any car of the same model.

gre.s: Though the two terms are often treated as ____, scientists use them to describe quite different phenomena.
gre.clue: scientists use them to describe quite different phenomena

lament.hook: LAMENT: 'LAME, meant to be better', sad regret.
lament.story: Lament. To grieve over or deeply regret something, often aloud. Twenty years ago, Shannon's grandfather sold the family home in the village to pay for his children's education. It was the right choice. Yet on quiet evenings he still laments it, speaking softly about the two mango trees, the pond where he learned to swim, and the courtyard where his mother cooked. As a noun, a lament is a song or poem of grief, like the slow songs of river boatmen. So, what verb means to express deep sorrow or regret?... Lament.
lament.example: Long after retiring, the old batsman still laments the easy catch he dropped in a final twenty years ago.

gre.s: Many critics ____ the decline of the independent bookstore, mourning the loss of places where readers once gathered.
gre.clue: mourning the loss of places where readers once gathered

lucid.hook: LUCID: full of LIGHT (lux), crystal clear.
lucid.story: Lucid. Clear and easy to understand; also, thinking clearly. Tommy had failed maths twice. Then a new teacher arrived and explained compound interest using one bank account, three years, and the price of a cup of tea. Every step made sense, and Tommy suddenly saw the whole picture. Her explanation was lucid. Lucid comes from the Latin lux, meaning light: a lucid explanation lets the light shine through. A person can also be lucid, thinking clearly after confusion or fever. So, what word describes an explanation so clear it is easy to follow?... Lucid.
lucid.example: Even after the long surgery, my grandfather was lucid enough to joke with the nurses and ask about the cricket score.

gre.s: Despite the complexity of the subject, her ____ explanation allowed even beginners to grasp the theory.
gre.clue: allowed even beginners to grasp the theory

mercenary.hook: MERCENARY: works only for MERCHANDISE and money.
mercenary.story: Mercenary. Motivated only by money; also, a soldier hired to fight for a foreign army. Patients at one private clinic noticed something odd. Whatever their illness, each was told they needed costly scans, more tests, and often surgery. The owner's new car grew shinier, but his patients did not get better. A young journalist named Jake finally exposed him. People called the doctor mercenary. Mercenary comes from the Latin for wages: historically, mercenaries were soldiers who fought for whoever paid them most. So, what word describes someone who acts only for money?... Mercenary.
mercenary.example: The club's owner was accused of mercenary motives when he sold its best young players to rivals a week after they won the league.

gre.s: Critics charged that the consultant's advice was ____, designed less to help her clients than to maximize her own fees.
gre.clue: designed less to help her clients than to maximize her own fees

mutiny.hook: MUTINY: the crew MUTES the captain and takes over.
mutiny.story: Mutiny. An open rebellion against authority, especially by soldiers or sailors. On a cargo ship in the Bay of Bengal, the crew had gone four months without pay. For weeks the sailors stayed silent. Then one morning, they refused to work, took over the bridge, and kept the captain in his cabin until the owners promised their wages. It was a mutiny. To remember it, picture a mute crew that finally finds its voice: the silent sailors rise in mutiny. So, what word names a rebellion by sailors or soldiers against their commanders?... Mutiny.
mutiny.example: When the coach cancelled their holiday for extra training, the exhausted players came close to staging a mutiny.

gre.s: Exhausted by months of harsh discipline and dwindling rations, the sailors threatened to ____ unless the captain agreed to turn the ship toward home.
gre.clue: unless the captain agreed to turn the ship toward home

poignant.hook: POIGNANT: POINTED, it pierces your heart.
poignant.story: Poignant. Deeply moving in a way that stirs sadness. At the airport, Preston watched an old man hug his son, who was leaving to work in Malaysia for five years. The father pressed a small packet of homemade cookies into his son's hands and said nothing. Neither could speak. Preston felt his throat tighten. It was a poignant moment. Poignant comes from an old French verb meaning to prick, the same root as pungent: a poignant scene pricks the heart. So, what word describes a moment so moving that it makes you sad?... Poignant.
poignant.example: In the war museum, the most poignant exhibits are ordinary belongings, a pair of spectacles or a child's shoe, left behind by the dead.

gre.s: The film's final scene is quietly ____: the elderly widower, alone in the empty house, still sets out two cups of tea each morning out of habit.
gre.clue: alone in the empty house, still sets out two cups of tea each morning out of habit

precarious.hook: PRECARIOUS: like a CAR parked on the edge of a cliff.
precarious.story: Precarious. Dangerously unstable or uncertain. On a city building site, a young worker named Henry stood on a thin bamboo scaffold six floors up, balancing a basket of bricks on his head. He wore rubber sandals and no harness, and below him buses roared past. His mother back in the village prayed for him every night. His position was precarious. The word comes from the Latin for prayer: something precarious is so unsteady that you can only pray it holds. So, what word describes a situation dangerously unstable and uncertain?... Precarious.
precarious.example: Moving from one short contract to the next, many young researchers lead a precarious life with no job security at all.

gre.s: With only a single seat separating the two parties, the governing coalition's majority remained ____, liable to collapse with one defection.
gre.clue: liable to collapse with one defection

predicament.hook: PREDICAMENT: a PREDICTION gone wrong, now you're stuck.
predicament.story: Predicament. A hard or awkward situation that is tough to get out of. Owen reached the bus terminal with five minutes to spare, then realised his wallet was gone. No ticket, no money, a dead phone, and his university admission test in another city the next morning. He stood there, wondering whom he could possibly ask. He was in a real predicament. Remember: a dilemma is a hard choice, while a predicament is a hard situation you are stuck in. So, what word names an awkward situation with no easy way out?... Predicament.
predicament.example: Having promised to attend two weddings on the same evening, Ayesha was in a predicament that no excuse could solve.

gre.s: Stranded abroad after their airline collapsed, and with no money to buy new tickets, the tourists faced a grim ____ that their embassy was slow to resolve.
gre.clue: Stranded abroad after their airline collapsed

proficient.hook: PROFICIENT: as skilled as a PRO.
proficient.story: Proficient. Skilled at something through training and practice. When Nicole joined a software company, she could barely write a program that worked. She practised every night after work, solved hundreds of coding problems, and asked senior colleagues endless questions. Two years later, the newest interns were lining up at her desk for help. She had become truly proficient. Proficient comes from a Latin verb meaning to make progress: you become proficient by progressing step by step. So, what word describes someone skilled through long practice?... Proficient.
proficient.example: Ayan became proficient at repairing mobile phones after spending two summers in his uncle's shop on Elephant Road.

gre.s: Although she had studied Spanish for only a year, she was already so ____ that native speakers often assumed she had grown up in Madrid.
gre.clue: native speakers often assumed she had grown up in Madrid

recourse.hook: RE-COURSE: the COURSE you turn to when all else fails.
recourse.story: Recourse. Something you can turn to for help when in trouble. When Mason's landlord refused to return his security deposit, Mason felt helpless. He could not afford a lawyer. Then a friend told him about a free legal aid clinic run by law students at his university. That clinic became his recourse, and within a month he had his money back. Recourse comes from the Latin for running back: a recourse is what you run back to when trouble comes. Do not confuse it with resource. So, what word means a source of help you can turn to?... Recourse.
recourse.example: With the bank closed for the holiday, Sumon's only recourse was to borrow from a neighbour to pay the hospital bill.

gre.s: Because their insurance policy explicitly excluded flood damage, the farmers found themselves without ____ when the river burst its banks and destroyed their crops.
gre.clue: Because their insurance policy explicitly excluded flood damage

refine.hook: RE-FINE: make it FINE again and again.
refine.story: Refine. To improve something with small changes; also, to remove impurities. Kristen wrote her statement of purpose in one evening and felt proud. Then she spent three weeks refining it: twelve drafts, cutting weak sentences, sharpening examples, and replacing vague words with exact ones. The final version was half as long and twice as strong. Refine means to make fine again and again, the way a sugar mill refines brown sugar until it is pure white. So, what verb means to improve something through careful small changes?... Refine.
refine.example: Over ten years, physicists refined their measurement of the particle's mass, cutting the margin of error in half.

gre.s: Over decades, the craftsmen continued to ____ their techniques, gradually eliminating flaws until their porcelain was the finest in the world.
gre.clue: gradually eliminating flaws

remuneration.hook: RE-MUNER-ATION: MONEY (munus) given back for work.
remuneration.story: Remuneration. What a person is paid for the work they do. Rhonda translated a long novel for a big city publisher. When she asked about payment, the editor offered her a free copy of the book and a thank-you in the preface. Rhonda smiled politely, and explained that her landlord did not accept thanks as rent. She wanted proper remuneration. The root is the Latin munus, meaning gift or service: remuneration is a gift given back for your service. Careful, it is remuneration, not renumeration. So, what word names payment for work?... Remuneration.
remuneration.example: Many interns at Dhaka's advertising agencies work long hours for remuneration that barely covers their bus fare.

gre.s: Many of the volunteers worked for years without ____, motivated not by money but by their deep commitment to the cause.
gre.clue: motivated not by money

serene.story: Serene. Calm, peaceful and untroubled. At dawn, Hope sat alone on the shore of a mountain lake. Mist rested on the green hills, the water lay perfectly still, and the only sound was a distant boatman's oar. After months of city traffic, she felt her shoulders loosen. The morning was serene. Serene comes from the Latin for a clear, cloudless sky: a serene mind has no storm clouds in it. A serene person stays calm even in a crisis. So, what word describes a scene perfectly calm and peaceful?... Serene.
serene.example: Even as reporters shouted questions at her, the newly elected mayor remained serene, answering each one with a slight smile.

gre.s: In contrast to the frantic, crowded market just outside its walls, the monastery garden remained ____, its stillness broken only by birdsong.
gre.clue: its stillness broken only by birdsong

sluggish.hook: SLUGGISH: as slow as a SLUG.
sluggish.story: Sluggish. Slow-moving and lacking energy. After his colleague's wedding lunch of spiced rice, creamy curry and two helpings of rice pudding, Bill went back to his desk. Every email took twice as long, his eyelids drooped, and his thoughts moved like cold honey. He felt completely sluggish. That year the country's economy was sluggish too, with businesses barely growing. Picture a slug crawling across a garden path after rain: sluggish things move like a slug. So, what word describes someone slow and heavy, with no energy?... Sluggish.
sluggish.example: The old laptop had grown so sluggish that opening a single spreadsheet took almost five minutes.

gre.s: Despite heavy government spending, the economy remained ____, growing at barely one percent for the third straight year.
gre.clue: growing at barely one percent for the third straight year

sporadic.hook: SPORADIC: like SPORES floating randomly here and there.
sporadic.story: Sporadic. Happening at irregular intervals; scattered. All through one dry March, Melanie's father watched the sky over his jute fields. Rain came only in sporadic showers: a ten-minute burst on Monday, nothing for nine days, then a drizzle one night. He could not plan his sowing. When the steady rains finally arrived, the whole family ran outside to stand in them. Sporadic comes from a Greek word for scattered, like seeds tossed while sowing; spore shares the root. So, what word describes events that happen only now and then, with no pattern?... Sporadic.
sporadic.example: Apart from sporadic visits from his nephews at Eid, the old fisherman saw almost no one during the long winter.

gre.s: Fighting in the region has been ____ rather than continuous, flaring up unpredictably and then falling silent for weeks.
gre.clue: flaring up unpredictably and then falling silent for weeks

abrasive.story: Abrasive. Rough and harsh in manner; irritating. Ruben's new manager at a downtown bank was brilliant with numbers but abrasive with people. He corrected staff loudly in front of customers, groaned at every question, and never said thank you. Within a month, two clerks had asked for transfers, and Ruben went home each evening feeling scraped raw. Abrasive comes from abrade, to scrape away; sandpaper is an abrasive. An abrasive person rubs everyone the wrong way. So, what word describes a manner so harsh it rubs people raw?... Abrasive.
abrasive.example: The new captain's abrasive style unsettled the squad, and by midseason several senior players had stopped speaking to him.

gre.s: Though his insights were often brilliant, the critic's ____ manner alienated many colleagues, who found his relentless sarcasm exhausting.
gre.clue: who found his relentless sarcasm exhausting

appease.hook: APPEASE: give them 'A PEACE' offering so they stop fighting.
appease.story: Appease. To calm someone's anger, often by giving them what they want. Six-year-old Molly was furious. Her cousins had eaten the last piece of her birthday cake, and she sat on the stairs with her arms crossed, refusing to speak. Her grandmother came out holding a bowl of rice pudding and the promise of a new kite. Slowly, Molly uncrossed her arms. The pudding appeased her. Appease comes from an old French phrase meaning to bring to peace: you appease someone when you restore their peace. So, what verb means to calm someone's anger by giving them what they want?... Appease.
appease.example: To appease fans furious about the cancelled concert, the organisers promised full refunds and a free show the following spring.

gre.s: Hoping to ____ the striking workers, management offered a modest raise, though it refused their central demand for shorter hours.
gre.clue: management offered a modest raise

assertive.hook: ASSERTIVE: firmly ASSERTS what she wants.
assertive.story: Assertive. Confident and firm in stating your views or rights. At her first team meeting, Rachel noticed a senior colleague presenting her idea as his own. Her heart pounded. In the past she would have stayed silent. This time she said, calmly and clearly, "That was my proposal. I'd like to explain the rest of it." The room went quiet, then the director nodded. Rachel had been assertive, not rude. To be assertive is to assert your view, standing firm without shouting. So, what word describes someone who states their rights firmly and confidently?... Assertive.
assertive.example: A short course in negotiation helped Farzana become more assertive when asking clients to settle their overdue invoices.

gre.s: Once timid in meetings, the young analyst became increasingly ____, confidently defending her proposals against senior colleagues.
gre.clue: confidently defending her proposals against senior colleagues

augment.hook: AUGMENT: like AUGMENTED reality adding layers to the world.
augment.story: Augment. To increase the size or amount of something. Kurt earned a modest salary as a small-town schoolteacher. To pay for his daughter's university fees, he began giving evening maths lessons on his veranda, and on weekends he sold honey from his brother's hives. Slowly, these small earnings augmented his income. When his daughter's admission letter came, he read it aloud to the whole lane. Augment comes from the Latin for increase, the same root as auction, where the price keeps rising. So, what verb means to make something bigger?... Augment.
augment.example: The museum augmented its small collection of Mughal miniatures with a generous loan from a private collector.

gre.s: Because her scholarship barely covered tuition, she took a part-time job to ____ her income, adding enough each month to pay the rent.
gre.clue: adding enough each month to pay the rent

caricature.story: Caricature. A picture or description that exaggerates features for comic effect. At the city book fair, Sonya sat on a plastic stool while a young artist sketched her. Two minutes later he turned the paper around: huge eyes, a tiny chin, and glasses as big as bicycle wheels. Sonya covered her mouth. It was a perfect caricature, unmistakably her. Caricature comes from an Italian word meaning to load: a caricature is overloaded with exaggeration. So, what word names a drawing that exaggerates someone's features for fun?... Caricature.
caricature.example: The film reduces the scientist to a caricature, a wild-haired genius who mutters equations and forgets to eat.

gre.s: The novel's portrait of the professor is less a realistic character study than a ____: his vanity is so inflated and his absent-mindedness so extreme that no reader could mistake him for a real person.
gre.clue: no reader could mistake him for a real person

clandestine.hook: CLANDESTINE: a secret CLAN meeting in the DESTINY hour of midnight.
clandestine.story: Clandestine. Done in secret, usually because it is not allowed. In Ricky's university dorm, cooking was strictly forbidden. Yet every Thursday night, after the warden's lights went out, Ricky and three friends met in a back room with a tiny electric cooker and a packet of noodles. They whispered, kept a towel under the door, and froze at every footstep. Those clandestine dinners became the best memory of their first year. Hear clan inside clandestine: picture a small secret clan meeting behind a closed door. So, what word describes something done secretly because it is not allowed?... Clandestine.
clandestine.example: Customs officers uncovered a clandestine workshop in Chattogram where fake medicines were packed into genuine-looking boxes.

gre.s: The two rival companies held ____ talks for months, keeping the negotiations hidden even from their own boards of directors.
gre.clue: keeping the negotiations hidden even from their own boards

complacent.hook: COMPLACENT: so COMfortable in their PLACE that they stop trying.
complacent.story: Complacent. Self-satisfied and unaware of possible dangers. After scoring well on his first GRE practice test, Tim stopped studying. "I already know enough," he told his friends, and spent the next six weeks watching cricket. On test day, the reading passages were harder than anything he had seen. He walked out knowing he had been complacent. Complacent comes from the Latin for very pleased, the same root as please: a complacent person is too pleased with himself to see danger coming. So, what word describes someone so self-satisfied that he stops trying?... Complacent.
complacent.example: Years without a serious flood had made the town's officials complacent, and the drains had not been cleaned in a decade.

gre.s: Having won the championship three years in a row, the team grew ____, skipping practices and underestimating opponents they once feared.
gre.clue: skipping practices and underestimating opponents

conducive.hook: CONDUCIVE: CONDUCTS you toward a result.
conducive.story: Conducive. Making a certain outcome likely; helpful. Lisa's family flat was loud: a television, three cousins, and a pressure cooker whistling every hour. Her grades kept slipping. Then her aunt offered a quiet back room with a window facing a mango tree. With silence, good light and a cup of tea at nine, Lisa studied better than ever. The room was conducive to study. Conducive is related to conduct, to lead: a conducive setting leads you toward a result. Do not confuse it with conclusive. So, what word describes conditions that help something happen?... Conducive.
conducive.example: Warm, humid air is highly conducive to the growth of mould, so archivists keep old manuscripts in cool, dry rooms.

gre.s: Critics argued that the open-plan office, with its constant chatter and interruptions, was hardly ____ to the deep concentration that serious research demands.
gre.clue: with its constant chatter and interruptions

correlate.story: Correlate. To be connected so that when one thing changes, the other tends to change too. For a school project, Scott recorded how many hours his classmates slept and their maths scores. As he plotted the dots, a pattern appeared: students who slept more tended to score higher. The two clearly correlated. His teacher smiled and added a warning: correlation does not prove that one causes the other. Correlate is simply co plus relate: two things related together. So, what verb means that two things rise and fall together?... Correlate.
correlate.example: In the survey, the number of trees on a street correlated closely with how safe residents felt walking there at night.

gre.s: Although rates of the two diseases tend to ____, researchers have found no evidence that one actually causes the other.
gre.clue: researchers have found no evidence that one actually causes the other

crafty.story: Crafty. Clever at getting what you want through tricks or deceit. Every afternoon at the big city market, one fish seller sprinkled water on his tired fish so they gleamed as if fresh from the river. Customers crowded around. Nina's mother leaned close, pressed one gently with her finger, and smelled it. Then she smiled and walked on to the next stall. The seller was crafty, but she was craftier. Craft first meant skill, so a crafty person uses skill to fool others. So, what word describes someone cleverly deceitful?... Crafty.
crafty.example: In the old folktale, a crafty jackal persuades the crocodile gripping his leg that it has only caught a tree root.

gre.s: The ____ negotiator concealed his true objectives behind a show of friendly candor, leading his rivals to concede far more than they had ever intended.
gre.clue: concealed his true objectives behind a show of friendly candor

craven.hook: CRAVEN: the opposite of a brave RAVEN, it flies away at any danger.
craven.story: Craven. Shamefully cowardly. On a crowded city bus, a man began harassing a college student. Brad, a big, strong passenger, saw everything, then looked out of the window and pretended to sleep. It was an elderly woman who stood up and shouted until the man got off. Later, Brad felt ashamed of his craven silence. Craven rhymes with raven: picture a big black raven that flaps away at the first sign of trouble, leaving others to face it. So, what word means contemptibly cowardly?... Craven.
craven.example: The board's craven silence, while the founder bullied junior staff for years, shocked investors when the truth finally came out.

gre.s: Historians have judged the general's retreat as ____, since he abandoned his troops at the first sign of danger.
gre.clue: abandoned his troops at the first sign of danger

debilitating.story: Debilitating. So harmful that it leaves someone weak or unable to function. When chikungunya struck Faith in her final year, the fever lasted only a few days, but the joint pain that followed was debilitating. For a month she could not climb the stairs to her classroom without stopping to rest. Her friends brought notes, and her mother cooked soft rice and lentils every day. Slowly her strength returned. Hear ability inside debilitating: a debilitating illness takes your ability away. So, what word describes something that leaves you too weak to function?... Debilitating.
debilitating.example: A debilitating shortage of trained nurses forced the rural hospital to close two of its four wards.

gre.s: For years she suffered from ____ migraines, which sometimes confined her to a dark room for days at a time.
gre.clue: confined her to a dark room for days at a time

denounce.story: Denounce. To publicly declare something wrong or evil. When a factory upstream began pouring dye into the river near Sean's village, the water turned purple and the fish died. Sean, a young schoolteacher, stood up at a public meeting and denounced the factory in front of journalists and local officials. His voice shook, but he did not stop. Within a month the dumping was investigated. Denounce shares a root with announce: to denounce something is to announce loudly that it is wrong. So, what verb means to condemn something publicly?... Denounce.
denounce.example: The football federation denounced the racist chanting from the stands and fined the home club heavily.

gre.s: Human rights groups were quick to ____ the arrests, calling them a blatant attempt to silence the government's most outspoken critics.
gre.clue: calling them a blatant attempt to silence the government's most outspoken critics

dismantle.hook: DIS-MANTLE: remove the MANTLE (covering) piece by piece.
dismantle.story: Dismantle. To take something apart piece by piece; also, to gradually end a system. After the spring fair ended, Megan watched the workers dismantle the giant bamboo stage. First the cloth banners came down, then the lights, then each pole, untied and stacked on a truck. By evening, the field was empty grass again. Laws and systems can be dismantled the same way, one piece at a time. A mantle is a cloak; to dismantle was first to strip off the cloak, then to take everything apart. So, what verb means to take something apart piece by piece?... Dismantle.
dismantle.example: After the festival, volunteers dismantled the bamboo stage in a single night and stacked the poles neatly for next year.

gre.s: The new administration promised not merely to reform the corrupt licensing system but to ____ it entirely, replacing the old agency with an independent commission.
gre.clue: not merely to reform the corrupt licensing system

eloquent.story: Eloquent. Fluent, persuasive and expressive in speaking or writing. At an inter-university debate, Jules was the last speaker. The hall was noisy and tired. Then he began, softly, with a story about his mother selling vegetables to pay his fees. His words were simple, clear and full of feeling. By the end, the hall was silent, and some judges were wiping their eyes. He had been truly eloquent. Eloquent comes from the Latin loqui, to speak: an eloquent person speaks out beautifully. So, what word describes a speaker who is fluent and moving?... Eloquent.
eloquent.example: Her eloquent letter to the city council, describing the children who played beside an open drain, won funding for a covered sewer.

gre.s: Though the senator was famously awkward in live debates, his written speeches were remarkably ____, moving even his opponents with their clarity and grace.
gre.clue: moving even his opponents with their clarity and grace

estranged.story: Estranged. No longer close or friendly; separated. Rosa and her elder brother had not spoken for eight years after a quarrel over their father's land. They lived in the same city but never visited. Then, at a cousin's wedding, they found themselves at the same table. Her brother pushed a plate of sweets toward her and quietly asked about her children. The estranged siblings talked until midnight. Estranged contains strange: estranged people have become strangers to each other. So, what word describes family members who are no longer close?... Estranged.
estranged.example: The novel follows an estranged father and daughter who are forced to share a car on a long drive across Spain.

gre.s: After decades of silence, the ____ siblings were finally reconciled at their mother's bedside.
gre.clue: After decades of silence

feeble.hook: FEEBLE: sounds weak, like a FEEBLE 'meh'.
feeble.story: Feeble. Lacking strength; also, weak and unconvincing. Hailey's grandfather was once the strongest boatman on the river. Now, at ninety, his grip is feeble, and he needs her arm to cross the courtyard, though his voice is still steady when he tells stories of river storms. That same week, Hailey's little brother offered a feeble excuse for missing school: the goat had eaten his homework. Feeble sounds like a weak little bleat, the cry of a tired lamb. So, what word describes something weak, whether a grip or an excuse?... Feeble.
feeble.example: Rakib's feeble excuse that a goat had eaten his homework only made the teacher laugh.

gre.s: The company's ____ response to the crisis, a single vague press release issued a week late, only deepened customers' anger.
gre.clue: a single vague press release issued a week late

frivolous.hook: FRIVOLOUS: FREE-and-VOLUME-less, no weight, no seriousness.
frivolous.story: Frivolous. Not serious; silly or unimportant. Two weeks before his final exams, Alex spent an entire evening choosing a new ringtone, then another hour arranging his apps by colour. His roommate, buried in past papers, looked up and said, "Your exams are in fourteen days." Alex knew it. His evening had been completely frivolous. In court, too, a frivolous complaint is one too silly to deserve serious time. Frivolous sounds a little like frills: pretty decoration with no real purpose. So, what word describes something silly and not worth serious attention?... Frivolous.
frivolous.example: The committee wasted an hour on frivolous questions about napkin colours while the real budget problem went undiscussed.

gre.s: The judge dismissed the lawsuit as ____, noting that the plaintiff had suffered no harm whatsoever.
gre.clue: had suffered no harm whatsoever

homogeneous.hook: HOMO = same, GENE = kind. Same kind all through.
homogeneous.story: Homogeneous. Made of parts that are all alike; the same throughout. Tammy's grandmother taught her to make bread dough. "Knead until it is the same everywhere," she said. "No dry spots, no lumps." Tammy kneaded until her arms ached, then pressed it: smooth, soft, perfectly homogeneous. A homogeneous group is one where every member is alike. Homo means same and genos means kind, so homogeneous means of the same kind throughout. Its opposite is heterogeneous, mixed. So, what word describes a mixture that is the same all the way through?... Homogeneous.
homogeneous.example: Geologists drilled cores at several points to check whether the rock layer was homogeneous or held pockets of other minerals.

gre.s: Once thought to be culturally ____, the region turns out to have been a patchwork of distinct languages and customs.
gre.clue: turns out to have been a patchwork

insidious.story: Insidious. Causing harm slowly and quietly, so it is hard to notice. For years, the tube well in Robin's village gave clear, cool water. Nobody suspected anything. But it carried arsenic, and slowly, over a decade, dark spots appeared on the hands of the old men who drank from it most. A health worker finally tested the water and painted the well red. The danger had been insidious. Insidious comes from the Latin for ambush: an insidious threat lies quietly in wait. So, what word describes harm that creeps in slowly and unnoticed?... Insidious.
insidious.example: Office gossip can have an insidious effect on a team, slowly eroding trust until colleagues stop sharing ideas.

gre.s: The danger of the pollutant lies in its ____ nature: it accumulates in the body slowly and without symptoms, causing irreversible harm long before it can be detected.
gre.clue: slowly and without symptoms

intertwined.story: Intertwined. Twisted together; closely connected. Every morning, Olive passes an old banyan tree outside her school, where a vine has climbed the trunk and wound around every branch. Nobody can tell anymore where the tree ends and the vine begins. Olive thinks of her two grandmothers, best friends since childhood, whose lives are just as intertwined: same village, same school, and now the same grandchildren. To twine is to twist, and inter means between: intertwined things are twisted around each other. So, what word describes two things closely twisted together?... Intertwined.
intertwined.example: Behind the television, the cables had become so intertwined that tracing a single wire took Kamal half an hour.

gre.s: In the novelist's vision, the fates of the two families are so ____ that no misfortune can befall one without eventually striking the other.
gre.clue: no misfortune can befall one without eventually striking the other

ire.story: Ire. Anger. Sam parked his motorbike across a narrow lane in the old city and ran into a sweet shop for five minutes. When he came back, a rickshaw, two vans and a furious fish seller were waiting. The fish seller's ire was magnificent: red face, waving arms, and a speech the whole lane could hear. Sam apologised and moved the bike at once. Ire is the root of irate, which means very angry; both come from the Latin ira, anger. So, what short word means anger?... Ire.
ire.example: Leaving dirty dishes in the hostel sink is the surest way to earn the ire of Mrs Akter, the strict warden.

gre.s: The new tax on mobile data drew the ____ of students across the country, who staged noisy protests outside the ministry for an entire week.
gre.clue: staged noisy protests outside the ministry

meticulous.hook: METICULOUS: METIC-ulous, every metric measured perfectly.
meticulous.story: Meticulous. Very careful and precise, attentive to every detail. Peter's mother stitches embroidered quilts in a quiet village. Each one takes months. She counts her stitches, unpicks any thread that wanders even slightly, and checks the pattern in daylight before every new row. When a buyer from the city examined one, she could not find a single mistake. Her work is meticulous. The word comes from the Latin for fearful: a meticulous person is almost afraid of the smallest error. So, what word describes work done with great attention to every detail?... Meticulous.
meticulous.example: A meticulous tailor in Old Dhaka measured my father twelve times before cutting a single inch of cloth for his wedding suit.

gre.s: The restoration took six years because the conservators were ____, cleaning the fresco one square centimeter at a time.
gre.clue: cleaning the fresco one square centimeter at a time

ornate.story: Ornate. Covered with a great deal of fancy decoration. Inside the old pink palace by the river, Dora stood still and stared. A grand staircase, crystal chandeliers, carved furniture and tall gilded mirrors filled every room. Even the ceilings seemed to curl with patterns. Her little sister tugged her hand and pointed at everything at once. The palace was truly ornate. Ornate shares its root with ornament: an ornate room is full of ornaments. So, what word describes something richly covered in fancy decoration?... Ornate.
ornate.example: The bride's ornate jamdani sari, woven with silver thread, took two weavers in Narayanganj almost four months to finish.

gre.s: Critics accustomed to the novelist's spare, plain prose were surprised by the ____ style of his memoir, with its long, flowery sentences and extravagant metaphors.
gre.clue: with its long, flowery sentences and extravagant metaphors

palpable.hook: PALPABLE: you can PALPATE it, touch it with your hand.
palpable.story: Palpable. So intense or obvious that it can almost be touched. In the minutes before the final exam results came out, Nate's whole family sat around one phone. Nobody spoke. His mother held her tea without drinking it, and his father kept checking the time. The tension was palpable. Then the page loaded, and Nate saw his name with top marks. His mother finally drank her tea, and the relief was just as palpable. Palpable comes from the Latin for touch: palpable feelings are ones you can almost touch. So, what word describes tension so strong you can almost feel it?... Palpable.
palpable.example: Relief was palpable in the village when the floodwater finally began to drop after eleven days.

gre.s: As the verdict was read, the courtroom's tension was ____, and several spectators visibly held their breath.
gre.clue: several spectators visibly held their breath

perpetuate.story: Perpetuate. To make something, often bad, continue for a long time. In Paul's office, new employees were always given the worst desks and the late shifts, simply because that was how the seniors had once been treated. Each year's juniors grew up and did the same to the next group. When Paul became a manager, he refused. "If we keep doing this, we perpetuate it forever." Perpetuate comes from perpetual, meaning lasting forever: to perpetuate a habit is to keep it going and going. So, what verb means to keep a bad practice alive?... Perpetuate.
perpetuate.example: Paying ransom to the pirates, the admiral warned, would only perpetuate the kidnappings it was meant to stop.

gre.s: Critics argue that the film's portrayal of the villagers as ignorant only serves to ____ stereotypes the director claimed to oppose.
gre.clue: stereotypes the director claimed to oppose

ploy.story: Ploy. A cunning plan or action designed to gain an advantage. Every evening at the old book market, one seller shouted, "Last copy! Last copy!" while waving a popular novel. Customers rushed to pay before it was gone. Arthur, a curious student, watched for an hour and noticed the seller pulling another last copy from a box under the table. Arthur grinned. It was a clever ploy. Ploy sounds close to plot: a ploy is a small plot to win an advantage. So, what word names a cunning trick to get ahead?... Ploy.
ploy.example: The free trial was just a ploy to collect card numbers, and most users were charged the moment it ended.

gre.s: Observers dismissed the minister's visit to the flooded villages, made days before the election with a dozen camera crews in tow, as a cynical ____ rather than a sincere act of compassion.
gre.clue: rather than a sincere act of compassion

prophetic.hook: PROPHETIC: like a PROPHET who foretells the future.
prophetic.story: Prophetic. Accurately predicting what will happen. In the nineteen nineties, Shannon's grandfather, a coastal rice farmer, warned his neighbours that the salty tides were creeping farther inland each year. "One day our rice will not grow here," he said. People shook their heads and went home. Today, many of those fields have turned into shrimp ponds, and Shannon often remembers his words. They seem prophetic now. A prophet foretells the future, and prophetic words turn out to be true. So, what word describes a warning that later comes true?... Prophetic.
prophetic.example: Written in 1949, the novel's picture of a society under constant surveillance now seems eerily prophetic.

gre.s: The economist's warnings, dismissed as alarmist when she first made them, proved ____ when the crisis struck exactly as she had predicted.
gre.clue: exactly as she had predicted

renounce.hook: RE-NOUNCE: an annouNCEment that you're giving it up.
renounce.story: Renounce. To formally give up a claim, right or belief. Neil's uncle owned a share of the family land, but he lived in Canada, and his sister farmed it alone to raise her children. One winter he flew home, sat with her before a lawyer, and signed a paper giving up his share forever. He renounced his claim so that her children would have security. Renounce shares a root with announce: you renounce something by announcing that you give it up. So, what verb means to formally give up a claim or right?... Renounce.
renounce.example: The heir shocked his family by renouncing his share of the tea estate and taking a small flat so he could work as a teacher.

gre.s: To accept the post, the businessman was required to ____ his foreign citizenship and divest himself of all private holdings.
gre.clue: divest himself of all private holdings

valor.hook: VALOR: VALUE of a hero's courage.
valor.story: Valor. Great bravery in the face of danger, as in war. Every December, Andy's grandfather takes out a faded photograph of young men in work shirts holding old rifles. In nineteen seventy-one, he was one of them, a freedom fighter crossing rivers at night during the war of independence. He rarely speaks of it, but the village honours him on Victory Day. Their valor is part of why their country exists. Valor shares a root with value, from the Latin for being strong: valor is strength of heart. So, what word means great bravery in battle?... Valor.
valor.example: The firefighters who carried workers out of the burning factory were honoured for their valor at a ceremony in Dhaka.

gre.s: The soldier was decorated for his ____, having repeatedly crossed enemy lines under heavy fire to carry wounded comrades to safety.
gre.clue: having repeatedly crossed enemy lines under heavy fire

amplify.hook: AMPLIFY: like a guitar AMP making sound louder.
amplify.story: Amplify. To make louder, larger or more intense; also, to expand on. On sports day at Sammy's school, the headmaster's voice was too soft to reach the back of the field. A technician wired a microphone into two old speakers, and suddenly his words boomed across the playground. The children cheered. The speakers had amplified his voice. Later, a teacher asked Sammy to amplify his short essay by adding examples. Amplify shares a root with ample, meaning large, and an amplifier makes sound larger. So, what verb means to make something louder or stronger?... Amplify.
amplify.example: Dry winds amplified the wildfire, driving the flames across the ridge faster than firefighters could dig trenches.

gre.s: Rather than calm public fears, the sensational news coverage served only to ____ them, turning a minor outbreak into a source of nationwide panic.
gre.clue: turning a minor outbreak into a source of nationwide panic

animosity.hook: ANIMOSITY: like ANIMALS growling at each other.
animosity.story: Animosity. Strong hostility or hatred. Two families in a farming village had quarrelled for thirty years over a strip of land no wider than a path. The fathers would not greet each other, and the mothers turned their faces at the market. Then Tara from one house and Ray from the other fell in love at college. At their wedding, the two grandfathers finally sat side by side, and the old animosity slowly melted. Animosity comes from the Latin animus, spirit or temper: animosity is a spirit turned hostile. So, what word names deep, lasting hostility?... Animosity.
animosity.example: Decades of animosity between the two chess clubs faded when their best players had to team up for the national championship.

gre.s: The two former allies now regard each other with open ____, refusing even to appear on the same stage after their bitter public quarrel.
gre.clue: after their bitter public quarrel

arduous.hook: ARDUOUS sounds like HARD-uous: hard work.
arduous.story: Arduous. Needing great effort and endurance; very difficult. To reach the top of a remote mountain peak, Nicole and her friends climbed for two days along steep, muddy trails. Leeches clung to their ankles, their water ran low, and every hill seemed to hide another hill. At the top, wrapped in cloud, Nicole sat down and smiled. The climb had been arduous, but worth it. Arduous comes from the Latin for steep: an arduous task feels like climbing a steep hill. So, what word describes a task that demands great effort and endurance?... Arduous.
arduous.example: Translating the thousand-page medical textbook into Bangla was an arduous task that occupied the team for four years.

gre.s: After months of ____ negotiations, marked by walkouts and late-night sessions, the two sides finally signed the agreement.
gre.clue: marked by walkouts and late-night sessions

avert.story: Avert. To prevent something bad from happening; also, to turn your eyes away. One stormy night, a tree fell across the railway line near Hugh's village. Hugh, a farm boy, saw it and ran down the track waving a red scarf as the night train's light appeared. The driver braked hard and stopped just short of the tree. Hugh had averted a disaster. Passengers who saw the huge trunk averted their eyes, shaking. Avert comes from the Latin for turn away: you turn the danger away. So, what verb means to prevent something bad from happening?... Avert.
avert.example: Quick thinking by the lab assistant, who shut off the gas valve, averted an explosion in the chemistry building.

gre.s: Only last-minute negotiations between the union and management managed to ____ a strike that would have shut down the country's ports for weeks.
gre.clue: last-minute negotiations between the union and management
