One rainy morning she whimsically cancelled the drawing test and took them all to sketch boats by the river. A whim is a sudden fancy, so a whimsical person is full of whims. So, what word describes art or a mood that is playful, fanciful and full of sudden impulses?... Whimsical.
whimsical.example: The picture book is full of whimsical touches, such as an elephant postman who delivers letters with his trunk.

gre.s: The architect's otherwise sober design included one ____ touch: a staircase painted to look like a row of giant piano keys.
gre.clue: otherwise sober design

willful.hook: WILL-FUL: full of your own WILL.
willful.story: Willful. Intentional; also, stubbornly determined to do as one wants. At her cousin's wedding, Rhonda's three-year-old nephew refused to wear shoes. Sandals were offered, then a chocolate, then his grandmother's gentle pleading. He sat on the floor, folded his arms, and went barefoot all evening. Everyone agreed he was the most willful guest there. In law, willful damage is damage done on purpose, not by accident. The trick: willful means full of will, your own will and nothing else. So, what word describes someone stubbornly set on getting their own way?... Willful.
willful.example: Smashing the bus shelter during the protest was a willful act, the magistrate said, and the fine would reflect that.

gre.s: The court ruled that the company's failure to report the leak was not an innocent oversight but a ____ deception, carried out with full knowledge of the risks.
gre.clue: not an innocent oversight

alienate.hook: ALIEN-ATE: makes you feel like an ALIEN.
alienate.story: Alienate. To drive people away so they feel unwelcome or shut out. When Andrew became class captain, he started giving orders and mocking anyone who made a mistake. Within a month, his friends stopped sitting with him at lunchtime, and he ate alone under the mango tree. He had alienated the very people who voted for him. An alien is an outsider, so to alienate someone is to make them feel like an alien among you. So, what verb means to push people away until they feel shut out?... Alienate.
alienate.example: The café's sudden price rise alienated the students who had been its most loyal customers for years.

gre.s: The senator's harsh remarks about immigrants threatened to ____ the very voters whose support she needed to win reelection.
gre.clue: the very voters whose support she needed

belligerent.story: Belligerent. Hostile and aggressive; eager to fight. After a small scrape between a bus and a car on the main road, the car owner jumped out shouting, fists raised, ready to fight the driver and anyone who tried to calm him. Traffic stopped in every direction. A traffic sergeant stepped between them and spoke quietly until the belligerent man finally backed away. The first part comes from the Latin for war, as in rebellion, so a belligerent person is always ready for war. So, what word describes someone hostile and itching for a fight?... Belligerent.
belligerent.example: After losing the toss, the belligerent captain argued with the umpire so loudly that play was delayed for twenty minutes.

gre.s: The diplomat's ____ remarks, which included open threats of military action, alarmed even his own government's allies.
gre.clue: open threats of military action

convoluted.hook: CONVOLUTED: like a coiled-up VOLUTE, twisted spiral.
convoluted.story: Convoluted. Twisted and so complicated it is hard to follow. Jenny went to a government office to renew her trade licence. She was sent to room four, then room nine, then back to room four, with a form needing three signatures. By afternoon she sat on a bench, holding a pile of papers. The process was hopelessly convoluted. Con means together and volu means roll, as in revolve, so something convoluted is rolled and twisted together like a tangled rope. So, what word describes a process so twisted it is hard to follow?... Convoluted.
convoluted.example: The film's convoluted plot, with three timelines and two sets of twins, left most of the audience lost by the interval.

gre.s: Students found the professor's lectures maddeningly ____, as each explanation looped through so many digressions that the main point was lost.
gre.clue: looped through so many digressions

decadent.story: Decadent. Marked by moral decline and excessive self-indulgence. In history class, Mark's teacher described the last years of a once powerful kingdom: rulers feasting through the night and building pleasure gardens while farmers went hungry and every warning was ignored. Mark was surprised how quickly a great empire could rot from the inside. Historians call such a court decadent. Decadent and decay come from the same Latin root for falling down, and a decadent society is one whose morals are decaying. So, what word describes a society sunk in luxury while its values fall apart?... Decadent.
decadent.example: Critics called the tycoon's gold-plated birthday cake decadent at a time when millions in the country could barely afford rice.

gre.s: Moralists of the era denounced the city's nightlife as ____, a sign that luxury and pleasure had corrupted the nation's character.
gre.clue: luxury and pleasure had corrupted the nation's character

deviate.story: Deviate. To move away from the usual path, plan, or rule. For twenty years, Kyle's father took the same road to his office downtown. One morning a burst water pipe flooded the street, and he had to deviate through a narrow lane of old houses. There he found a tiny sweet shop selling the best sweets he had ever tasted. Now he deviates from his route every Friday, just for that shop. Via means road in Latin, so to deviate is to go off the road. So, what verb means to move away from the usual path?... Deviate.
deviate.example: Whenever the professor deviated from her notes, the lecture grew livelier, full of stories from her fieldwork in the haor wetlands.

gre.s: Investigators concluded that the accident occurred because the crew chose to ____ from standard procedures, skipping two of the required safety checks before takeoff.
gre.clue: skipping two of the required safety checks

devious.story: Devious. Using dishonest or tricky methods to achieve goals. During the class election, Riley noticed something strange. His rival was quietly spreading a rumour that Riley planned to cancel the annual picnic, which was never true. Nobody saw who started it, but it spread fast, and Riley felt more hurt than angry. It was a devious trick, clever and dishonest at once. Devious and deviate share the Latin via, road, so a devious person leaves the straight road to get what he wants. So, what word describes someone who uses sneaky, dishonest methods?... Devious.
devious.example: In a devious move, the company changed its refund policy late on a Friday night, hoping customers would not notice until too late.

gre.s: Unable to win the contract fairly, the company resorted to ____ tactics, secretly leaking false information about its competitors to the press.
gre.clue: secretly leaking false information

disseminate.hook: DIS-SEMIN-ate: 'semin' is Latin for seed. Scattering seeds in every direction.
disseminate.story: Disseminate. To spread information or ideas widely. When a cyclone warning came for the southern coast, Red Crescent volunteers rode bicycles through the villages with megaphones, while the radio repeated the signal every hour. Loudspeakers announced it, and children ran from house to house. By evening the warning had been disseminated to every family, and people moved into the shelters. Hidden inside disseminate is semin, from the Latin for seed, so to disseminate is to scatter ideas like seeds in every direction. So, what verb means to spread information far and wide?... Disseminate.
disseminate.example: Community radio stations along the coast disseminate cyclone warnings in local dialects so that fishermen understand them quickly.

gre.s: Public health officials worked to ____ accurate information about the virus as quickly as rumors were spreading online.
gre.clue: as quickly as rumors were spreading

duress.story: Duress. Threats or force used to make someone do something. A small-town shopkeeper signed away his land after local thugs visited his shop three nights in a row and warned him about his children. Later, in court, his lawyer argued that the signature meant nothing, because it was given under duress. The judge agreed, and the land was returned to him. Duress shares a root with durable, meaning hard, so duress is hard pressure that leaves you no real choice. So, what word names the threats used to force someone into an act?... Duress.
duress.example: Hostages who praised their captors in a video later explained that they had spoken under duress.

gre.s: The judge ruled the confession inadmissible because it had been obtained under ____: the suspect had been threatened and denied sleep for three days.
gre.clue: had been threatened and denied sleep for three days

egalitarian.hook: EGALITARIAN: EGAL means equal in French (égal).
egalitarian.story: Egalitarian. Believing in equal rights and opportunities for all people. At Nina's grandmother's house, everyone eats together on one long mat: the family, the cook, the gardener, and the boy who brings milk each morning. Nobody gets a better plate, and the youngest serves the oldest first. Nina once saw a visiting uncle look confused, then sit down happily beside the gardener. Her grandmother's home is truly egalitarian. The first part is French for equal, so egalitarian means believing everyone is equal. So, what word describes the belief that all people deserve equal rights?... Egalitarian.
egalitarian.example: The village cooperative is strikingly egalitarian, giving every member one vote no matter how much land or money they bring.

gre.s: Although the society claimed to be ____, its rigid caste system ensured that wealth and power remained in the hands of a few families.
gre.clue: its rigid caste system ensured

evasive.story: Evasive. Avoiding giving a clear, straight answer. When Tracy asked her younger brother why the window was broken, he talked about the weather, the cricket score, and the strange noise the neighbour's cat made at night. Everything except the window. Tracy folded her arms and waited. His answers were completely evasive. Finally he admitted that the ball had flown farther than he planned. Evasive comes from evade, to slip away, and an evasive answer slips away from the question. So, what word describes an answer that dodges the question?... Evasive.
evasive.example: My little brother turns evasive whenever Ammu asks about his homework, suddenly eager to discuss football or the weather.

gre.s: When asked directly about the missing funds, the treasurer grew ____, changing the subject and answering questions nobody had asked.
gre.clue: changing the subject and answering questions nobody had asked

expedite.hook: EXPEDITE: as fast as an EXPRESS delivery.
expedite.story: Expedite. To make something happen faster. Peyton's student visa interview was only five days away, but her new passport was still being processed. Her father took the bus to the passport office at dawn, showed the interview letter, and politely asked whether they could expedite the case. The officer nodded and stamped a form, and the passport arrived in two days. Peyton hugged it with relief. Ex means out and ped means foot, so to expedite is to free the feet so things can move faster. So, what verb means to speed something up?... Expedite.
expedite.example: A new online system has expedited passport renewals, cutting the wait from several months to a few weeks.

gre.s: To ____ the relief effort, the government waived the usual customs inspections for shipments of food and medicine.
gre.clue: waived the usual customs inspections

fervent.story: Fervent. Having or showing intense passion. On the night of a big cricket match, Shawn's grandmother sat right in front of the television, praying under her breath before every single ball. When their team hit the winning run, she clapped and cried at the same time, and hugged everyone in the room. Nobody in the family was a more fervent fan. Fervent comes from the Latin for boiling, so a fervent person's feelings are bubbling hot. So, what word describes passion that is intense and glowing?... Fervent.
fervent.example: A fervent believer in public libraries, the retired teacher gave her entire collection of three thousand books to the town of Jashore.

gre.s: Though once a ____ supporter of the policy, attending every rally and writing letters to every newspaper, he became its harshest critic after seeing its effects.
gre.clue: attending every rally and writing letters to every newspaper

fervor.story: Fervor. Strong, burning enthusiasm or emotion. Before dawn on the twenty-first of February, Lily joined thousands of people walking barefoot to the language martyrs' monument with flowers in their hands. Old men, schoolchildren and students sang the old song of mourning, their voices rising together in the cold air. Lily felt the fervor in her chest, a deep passion for the mother tongue that so many had died to protect. Fervor sounds close to fever, and fervor is a fever of strong feeling. So, what word names a burning enthusiasm shared by a whole crowd?... Fervor.
fervor.example: The scientist spoke about coral reefs with such fervor that several students switched their majors to marine biology.

gre.s: The early ____ of the movement gradually cooled into apathy as its leaders became mired in internal disputes.
gre.clue: gradually cooled into apathy

flamboyant.hook: FLAMBOYANT: like FLAMES, bright and impossible to ignore.
flamboyant.story: Flamboyant. Very confident, showy, and colorful in a way that attracts attention. At the spring fair, Zach's uncle arrived in a bright red suit embroidered with gold, a yellow scarf, and sunglasses shaped like stars. He danced to every drum, greeted strangers like old friends, and posed for every camera. The children followed him everywhere. He was gloriously flamboyant. Flamboyant comes from the French for flaming, so a flamboyant person blazes like a flame that nobody can ignore. So, what word describes a showy, colorful person who loves attention?... Flamboyant.
flamboyant.example: The flamboyant chess champion arrived at every match in a velvet cape, though his play was cautious and precise.

gre.s: Unlike her ____ predecessor, who favored sequined gowns and dramatic entrances, the new director dresses plainly and avoids the spotlight.
gre.clue: who favored sequined gowns and dramatic entrances

impediment.story: Impediment. An obstacle; something that blocks progress. Abby dreamed of studying abroad, but her village had no reliable internet, a serious impediment to her GRE preparation. So every Friday she rode a crowded bus for two hours to the district town, where a library had free wifi, and studied until closing time. A year later, she won a scholarship. The impediment had slowed her, never stopped her. Impede comes from the Latin for shackling the feet, so an impediment ties up your feet as you try to move. So, what word names an obstacle that blocks your progress?... Impediment.
impediment.example: Poor eyesight was no impediment to Rafiq's career as a radio host, since listeners only ever heard his voice.

gre.s: Lack of reliable electricity remains the single greatest ____ to industrial growth in the region, deterring investors who might otherwise build factories there.
gre.clue: deterring investors who might otherwise build factories there

incendiary.hook: INCENDIARY: think INCENSE that's lit, or a fire that's lit.
incendiary.story: Incendiary. Designed to start fires; also, tending to stir up conflict or anger. In a quiet town, someone posted an incendiary message online, a false claim meant to make two neighbourhoods hate each other. Within hours, angry crowds gathered. Then an old imam and a local teacher stood together in the market and calmly told everyone the truth, and the crowd slowly went home. Incendiary words work like incendiary bombs: they are made to start fires. Incense, which is lit to burn, comes from the same Latin root. So, what word describes speech designed to inflame anger?... Incendiary.
incendiary.example: The blogger was arrested after posting incendiary videos that urged viewers to attack a neighbouring village.

gre.s: The editor refused to print the letter, judging its ____ language likely to provoke riots in an already tense city.
gre.clue: likely to provoke riots

incessant.story: Incessant. Going on and on without ever stopping. One July, the monsoon rain over the hills fell for three days without a pause. It drummed on the tin roof all night, gurgled in the drains, and turned the lane into a small river. Ivy lay awake, listening to the incessant rain, and wondered whether her exam would be cancelled. In means not, and cess comes from the same root as cease, so something incessant does not cease. So, what word describes rain or noise that never stops?... Incessant.
incessant.example: The incessant honking on Mirpur Road makes it almost impossible to hold a phone conversation near the bus stop.

gre.s: The ____ noise from the construction site, which continued day and night for months, drove many residents to move away.
gre.clue: which continued day and night for months

innocuous.story: Innocuous. Harmless and unlikely to upset anyone. In her first week at a new office, Sasha worried that her question would sound silly in the meeting. Finally, in a soft voice, she asked whether the report could be sent a day later. It was a completely innocuous request, and her manager simply nodded and smiled. Afterwards Sasha shook her head at herself for being so nervous. Innocuous shares a root with noxious, meaning harmful, and in means not, so innocuous means not harmful at all. So, what word describes a remark or request that harms nobody?... Innocuous.
innocuous.example: Most garden spiders are innocuous to humans, though their size frightens many people who find them in the shed.

gre.s: What seemed an ____ comment about the budget was interpreted by the minister as a direct attack and provoked a furious response.
gre.clue: was interpreted by the minister as a direct attack

insular.hook: INSULAR: like an ISLAND (insula in Latin), cut off from the world.
insular.story: Insular. Narrow-minded and uninterested in outside ideas or cultures. When Felix went to study in Toronto, he spent his whole first year with students from his home country, eating at the same restaurant from home and never trying anything new. Then a Korean classmate invited him home for dinner, and over bowls of spicy soup Felix realised how insular his life had become. The root insula is Latin for island, so an insular person lives like an island, cut off from new ideas. So, what word describes a narrow mind closed to outside ideas and cultures?... Insular.
insular.example: Raised in an insular boarding school, Omar knew almost nothing about popular music until he arrived at university.

gre.s: Critics accused the academic department of being ____, citing its refusal to engage with scholars from other disciplines or countries.
gre.clue: its refusal to engage with scholars from other disciplines or countries

intrepid.story: Intrepid. Fearless and adventurous. Sharon grew up in a crowded city flat, but every winter she leads a group of young women up the steep jungle trails to the top of a remote mountain. They cross slippery streams, sleep in bamboo huts, and climb through the clouds. When others hesitate at a narrow ridge, Sharon goes first, smiling. Her friends call her their intrepid leader. Trepid means trembling, as in trepidation, and in means not, so an intrepid person does not tremble. So, what word describes someone fearless and adventurous?... Intrepid.
intrepid.example: Intrepid divers explored the flooded cave for six hours, mapping tunnels that no person had ever entered.

gre.s: The ____ journalist ventured into the war zone that other reporters had fled, sending back dispatches from the front lines.
gre.clue: that other reporters had fled

paragon.story: Paragon. A model of excellence; a perfect example. Everyone in Kathy's village knew Miss Rose, the schoolteacher who taught there for forty years. She was never late, never lost her temper, and paid for poor children's books from her own salary. When she retired, the whole village came to say goodbye. She was a paragon of kindness and duty. Paragon comes from an old Italian word for a touchstone, so a paragon is the standard everything else is measured against. So, what word names a perfect model of excellence?... Paragon.
paragon.example: Our neighbour, a paragon of patience, taught all six of us children to ride a bicycle without once raising his voice.

gre.s: Admired throughout her long career as a ____ of integrity, the judge stunned the public when evidence emerged that she had accepted bribes for years.
gre.clue: Admired throughout her long career

parochial.hook: PAROCHIAL: limited to the local PARISH.
parochial.story: Parochial. Having a limited or narrow outlook. At a neighbourhood committee meeting in a river town, the members argued for two hours about who would pay for one street light, while a flood warning for the whole district lay unread on the table. Ian, a young engineer, finally stood up and reminded them of the river. Their concerns had been painfully parochial. Parochial comes from parish, a small local church area, so a parochial view never looks beyond the parish. So, what word describes a narrow outlook that ignores the bigger picture?... Parochial.
parochial.example: The newspaper's parochial coverage filled its front page with a council quarrel on the very day a war broke out abroad.

gre.s: Critics complained that the festival had become increasingly ____, showcasing only local filmmakers and ignoring the vibrant international cinema it had once championed.
gre.clue: showcasing only local filmmakers and ignoring the vibrant international cinema

penchant.hook: PENCHANT: leaning toward it like a PENDANT hangs down.
penchant.story: Penchant. A strong liking or habitual tendency. Travis's father has a penchant for street food. On every evening walk through the old city, he stops for spicy snacks, then a cup of creamy tea, then hot syrupy spirals from a pan of bubbling oil. His wife pretends to complain, but she always shares the sweets. Penchant comes from the French for leaning, from the same Latin root as pendant, so a penchant is something you lean toward again and again. So, what word names a strong, habitual liking for something?... Penchant.
penchant.example: Kabir's penchant for puns made him popular at parties and unbearable during exam week.

gre.s: Given the senator's well-known ____ for theatrical gestures, no one was surprised when he tore up the bill on live television.
gre.clue: no one was surprised

poise.hook: POISE: perfectly POISED, balanced and calm.
poise.story: Poise. A graceful, calm, self-controlled manner. Halfway through Natalie's speech at the national debate, the microphone died and the hall filled with whispers. She did not panic. She stepped forward, lifted her voice, and finished every sentence calmly, as if nothing had happened. The judges remembered her poise even more than her arguments. Poise also means balance, as when a dancer stands poised on one foot, so think of poise as a mind perfectly balanced. So, what word names a graceful calm that stays steady under pressure?... Poise.
poise.example: Only fourteen, the young pianist played before a packed hall at Shilpakala Academy with the poise of a seasoned professional.

gre.s: Even when hecklers repeatedly interrupted her speech, the young candidate showed remarkable ____, answering each insult calmly and returning to her argument without missing a beat.
gre.clue: answering each insult calmly

preclude.hook: PRE-CLUDE: CLOSE the door BEFORE it can happen.
preclude.story: Preclude. To prevent from happening; to make impossible. Finn had trained for months for the inter-university cricket final. Then, three days before the match, he broke his wrist falling off a rickshaw. The injury precluded any chance of playing. He sat in the stands with his arm in a cast, cheering louder than anyone. Pre means before and clude means close, as in include and exclude, so to preclude something is to close the door on it before it can happen. So, what verb means to make something impossible in advance?... Preclude.
preclude.example: Dense fog precluded any flights from leaving Dhaka until midday, stranding hundreds of passengers in the terminal.

gre.s: The patient's weak heart may ____ surgery, forcing doctors to consider gentler forms of treatment.
gre.clue: forcing doctors to consider gentler forms of treatment

replenish.story: Replenish. To fill something up again. After a long dry winter, the pond behind Ruth's house had shrunk to a muddy puddle, and the ducks wandered around its edge. Then came the first heavy rains of the monsoon. Within a week the pond was full again, frogs sang at night, and the ducks swam in circles. Ruth smiled as the rain replenished it. Plenish comes from the Latin for full, as in plenty, so to replenish is to make full again. So, what verb means to refill something that has run low?... Replenish.
replenish.example: Elephants visit the salt lick every evening to replenish the minerals they lose in the summer heat.

gre.s: After the long drought, months of heavy rain were needed to ____ the reservoirs, which had shrunk to a tenth of their usual capacity.
gre.clue: which had shrunk to a tenth of their usual capacity

rigor.story: Rigor. Strictness, thoroughness, and accuracy; also, harsh conditions. Before Adrian could submit his thesis, his supervisor checked every number, every source, and every comma, and made him repeat one experiment three times. Adrian grumbled at first. But at his defence, the examiners praised the rigor of his work. The word can also mean harsh conditions, like the rigors of a long winter. Rigor and rigid share a root, so rigor is rigid strictness. So, what word names strict, careful thoroughness?... Rigor.
rigor.example: Few of the volunteers were prepared for the rigors of a long winter at the Antarctic research station.

gre.s: The journal is famous for its ____: every submitted paper is checked by three independent reviewers, and every statistical claim must be reproduced before publication.
gre.clue: every statistical claim must be reproduced before publication

unscrupulous.story: Unscrupulous. Willing to cheat or do wrong to get what one wants. A man in a neat suit came to Sean's village, promising young men good jobs abroad for a fee of three thousand dollars each. Families sold cattle to pay him. Then he vanished, and his phone number stopped working. The police later called him an unscrupulous agent. Scruple comes from the Latin for a small sharp stone, like a pebble in your shoe that troubles you; an unscrupulous person feels no such pebble. So, what word describes someone with no conscience about cheating?... Unscrupulous.
unscrupulous.example: Unscrupulous builders sometimes save money by mixing too much sand into the concrete, endangering everyone who will live inside.

gre.s: The ____ landlord evicted elderly tenants on false pretexts so that he could rent their apartments at triple the price.
gre.clue: evicted elderly tenants on false pretexts

utilitarian.story: Utilitarian. Built for practical use, with little thought for beauty. The flood shelter by the river is a plain grey concrete box on tall pillars, with bare walls, steel shutters and a wide ramp for cattle. It is not pretty. But when the river rose, four hundred people and their animals stayed safe and dry inside. Sometimes a utilitarian building is the most beautiful thing in the village. Utilitarian comes from utility, meaning usefulness: use first, beauty later. So, what word describes something designed purely to be useful?... Utilitarian.
utilitarian.example: Grandfather's utilitarian bicycle had no gears, no bell and no paint, yet it carried him to the market for forty years.

gre.s: The factory's ____ design, which prioritized efficiency over appearance, made it one of the least attractive buildings in the city.
gre.clue: prioritized efficiency over appearance

xenophobic.story: Xenophobic. Fearing or disliking people from other countries. When Rob moved to a small town abroad for his master's degree, a neighbour refused to return his greeting and once told him to go back home. Rob felt lonely for weeks. But his elderly landlady brought him soup when he caught a cold and introduced him to her friends. One xenophobic neighbour had hurt him; many kind ones helped him heal. Xeno is Greek for stranger and phobia means fear, so xenophobic means afraid of strangers from abroad. So, what word describes fear or dislike of foreigners?... Xenophobic.
xenophobic.example: Some fans shouted xenophobic insults at the visiting team's foreign players, and the league banned them from the stadium for a year.

gre.s: Critics warned that the party's ____ rhetoric, which blamed immigrants for every economic problem, would inflame hostility toward the nation's foreign-born residents.
gre.clue: blamed immigrants for every economic problem

abject.hook: AB-JECT: thrown (ject) away (ab), cast down to the lowest point.
abject.story: Abject. Extremely miserable or hopeless; completely without pride or dignity. After river erosion swallowed his family's land, Sam lived for a season in abject poverty, sleeping under plastic sheets on an embankment and eating one meal a day. Yet he never stopped going to school. Today he teaches in the same district, and he still remembers those abject months. Ab means away and ject means thrown, as in reject, so abject means thrown away, cast down to the lowest point. So, what word describes misery so deep it feels completely hopeless?... Abject.
abject.example: Caught copying his lab report, Rafi sent the professor an abject email that apologized four times in three short paragraphs.

gre.s: Far from the defiant statement his supporters expected, the senator issued an ____ apology, begging forgiveness and conceding every one of his critics' points.
gre.clue: begging forgiveness and conceding every one of his critics' points

aloof.hook: ALOOF: sits ALOFT on the ROOF, far above everyone.
aloof.story: Aloof. Distant and unfriendly; emotionally reserved. When a new boy named Zeke joined Frank's class, he sat alone, answered in single words, and never joined the cricket at lunch. Everyone thought he was proud and aloof. Then Frank learned that Zeke's father had just lost his job, and the boy was simply shy and sad. The next day, Frank asked him to bat first. Aloof began as a sailor's word for keeping a ship away from the shore, so an aloof person keeps away from others. So, what word describes someone who stays cool and distant?... Aloof.
aloof.example: The new striker stayed aloof from his teammates during training, eating lunch alone and skipping the squad's evening card games.

gre.s: Although the actress appeared ____ in interviews, rarely smiling or revealing anything personal, her friends describe her as warm and playful.
gre.clue: rarely smiling or revealing anything personal

ambivalent.hook: AMBI = both (ambidextrous). Feeling BOTH ways at once.
ambivalent.story: Ambivalent. Having mixed or contradictory feelings about something. When Mason got a job offer in Singapore, his mother was ambivalent. She was proud that her son had done so well, and she told every neighbour about it. But at night she thought of his empty room and wondered who would eat her mango pickle now. Ambi means both, as in ambidextrous, and valent means strength, so ambivalent means feeling two strong pulls at once. So, what word describes feeling both happy and sad about the same thing?... Ambivalent.
ambivalent.example: Nusrat felt ambivalent about the job offer in Chittagong, eager for the higher salary but reluctant to leave her parents in Dhaka.

gre.s: The critic remained ____ about the novel, admiring its lyrical prose while deploring its sluggish, aimless plot.
gre.clue: admiring its lyrical prose while deploring

amicable.story: Amicable. Friendly and without serious disagreement. Two brothers in a quiet town had to divide the family land and house. The neighbours expected shouting and lawyers, as so often happens. Instead, the brothers sat on the veranda over tea, walked the fields together, and agreed on every boundary in a single afternoon. Their mother cried with relief. It was a completely amicable settlement. Amicable comes from amicus, the Latin for friend, like amigo in Spanish. So, what word describes an agreement reached in a friendly way?... Amicable.
amicable.example: The two neighbors ended their long quarrel over the shared wall with an amicable chat over tea on the rooftop.

gre.s: Although the negotiations had been tense, the two companies reached an ____ settlement, parting on such good terms that they later launched a joint venture.
gre.clue: parting on such good terms that they later launched a joint venture

arcane.hook: ARCANE: hidden in an ARK, like secret knowledge only priests can read.
arcane.story: Arcane. Obscure and puzzling, familiar only to a small group of specialists. In a back room of the county land office, Rob's uncle spends his days reading old land records full of Persian terms. Old record terms mean nothing to most people, but he reads a century-old deed as easily as a newspaper. To everyone else, it is arcane knowledge. Arcane comes from the Latin for a chest or box, the same root as ark, so arcane knowledge is locked away for the few. So, what word describes knowledge so obscure that only specialists understand it?... Arcane.
arcane.example: The tax code is so arcane that even experienced accountants in Motijheel sometimes phone colleagues to interpret a single clause.

gre.s: The scholar's knowledge of ____ medieval manuscripts, which perhaps a dozen people in the world could read, made her indispensable to the museum.
gre.clue: which perhaps a dozen people in the world could read

austere.hook: AUSTERE sounds like 'a stair' of bare concrete: no carpet, no decoration, just hard steps.
austere.story: Austere. Very strict or serious; also, extremely plain, without comfort or decoration. Alan's grandfather lived in an austere room: a wooden bed, one chair, a shelf of books and a single bulb. No television, no carpet. He rose at dawn, ate plain rice and dal, and wasted nothing. Alan used to find it sad. Now, as a stressed young banker, he sometimes envies that austere peace. Think of austerity, when a government cuts every luxury: austere means stripped down to bare needs. So, what word describes a life or room that is very plain and strict?... Austere.
austere.example: The physics department occupied an austere concrete building with bare walls, metal chairs, and a single flickering lamp in each corridor.

gre.s: In contrast to the lavish palaces of his predecessors, the new ruler's residence was strikingly ____, furnished with little more than a desk and a cot.
gre.clue: In contrast to the lavish palaces

buoyant.hook: BUOYANT: like a BUOY, always floating up.
buoyant.story: Buoyant. Able to stay afloat; also, lighthearted and hopeful. At his first swimming lesson in the village pond, Nell's little brother clung to a raft of banana trunks, terrified. The trunks were so buoyant that they floated even with him on top, and soon he was kicking and laughing. He came home in a buoyant mood, telling everyone he would swim across the great river one day. A buoy floats up on the water, and a buoyant person's spirits float up the same way. So, what word describes something that floats, or a mood that stays light and hopeful?... Buoyant.
buoyant.example: Despite losing the first two matches, the team's mood stayed buoyant, and the players joked loudly on the bus back to Sylhet.

gre.s: Investors remained ____ despite the gloomy forecasts, convinced that the economy would rebound within a few months and reward those who held their nerve.
gre.clue: convinced that the economy would rebound within a few months

caustic.hook: CAUSTIC soda burns your skin; caustic words burn your feelings.
caustic.story: Caustic. Able to burn chemically; also, sarcastically bitter and hurtful. In the chemistry lab, the teacher warned Isabelle never to touch caustic soda, because it burns the skin. That evening, at a family gathering, an aunt glanced at Isabelle's results and said, "Only seventy marks? Your cousin got ninety, and she hardly studies." The caustic remark stung far longer than any chemical. Caustic comes from the Greek for burning, so caustic words burn feelings the way caustic soda burns skin. So, what word describes a comment that is bitter and hurtful?... Caustic.
caustic.example: The chemistry teacher warned the class that the caustic solution could burn skin within seconds and insisted everyone wear gloves.

gre.s: The reviewer's ____ wit, which spared neither the actors nor the director, made her columns as feared as they were entertaining.
gre.clue: spared neither the actors nor the director

conundrum.hook: CONUNDRUM: a DRUM of confusion banging in your head.
conundrum.story: Conundrum. A puzzling problem that has no easy answer. Travis won two scholarships in the same week: one to study engineering in Germany, the other to study medicine at home, close to his parents. Both were dreams. That night he sat on the roof, watching the city lights and turning it over in his head. It was a real conundrum, with no easy answer. Picture a drum of confusion banging inside your head: that is a conundrum. So, what word names a puzzling problem with no easy answer?... Conundrum.
conundrum.example: Choosing a university became a real conundrum for Tanvir, since the best program was abroad but his family could not afford the fees.

gre.s: The dwindling water supply poses a genuine ____ for officials: restricting use would anger farmers, yet doing nothing would leave the city dry within a decade.
gre.clue: restricting use would anger farmers, yet doing nothing would leave the city dry

curtail.story: Curtail. To reduce or cut short. When fuel prices rose sharply, Carl's family had to curtail their spending. No more Friday dinners at the Chinese restaurant, fewer new clothes for the holidays, and the air conditioner switched off before midnight. Carl's mother even curtailed her long phone calls to her sister. They managed, and they grew closer around the dinner table. Hear the word tail inside curtail, and picture a long tail being cut short. So, what verb means to cut something back or cut it short?... Curtail.
curtail.example: Repeated power cuts curtailed evening study hours at the dormitory, so students began gathering under the streetlights to finish their homework.

gre.s: Fearing a budget shortfall, the university was forced to ____ its research programs, eliminating nearly a third of them.
gre.clue: eliminating nearly a third of them

detract.story: Detract. To reduce the value or quality of something. Jessie's wedding photographs were beautiful: a red sari, marigolds, soft evening light. But in the background of every picture hung a tangle of electric wires and a rusty water tank. Her photographer promised to edit them out, because they detracted from the beauty of the day. Tract comes from the Latin for pull, as in tractor, and de means away, so to detract is to pull value away. So, what verb means to take away from something's value or beauty?... Detract.
detract.example: The noisy air conditioner detracted from an otherwise moving concert, drowning out the softest passages of the sitar solo.

gre.s: A few minor typographical errors do little to ____ from what is otherwise a meticulously researched and elegantly written history.
gre.clue: otherwise a meticulously researched and elegantly written history

enmity.story: Enmity. Deep hostility; the state of being enemies. For thirty years, two families in a farming village had not spoken. A quarrel over a mango tree on the boundary had grown into an enmity that their grandchildren inherited without knowing why. Then the floods came, and one family's boat was the only one left. They rescued their neighbours without a word, and the old enmity simply melted on the water. Enmity is built from enemy: the state of being enemies. So, what word names a long, deep hostility between people?... Enmity.
enmity.example: Years of open enmity ended only when the two retired tennis champions, once bitter rivals, agreed to coach the national youth squad together.

gre.s: The ____ between the two clans, rooted in a dispute over land generations earlier, was so bitter that members refused even to attend the same weddings.
gre.clue: so bitter that members refused even to attend the same weddings

ephemeral.hook: EPHEMERAL: like an Instagram story, gone in a day.
ephemeral.story: Ephemeral. Short-lived; fading soon after it appears. On winter mornings, fog covers the hillside tea gardens, and drops of dew shine on the leaves like tiny diamonds. Piper stopped on the path to photograph them. By nine o'clock the sun had burned the mist away, and the diamonds were gone. Such beauty is ephemeral. Ephemeral comes from the Greek for lasting only a day, so ephemeral things are here today and gone tomorrow. So, what word describes beauty that fades almost as soon as it appears?... Ephemeral.
ephemeral.example: Most viral dance trends are ephemeral, filling every phone screen in Dhaka for a week before they are forgotten entirely.

gre.s: Unlike the ____ fashions that vanish within a season, the designer's classic coat has remained popular for over fifty years.
gre.clue: vanish within a season

exorbitant.hook: EX-ORBIT-ANT: prices gone OUT OF ORBIT.
exorbitant.story: Exorbitant. Unreasonably high, especially of price. Two days before the holiday, Stan tried to buy a bus ticket home. The man at the counter shrugged and asked for three times the normal fare. Stan stared at him. Every ticket left in the city had an exorbitant price. In the end, he shared a minibus with five other students. Ex means out of and orbita means track, so an exorbitant price has jumped right out of its normal track. So, what word describes a price that is unreasonably high?... Exorbitant.
exorbitant.example: The landlord demanded an exorbitant deposit of six months' rent, so the young couple kept searching for another flat in Mirpur.

gre.s: Many families who once used the private clinic now avoid it, since its ____ fees put even routine checkups beyond the reach of ordinary workers.
gre.clue: put even routine checkups beyond the reach of ordinary workers

fawn.hook: FAWN: like a puppy wagging its tail, licking boots.
fawn.story: Fawn. To flatter or please someone excessively to gain favour. When the company director visited the port city branch, one officer rushed to carry his bag, laughed loudly at every joke, and praised even his tie. The other staff exchanged quiet glances. They had seen him fawn over every boss who ever visited. Picture a puppy wagging its tail and licking your shoes for a biscuit: that is how a fawning person behaves. Do not confuse it with a fawn, the baby deer. So, what verb means to flatter someone too much to win their favour?... Fawn.
fawn.example: Reporters who fawned over the billionaire at his product launch later struggled to ask him any hard questions about his company's debts.

gre.s: Whenever the visiting director appeared, the junior staff would ____, laughing politely at his weakest jokes and praising his every remark, while the senior engineers remained coolly professional.
gre.clue: praising his every remark

flagrant.hook: FLAGRANT: as obvious as a FLAG waving in your face.
flagrant.story: Flagrant. Done openly and shamelessly, so the wrong is impossible to miss. In a school cricket match, the bowler stepped far over the line, a clear no-ball, and the batsman was caught. Yet the umpire, who happened to be the bowler's uncle, raised his finger and gave the batsman out. The crowd went silent, then booed. It was a flagrant act of favouritism. Flagrant comes from the Latin for blazing, so a flagrant wrong blazes in plain sight. So, what word describes wrongdoing that is shameless and impossible to miss?... Flagrant.
flagrant.example: The referee sent off the defender for a flagrant foul, a reckless late tackle that left the striker lying on the grass.

gre.s: Far from being a subtle oversight, the company's dumping of chemicals into the river was a ____ violation of environmental law, carried out openly in daylight for years.
gre.clue: carried out openly in daylight for years

forgo.story: Forgo. To do without something pleasant; to give up. Every holiday, Lena's family buys new clothes. This year, after floods destroyed the home of her school's cleaner, Lena decided to forgo her new dress and gave the money to his family instead. Her mother said nothing, only held her close. In forgo, for means away, so to forgo something is to let it go away. Do not mix it up with forego, which means to go before. So, what verb means to give up something pleasant by choice?... Forgo.
forgo.example: To pay her younger brother's school fees, Shirin decided to forgo new clothes for Eid two years in a row.

gre.s: Determined to finish her dissertation by spring, the doctoral student chose to ____ the holiday trip her friends had planned, staying behind in the library instead.
gre.clue: staying behind in the library instead

improvise.hook: IMPROVISE: IM-PRO-VISE, not foreseen (pro-vise), done on the spot.
improvise.story: Improvise. To make or do something on the spot without planning ahead. Halfway through Isaac's sister's wedding party, the power went out and the music died. Then Isaac grabbed a steel pot and a spoon, his cousins started clapping, and the aunties began singing old wedding songs. Everyone danced harder than before. They had improvised a whole band in two minutes. Im means not, and provise is from the Latin for foreseen, as in provide, so to improvise is to act without foreseeing. So, what verb means to make something up on the spot?... Improvise.
improvise.example: When the tent pole snapped during the camping trip, Farhan improvised a replacement from a bamboo stick and some rope.

gre.s: When the main speaker failed to arrive, the host was forced to ____, delivering a twenty-minute talk with no notes at all.
gre.clue: with no notes at all

indiscriminate.hook: IN-DISCRIMINATE: doesn't DISCRIMINATE, doesn't choose carefully.
indiscriminate.story: Indiscriminate. Done carelessly, without choosing or judging with care. Every evening, Anna watched her uncle forward dozens of messages to the family group: health tips, fake news, old jokes and photos of flowers, all without reading them first. One day he forwarded a scam, and two cousins nearly lost money. Anna gently asked him to be less indiscriminate. To discriminate is to choose carefully between things, so indiscriminate means not choosing at all, just grabbing everything. So, what word describes careless action done without judgment?... Indiscriminate.
indiscriminate.example: Doctors warn that the indiscriminate use of antibiotics, often bought without a prescription, is breeding bacteria that no drug can kill.

gre.s: Critics condemned the ____ bombing campaign, which struck hospitals and markets as readily as military targets.
gre.clue: struck hospitals and markets as readily as military targets

inquisitive.story: Inquisitive. Curious; eager for knowledge. Four-year-old Archie never stops asking questions. Why is the sky blue? Why do ducks not get wet? Where does the rain go after it falls? His grandmother answers every one patiently, and when she does not know, she says, "Let us find out together." An inquisitive child keeps the whole family thinking. Inquisitive comes from inquire, to ask, so an inquisitive person is always inquiring. So, what word describes a child who is curious about everything?... Inquisitive.
inquisitive.example: An inquisitive reader, my grandfather filled the margins of his books with questions he planned to look up later.

gre.s: Endlessly ____, the young scientist pestered her mentors with questions and spent her weekends dismantling old instruments to learn how they worked.
gre.clue: pestered her mentors with questions

meritorious.story: Meritorious. Deserving praise or reward. During the floods, a young boatman named Rudy made trip after trip through the rising water, carrying old people and children to the school shelter. He did not stop for two days, even when his hands blistered. Later, the district honoured him with an award for meritorious service. Rudy only said he had done what any neighbour would do. Meritorious means full of merit, deserving praise. So, what word describes an action that deserves honour and reward?... Meritorious.
meritorious.example: The fire officer received a medal for meritorious service after pulling six workers from the burning garment factory in Ashulia.

gre.s: The committee rejected his nomination, arguing that his work, while competent, was not especially ____ and did nothing to distinguish him from his peers.
gre.clue: did nothing to distinguish him from his peers

narcissist.hook: NARCISSUS: fell in love with his own reflection.
narcissist.story: Narcissist. Someone overly absorbed in admiring themselves and their looks. At a cousin's wedding, Sienna noticed one guest who spent the whole evening taking selfies. He checked his hair in every mirror, posted forty photos of himself, and never once asked the bride how she was. Sienna whispered to her sister that he was a true narcissist. In the Greek myth, Narcissus fell in love with his own reflection in a pool, and a narcissist does much the same. So, what word names someone obsessed with admiring himself?... Narcissist.
narcissist.example: Only a narcissist would turn a friend's wedding toast into ten minutes about his own career, the guests muttered afterward.

gre.s: A thoroughgoing ____, the actor treated every interview as an occasion for self-praise and could rarely sit through a conversation that was not about himself.
gre.clue: could rarely sit through a conversation that was not about himself

placid.hook: PLACID: a PLACE that's calm, like a still lake.
placid.story: Placid. Calm and peaceful; not easily upset. On a still winter morning, the mountain lake lies so placid that the green hills appear twice, once against the sky and once upside down in the water. Ralph's grandmother is like that lake. Even when the rice burns or the grandchildren shout, she smiles and fixes things. Her placid nature calms everyone around her. Placid is a cousin of placate, which means to calm someone down. So, what word describes a calm lake, or a calm person who is not easily upset?... Placid.
placid.example: Even when the toddlers screamed and threw rice across the table, their placid grandmother simply carried on with her story.

gre.s: Despite the chaos surrounding him, the pilot remained ____, calmly guiding the damaged plane to a safe landing.
gre.clue: calmly guiding the damaged plane

rhapsody.hook: RHAPSODY: Bohemian RHAPSODY — wild, joyful music.
rhapsody.story: Rhapsody. An expression of extreme enthusiasm; also, a free-form piece of music. After her first trip to the mangrove forest, Talia could not stop talking. At dinner she went into a rhapsody about the spotted deer, the silent mangroves at dawn, and a tiger's pawprint she saw in the mud. Her father put down his fork and said he would book the next trip himself. To rhapsodize is to speak with wild delight, like music flowing freely, as in the famous song Bohemian Rhapsody. So, what word names a burst of joyful, enthusiastic praise?... Rhapsody.
rhapsody.example: Her travel blog dissolved into a rhapsody about the tea gardens of Srimangal, with three paragraphs devoted to the morning mist alone.

gre.s: The critic, usually so restrained, launched into a ____ about the young violinist, praising her tone and phrasing in such ecstatic terms that readers were astonished.
gre.clue: in such ecstatic terms

schism.hook: SCHISM (pronounced SIZ-um): a SCISSOR-cut through a group.
schism.story: Schism. A split or division between groups, often over beliefs. Craig's university drama club had been close for years. Then a fierce argument broke out over whether to perform only local plays or translations of Shakespeare too. Friends stopped speaking, and by the end of the year there were two separate clubs rehearsing in different halls. The schism lasted three years, until a new president brought them back together. Schism comes from the Greek for split, and a schism splits a group in two. So, what word names a split within a group over beliefs?... Schism.
schism.example: A schism in the chess club over whether to allow speed games led half its members to start a rival group across town.

gre.s: What began as a minor disagreement over doctrine eventually produced a lasting ____ within the movement, as its followers divided into two hostile camps.
gre.clue: as its followers divided into two hostile camps

sordid.story: Sordid. Morally ignoble or dishonourable; also, dirty and squalid. When a newspaper investigated a factory owner, the details were sordid: unpaid wages, fake safety certificates, and bribes to inspectors so the cracked walls would be ignored. Workers who complained were quietly fired. Meg, a young reporter, felt sick as she typed the story late at night. Sordid comes from the Latin for dirt, and a sordid affair is morally filthy. So, what word describes a scandal that is shameful, dirty and dishonourable?... Sordid.
sordid.example: Journalists spent months tracing the sordid deals through which public land in Dhaka was quietly sold to friends of officials.

gre.s: The memoir, which promised an inspiring tale of artistic triumph, instead revealed a ____ history of bribery, betrayal, and blackmail.
gre.clue: bribery, betrayal, and blackmail

superfluous.story: Superfluous. More than needed; unnecessary. Before his trip to the beach, Zach packed six shirts, three pairs of shoes, a heavy jacket and an umbrella. His sister unpacked half of it. "It is the beach in April," she said, "and the jacket is superfluous." He went with one small bag and never missed a thing. Super means over and fluous means flowing, so superfluous things overflow beyond what you need. So, what word describes something extra and unnecessary?... Superfluous.
superfluous.example: Apologizing again would be superfluous, Mitu decided, since her sister had already forgiven her the night before.

gre.s: The editor cut several paragraphs that she considered ____, since they merely repeated points made earlier in the chapter.
gre.clue: merely repeated points made earlier

tenuous.hook: TENUOUS: as THIN as a thread.
tenuous.story: Tenuous. Very weak or slight. In a storm on the coast, Roger's fishing boat broke loose from the jetty, held only by a thin, fraying rope. He grabbed it just as the last strands began to split. The link was so tenuous that one more wave would have taken the boat. Years later, his son met the word in a GRE passage about a tenuous argument, and he smiled: an argument, like a rope, can hang by a thread. Tenuous comes from the Latin for thin. So, what word describes a link or argument that is very weak?... Tenuous.
tenuous.example: The village's tenuous internet connection dropped every few minutes, making Rakib's online exam a test of patience as much as knowledge.

gre.s: The prosecutor's case rested on a ____ chain of circumstantial evidence, and the defense easily broke it by showing that the key witness had been miles away.
gre.clue: the defense easily broke it

veritable.story: Veritable. Real; used to emphasize that a description is accurate. When Ingrid's grandmother cooked for the holiday, the kitchen became a veritable factory. Three stoves burned at once, pots of biryani and korma bubbled side by side, and four aunts chopped onions in a row. By noon there was food for two hundred guests. Calling it a factory was no exaggeration; it was a veritable one. Veritable comes from veritas, the Latin for truth, as in verify. So, what word means truly deserving a description, real in every sense?... Veritable.
veritable.example: Grandma's kitchen became a veritable factory before Eid, turning out hundreds of pitha for relatives, neighbors, and the night guards.

gre.s: The once-neglected archive has become a ____ goldmine for historians: scholars have already uncovered hundreds of documents previously thought lost.
gre.clue: scholars have already uncovered hundreds of documents previously thought lost

zealous.story: Zealous. Showing great energy and enthusiasm for a cause or goal. Every Saturday, a group of students gathers at the city beach with gloves and sacks to pick up plastic. Their leader, Nadia, arrives first and leaves last, and she has convinced half her university to join. Even in the rain, she sings as she works. Nobody is more zealous about clean beaches. Zealous means full of zeal, which is burning enthusiasm. So, what word describes someone full of eager energy for a cause?... Zealous.
zealous.example: A zealous volunteer, Imran spent every weekend of the dengue season knocking on doors to warn families about standing water.

gre.s: The new inspector was so ____ in enforcing the regulations that he fined shops for violations his predecessors had ignored for years.
gre.clue: fined shops for violations his predecessors had ignored for years

abreast.hook: A-BREAST: chest to chest, side by side, keeping pace.
abreast.story: Abreast. Up to date with the latest news or developments; also, side by side. Every morning, Cole's grandfather reads three newspapers on the veranda with his tea, then listens to the radio news at noon. At eighty, he knows more about world events than his grandsons. He likes to keep abreast of everything. In the evening, the two of them stroll abreast along the river, arguing about politics. Abreast literally means breast to breast, side by side, so keeping abreast of the news means keeping pace with it. So, what word means staying fully up to date?... Abreast.
abreast.example: Farida reads three newspapers on her morning commute to keep abreast of the cricket board's latest selection decisions.

gre.s: Researchers in such a fast-moving field must read constantly to stay ____ of new findings; otherwise their own work can become obsolete within months.
gre.clue: otherwise their own work can become obsolete within months

altruistic.hook: ALTRUISTIC: ALTER (other) + TRUE care for others.
altruistic.story: Altruistic. Showing selfless concern for the well-being of others. Every winter, Mitch's mother collects old blankets from her whole building. She washes them, mends the torn ones, and goes at night to the railway station to give them to people sleeping in the cold. She never posts a photo or tells anyone. Her kindness is purely altruistic. Altruistic comes from the Latin alter, meaning other, as in alternative, so an altruistic person lives for others. So, what word describes kindness that expects nothing in return?... Altruistic.
altruistic.example: Rahim's altruistic decision to donate a kidney to a stranger inspired dozens of people in his neighborhood to register as organ donors.

gre.s: Although the donor claimed his motives were purely ____, critics noted that the gift earned him an enormous tax deduction.
gre.clue: the gift earned him an enormous tax deduction

amorphous.hook: A-MORPH-ous: 'a' means without, 'morph' means shape. Without shape.
amorphous.story: Amorphous. Without a clear shape, form, or structure. At the first meeting of their startup, Frank and his friends talked for three hours about apps, delivery, farming and education, but nobody could say what the business actually was. Their plan was amorphous, like a cloud drifting over the river. Their mentor gave them one week to choose a single idea. A means without and morph means shape, as in morphing, so amorphous means without shape. So, what word describes a plan with no clear form?... Amorphous.
amorphous.example: The protest movement remained amorphous for months, with no leaders, no headquarters, and no agreed list of demands.

gre.s: The committee's proposal remained frustratingly ____: it gestured toward reform but specified no budget, no timeline, and no responsible agency.
gre.clue: specified no budget, no timeline, and no responsible agency

anomalous.story: Anomalous. Deviating from what is normal or expected. Mango trees flower in late winter and give fruit in summer. But one year, Steve's grandfather found a single tree heavy with tiny green mangoes in December. Neighbours came from three villages to see it. A botanist from the university said the anomalous tree may have been confused by unusual weather. An anomaly is something that does not fit the pattern, so anomalous means out of the ordinary. So, what word describes something that breaks from the normal pattern?... Anomalous.
anomalous.example: An anomalous spike in electricity use every midnight led auditors to discover an illegal cryptocurrency mining rig in the basement.

gre.s: Because every other sample showed the same chemical signature, researchers dismissed the one ____ reading as the result of contamination.
gre.clue: every other sample showed the same chemical signature

antithesis.hook: ANTI-THESIS: against the thesis, the exact opposite.
antithesis.story: Antithesis. Something that is the exact reverse of another thing. Sam's two grandmothers could not be more different. One lives in a quiet hill village, rises at dawn, and speaks softly to her plants. The other lives in a busy city flat, stays up late watching cricket, and shouts at every umpire. Each is the antithesis of the other, yet both love Sam fiercely. Anti means against and thesis means a position, so an antithesis stands directly against something. So, what word names the exact opposite of another thing?... Antithesis.
antithesis.example: Shy and soft-spoken, the new captain was the antithesis of his loud predecessor, yet the players responded to him just as well.

gre.s: The minimalist new museum, with its bare white walls and empty spaces, is the ____ of the ornate palace that once stood on the site.
gre.clue: bare white walls and empty spaces

archetype.story: Archetype. The classic example of a type; the original pattern others copy. When people picture an old village schoolteacher, many imagine the same figure: an old man in a white shirt and thick glasses, walking to school with a black umbrella, strict in class but kind afterwards. Sean's grandfather fit that picture exactly. He was the archetype of the village teacher. Arch means first or chief, as in archbishop, so an archetype is the first model that others follow. So, what word names the classic, original example of a type?... Archetype.
archetype.example: For many Bangladeshi readers, Himu has become the archetype of the carefree young man drifting through Dhaka in a yellow panjabi.

gre.s: The scheming stepmother of old folk tales is the ____ from which countless later villains, in novels and films alike, have been copied.
gre.clue: from which countless later villains

audacious.hook: AUDACIOUS: 'AUDACity' — the nerve to do something bold.
audacious.story: Audacious. Showing bold willingness to take risks; daringly bold, sometimes rude. At nineteen, Leah walked into the office of a famous city fashion designer without an appointment, laid her sketches on his desk, and offered to work for free for one month to prove herself. The receptionist froze. The designer stared, then smiled, and hired her that afternoon. It was an audacious move. Audacious comes from the Latin for dare, the same root as audacity, the nerve to try something bold. So, what word describes a daringly bold act?... Audacious.
audacious.example: In an audacious move, the chess prodigy sacrificed her queen in the opening, a gamble that stunned the grandmaster across the board.

gre.s: The startup's ____ plan to compete directly with three established giants struck investors as either visionary or reckless.
gre.clue: either visionary or reckless

censure.hook: CENSURE: like a CENSOR, it officially condemns what you did.
censure.story: Censure. To criticize someone strongly and officially; also, such official criticism. A young doctor in a northern town discovered that her hospital's director had been selling free government medicines. She reported it. After an inquiry, the health ministry formally censured the director and removed him from his post. The public censure made front-page news, and the doctor received hundreds of letters of thanks. Do not confuse censure with censor: a censor cuts words out, but censure is official blame. So, what word means to criticize someone strongly and officially?... Censure.
censure.example: Parliament censured the minister after an inquiry found he had hidden the true cost of the bridge from lawmakers.

gre.s: The medical board voted to ____ the surgeon for his reckless conduct, though it stopped short of revoking his license.
gre.clue: his reckless conduct

deference.hook: DEFERENCE: you DEFER, or step aside, out of respect.
deference.story: Deference. Polite submission and respect for another's opinion or authority. At a family meeting about a cousin's wedding, everyone had an opinion, and the voices grew loud. Then Josh's grandfather cleared his throat. The room went quiet at once, and even the eldest uncle lowered his eyes and waited. Out of deference, nobody spoke until the old man had finished. Deference comes from defer, to step aside and let someone else go first. So, what word names the respect that makes you yield to an elder's view?... Deference.
deference.example: In deference to her grandfather's wishes, Labiba held her wedding in the family's village home rather than a Dhaka convention hall.

gre.s: Out of ____ to the senior surgeon, the young resident kept her doubts to herself, a silence she later regretted.
gre.clue: kept her doubts to herself

discernible.hook: DISCERN = to see clearly. DISCERNIBLE = can be seen.
discernible.story: Discernible. Able to be noticed or understood, though perhaps with difficulty. Far out in the Bay of Bengal, Rex's fishing boat had been at sea for six days. Through the morning haze, a thin grey line was barely discernible on the horizon. Slowly it grew into palm trees and the coast of a small island. Rex smiled and called to the crew. Home was clearly discernible at last. To discern is to see clearly, so something discernible can just be seen. So, what word describes something you can just make out, though with difficulty?... Discernible.
discernible.example: By the third week of the new diet, there was a discernible improvement in his blood pressure, though he still felt tired.

gre.s: Although the forgery fooled most experts, a faint but ____ difference in the brushwork eventually gave it away.
gre.clue: eventually gave it away

disconcerting.hook: DIS-CONCERT-ING: throws the CONCERT out of tune.
disconcerting.story: Disconcerting. Causing one to feel unsettled or uneasy. In the middle of her job interview, Nadia noticed that one interviewer had not looked up once. He kept writing and never nodded or smiled, even at her best answers. It was disconcerting, and she lost her place twice. Later she learned that he took detailed notes for everyone. To disconcert is to throw things out of concert, out of harmony, so something disconcerting knocks your calm out of tune. So, what word describes something that leaves you feeling unsettled?... Disconcerting.
disconcerting.example: It was disconcerting to hear my own voice played back on the radio, slightly higher and faster than I had imagined it.

gre.s: Audiences found the film's abrupt shifts in tone ____: scenes of broad slapstick gave way, without warning, to moments of genuine brutality.
gre.clue: gave way, without warning, to moments of genuine brutality

disingenuous.story: Disingenuous. Not sincere; pretending to know less than one does. When Pam moved out of her flat, she asked the landlord for her deposit. He looked puzzled and said, "Which deposit? I never knew about any deposit." But Pam had his signed receipt in her bag. His puzzled face was completely disingenuous. She calmly took out the receipt, and his memory returned at once. Ingenuous means innocent and frank, and dis means not, so a disingenuous person only pretends to be innocent. So, what word describes fake innocence, pretending not to know?... Disingenuous.
disingenuous.example: Calling the fee hike a 'small adjustment' was disingenuous, since tuition at the private university rose by nearly forty percent.

gre.s: It is ____ of the company to claim it was unaware of the defect, since internal emails show executives discussed it for months.
gre.clue: internal emails show executives discussed it for months

divulge.hook: DIVULGE: DIVE into the secrets and BULGE them out.
divulge.story: Divulge. To tell something that was meant to stay private. For weeks, Tori's family planned a surprise party for her father's sixtieth birthday, and everyone promised to keep it secret. Then, at dinner, her little cousin blurted out, "Is the cake chocolate or vanilla?" The secret was out. Her father promised to act surprised anyway. The cousin had divulged everything. The root vulg comes from the Latin for common people, as in vulgar, so to divulge is to make a secret common knowledge. So, what verb means to reveal a private secret?... Divulge.
divulge.example: Even after ten years, my aunt refuses to divulge the secret ingredient that makes her mutton curry so famous at family weddings.

gre.s: The journalist went to prison rather than ____ the identity of her source.
gre.clue: went to prison rather than

dogged.hook: DOGGED: like a DOG holding a bone, refusing to let go.
dogged.story: Dogged. Refusing to give up, even when progress is slow or hard. Ron failed his driving test three times. The examiner frowned at his parking, his turns, his nervous hands. Each time, Ron went home, practised in an empty field at dawn, and booked the test again. On the fourth try he passed, and the examiner shook his hand. His dogged effort had paid off. Picture a dog holding a bone and refusing to let go: that is dogged determination. So, what word describes stubborn, never-give-up persistence?... Dogged.
dogged.example: Through dogged practice every dawn on the Rajshahi riverbank, the young sprinter shaved a full second off her best time.

gre.s: Thanks to her ____ persistence, the reporter eventually uncovered the scandal that others had abandoned after a few weeks.
gre.clue: that others had abandoned after a few weeks

elated.story: Elated. Ecstatically happy. When the university admission results came out, Amy's father stood in the crowd outside the gate, running his finger down the long list. Then he found her name. He shouted, hugged a complete stranger, and called every relative in the village, one after another. Amy had never seen him so elated, and she was elated too. Elated comes from the Latin for lifted up, and an elated person feels lifted high with joy. So, what word describes someone ecstatically happy?... Elated.
elated.example: The astronomers were elated when the telescope finally captured a clear image of the comet they had tracked for six years.

gre.s: The team was ____ after the unexpected victory, celebrating late into the night in the streets of their small town.
gre.clue: celebrating late into the night

empathetic.hook: EMPATHETIC: feeling IN (em) someone else's pain (pathos).
empathetic.story: Empathetic. Able to understand and share the feelings of others. When Zane failed his first semester exam, he sat alone in the dorm canteen, too ashamed to call home. His roommate Ivan did not lecture him. He sat down, ordered two cups of tea, and said quietly that he had failed a course in his first year too. For the first time that week, Zane felt understood. Ivan was deeply empathetic. Em means in, and path means feeling, as in sympathy, so an empathetic person feels from inside someone else's heart. So, what word describes someone who truly shares your feelings?... Empathetic.
empathetic.example: An empathetic coach, Sharmin noticed whenever a player was struggling at home and quietly lightened her training load.

gre.s: The best nurses are not only technically skilled but also ____, able to sense a frightened patient's anxiety and respond to it before a word is spoken.
gre.clue: able to sense a frightened patient's anxiety

exacting.hook: EXACTING: demands everything to be EXACT.
exacting.story: Exacting. Making great demands on skill, attention, or effort. Joanna learned classical songs from an old teacher who was famously exacting. Every note had to be perfect, every word clear, every breath in the right place. One small slip, and Joanna sang the whole song again. It was exhausting, but after five years, Joanna sang on national television. Exacting comes from exact: an exacting teacher demands that everything be exact. So, what word describes a task or a person that demands great care and effort?... Exacting.
exacting.example: Restoring the old Armenian church in Dhaka was exacting work, as each cracked tile had to be matched by hand to the original.

gre.s: The surgeon's ____ standards, which allowed no margin for error, made her residency program one of the most demanding in the country.
gre.clue: which allowed no margin for error

exasperated.hook: EXASPERATED: EX-ASP, bitten by a snake of annoyance.
exasperated.story: Exasperated. Intensely irritated and frustrated. Sandy had called the internet company six times in two days. Each time, a recorded voice told her to press one, then two, then wait, and then the line went dead. On the seventh call, with her online class starting in ten minutes, she threw the phone onto the bed, completely exasperated. The root asper is Latin for rough, so exasperated means rubbed rough, like nerves scraped raw. So, what word describes someone pushed to the edge of their patience?... Exasperated.
exasperated.example: Exasperated by the endless traffic jams on Mirpur Road, Kamal finally bought a bicycle and began riding to his office.

gre.s: After the airline cancelled his flight for the third time in a week, the ____ traveler finally gave up and rented a car.
gre.clue: for the third time in a week

fanciful.story: Fanciful. Imaginative but unrealistic. When Russell was eight, he told his friends that a giant catfish lived at the bottom of the village pond and came up only on full-moon nights to eat mangoes. His friends believed him for a whole summer. His mother called it one of his fanciful stories. Today Russell writes children's books, and his tales are still wonderfully fanciful. Fanciful simply means full of fancy, which is imagination. So, what word describes an idea that is imaginative but not realistic?... Fanciful.
fanciful.example: Most engineers thought his scheme of floating solar farms on every village pond was fanciful, until a pilot project actually worked.

gre.s: The historian dismissed the legend as ____, pointing out that no record from the period mentions a sea monster at all.
gre.clue: no record from the period mentions

gratuitous.hook: GRATUITOUS: like a GRATUITY (tip), extra and not required.
gratuitous.story: Gratuitous. Unnecessary and unjustified; also, given free of charge. Shelly watched a new action film with her family one Friday evening. The story was moving, but every few minutes a loud, bloody fight broke out that had nothing to do with the plot. Her father shook his head at all the gratuitous violence. Gratuitous comes from the same root as gratuity, a tip given freely without being required, so gratuitous things are extra, added for no good reason. So, what word describes something added without any good reason?... Gratuitous.
gratuitous.example: The coach's gratuitous insults after the defeat hurt the young players far more than the scoreline itself.

gre.s: The reviewer's remarks about the author's appearance were entirely ____: they had no bearing on the quality of the novel and served only to humiliate her.
gre.clue: had no bearing on the quality of the novel

idiosyncratic.hook: IDIO-SYNCRATIC: IDIO means one's own (as in idiom).
idiosyncratic.story: Idiosyncratic. Peculiar to an individual; distinctive and unusual. Toby's chemistry professor wore the same blue sweater even in the June heat, drank tea only from a steel glass, and began every lecture by quoting a line of an old folk song. His students found these habits idiosyncratic, but they loved him for them, and they still copy his quotes today. Idio means one's own, as in idiom, so an idiosyncratic habit belongs to one person alone. So, what word describes a habit that is strange and peculiar to one person?... Idiosyncratic.
idiosyncratic.example: The professor's idiosyncratic grading system awarded extra marks for the questions students asked rather than the answers they gave.

gre.s: The novelist's spelling and punctuation are so ____ that editors hesitate to correct them, fearing they would erase the very quirks that make her voice unmistakable.
gre.clue: the very quirks that make her voice unmistakable

monotonous.hook: MONO-TONE: one tone, over and over.
monotonous.story: Monotonous. Dull and tedious because of lack of variety. In a big garment factory, Rita sews the same pocket onto the same shirt, hundreds of times a day, to the same hum of machines. The work is monotonous, and the hours are long. But every evening she studies English from a small book, dreaming of a different job. Mono means one and tone means sound, so monotonous means one tone, over and over. So, what word describes work that is dull because it never changes?... Monotonous.
monotonous.example: The lecturer's monotonous voice, never rising or falling, sent half the back row to sleep before the tea break.

gre.s: The ____ landscape, mile after mile of identical wheat fields, made the long drive feel endless.
gre.clue: mile after mile of identical wheat fields

oust.story: Oust. To force someone out of a position or place. For ten years, the same man ran the market traders' association in town, collecting fees and doing very little. At last the small shopkeepers called a vote. Almost every hand went up. They ousted him and elected a young vegetable seller named Sally, and the traders cheered as she took the chair. Oust sounds like out, and to oust someone is to push them out. So, what verb means to force someone out of power?... Oust.
oust.example: Shareholders voted to oust the chief executive after the company lost a third of its value in a single year.

gre.s: The rebels' attempt to ____ the dictator failed when the army remained loyal to him.
gre.clue: when the army remained loyal to him

reproach.hook: REPROACH: re-APPROACH someone to tell them they disappointed you.
reproach.story: Reproach. To tell someone you are disappointed by what they did; also, such criticism. Shane came home at two in the morning, after promising to be back by ten. His mother was waiting on the sofa. She did not shout. She only said softly that she had kept his rice warm for four hours. That gentle reproach hurt more than any scolding, and he never came home late again without calling. Hear approach inside reproach: you approach someone to show how they let you down. So, what word names a quiet criticism that shows disappointment?... Reproach.
