When the new factory manager arrived at the plant, he snapped his fingers at workers, demanded tea without ever saying please, and never learned anyone's name. "Do it now" was his favourite sentence. Barry, a supervisor of twenty years, found his imperious tone hard to bear. Imperious shares a root with empire and emperor: an imperious person gives orders like an emperor. So, what word describes someone who orders others around as if they were royalty?... Imperious.
imperious.example: The new manager's imperious emails, full of commands and deadlines but never a single please, soon drove two engineers to resign.

gre.s: The duchess dismissed the servants with an ____ wave of her hand, never deigning to look at them.
gre.clue: never deigning to look at them

judicious.story: Judicious. Having or showing good judgment. When Nicole's family argued about whether to sell their land in the village or keep it, voices rose and tempers flared. Nicole's mother listened quietly to everyone. Then she suggested selling half and keeping half, so the family could pay its debts and still keep a home to return to. One by one, everyone agreed. It was a judicious decision. Judicious is linked to judge: a judicious person weighs things like a wise judge. So, what word means showing wise and careful judgment?... Judicious.
judicious.example: A judicious use of colour, just one red chair in an otherwise grey room, made the small apartment feel striking.

gre.s: With only limited funds available, the museum made a ____ decision to repair its roof before purchasing any new artworks.
gre.clue: repair its roof before purchasing any new artworks

laudable.story: Laudable. Worthy of praise and admiration. Every Friday, Ross, a small-town college student, spends his only day off teaching street children to read under a tree near the railway station. He buys the chalk and notebooks with his own pocket money. When a local newspaper wrote about him, it called his effort laudable, and three more volunteers joined him the next week. To laud means to praise, so laudable means worthy of praise; on diplomas, cum laude means with praise. So, what word describes an action that deserves praise?... Laudable.
laudable.example: The club's laudable plan to plant a tree for every goal scored this season has already greened three school playgrounds.

gre.s: Although the program's goals were ____, its execution was so poor that it ultimately did more harm than good.
gre.clue: its execution was so poor

ostentatious.hook: OSTENTATIOUS: 'OSTEN-TATIOUS', 'Look at me, look at my stuff!'
ostentatious.story: Ostentatious. Flashy and meant to show off wealth or importance. When a businessman's son got married in the city, the guests arrived to find a line of white cars, a chocolate fountain, and a stage covered in thousands of imported roses. The groom rode in on a decorated horse, followed by a brass band. Mandy whispered to her friend that it was all rather ostentatious. Ostentatious comes from the Latin for showing off, and ostentatious things seem to shout, look at me. So, what word describes a display that is flashy and showy?... Ostentatious.
ostentatious.example: The minister's ostentatious motorcade of twenty cars jammed Mirpur Road for an hour during the morning rush.

gre.s: Though enormously wealthy, the philanthropist lived without ____ display, driving an old car and living in a modest house.
gre.clue: driving an old car and living in a modest house

panache.hook: PANACHE: originally a feather plume on a knight's helmet. Pure style.
panache.story: Panache. Flamboyant confidence and stylish flair. At the university cultural night, Adam walked onto the stage in a bright yellow suit, bowed with a sweep of his arm, and sang an old folk song as if the whole auditorium belonged to him. He even winked at the front row. The students cheered for five minutes. He sang with real panache. Panache was once the feather plume on a knight's helmet; a person with panache wears confidence like that bright plume. So, what word means confident, stylish flair?... Panache.
panache.example: The goalkeeper saved the last penalty with real panache, diving full length and springing up at once to salute the crowd.

gre.s: The chef plated each dish with such ____, flambéing desserts at the table with a theatrical flourish, that diners often applauded.
gre.clue: with a theatrical flourish

pedantic.hook: PEDANTIC: a PEDAL-pushing professor who corrects every tiny thing.
pedantic.story: Pedantic. Overly concerned with minor details or rules; showing off learning. When Chelsea told a story about her trip to the hills, her cousin kept interrupting. "Actually, it was not three hours, it was two hours and fifty minutes." "Actually, that hill is not a mountain." By the end, nobody wanted to hear about the trip. His pedantic corrections had killed the story. A pedant was once a schoolmaster, and a pedantic person still corrects everyone like a fussy teacher. So, what word describes someone obsessed with tiny details?... Pedantic.
pedantic.example: The editor's pedantic notes on comma placement filled the margins, yet she said nothing about the plot's glaring holes.

gre.s: Students found the lecturer ____, as he would interrupt a lively discussion to correct a trivial grammatical error.
gre.clue: interrupt a lively discussion to correct a trivial grammatical error

prescient.story: Prescient. Having knowledge of events before they happen. One April, Sam's grandmother watched the sky and the ants carrying food up the walls and said, "The floods will come early this year. Move the rice up to the loft." Everyone smiled at her. In June, the water rose weeks early, and theirs was the only rice in the village that stayed dry. Her warning had been prescient. Pre means before and scient means knowing, as in science: prescient means knowing beforehand. So, what word describes someone who foresees the future accurately?... Prescient.
prescient.example: In 1965, Gordon Moore made the prescient forecast that the number of transistors on a chip would keep doubling.

gre.s: The novel now seems remarkably ____, having described smartphones and social media decades before either existed.
gre.clue: decades before either existed

quibble.hook: QUIBBLE: a small QUIBBLE, like a QUIBBLING nibble.
quibble.story: Quibble. To argue about trivial matters; also, a minor objection. Bella and her brother had planned a family trip to the hills for weeks. But on the night before, they spent an hour quibbling over who would sit by the window on the train. Their father finally said, "You will take turns. One more quibble and we all stay home." Silence fell at once. Quibble rhymes with nibble: small nibbles at an argument instead of a real bite. So, what verb means to argue over small, unimportant things?... Quibble.
quibble.example: The two professors quibbled for an hour over whether the manuscript dated from 1802 or 1803.

gre.s: The reviewer admired the novel's ambition and its vivid characters; her only ____ concerned a handful of typographical errors that hardly diminished its power.
gre.clue: that hardly diminished its power

shirk.hook: SHIRK: like a SHARK swimming away from work.
shirk.story: Shirk. To deliberately dodge work or a duty you should do. Toby was part of a group project on river pollution. While his three teammates collected water samples from the city river in the heat, he always had an excuse: a headache, a cousin's wedding, a broken phone. On presentation day, he tried to take the credit. The teacher, who had seen everything, gave him a lower mark for shirking his duties. Shirk sounds like shark: picture a lazy shark slipping away whenever there is work to do. So, what verb means to dodge a responsibility?... Shirk.
shirk.example: Soldiers who shirked guard duty during the campaign were ordered to dig latrines for a week as punishment.

gre.s: Unlike her predecessor, who tended to ____ difficult decisions by delegating them to committees, the new director confronted every problem personally.
gre.clue: by delegating them to committees

supersede.hook: SUPER-SEDE: sits (sede) above, takes the top seat.
supersede.story: Supersede. To replace something older or less effective. Mia's grandfather kept a heavy black telephone with a turning dial on his desk for thirty years. When the family gave him a smartphone, he grumbled at first, then discovered video calls with his granddaughter in Canada. The new phone soon superseded the old one, though he kept it on his desk for memory's sake. Super means above and sede means sit: whatever supersedes the old thing takes the higher seat. So, what verb means to replace something older?... Supersede.
supersede.example: The 2024 building code supersedes all earlier guidelines, so builders in Chattogram must now follow its stricter fire rules.

gre.s: Most experts expect electric vehicles to eventually ____ gasoline-powered cars, just as cars once replaced horse-drawn carriages.
gre.clue: just as cars once replaced horse-drawn carriages

swindle.hook: SWINDLE: like a WINDOW that's actually a painting, a trick.
swindle.story: Swindle. To cheat someone out of money; a fraud. A man knocked on Shane's grandmother's door, claiming he could double her savings in a month through a special scheme. He showed shiny papers and an official-looking card. Luckily, Shane arrived, checked the man's name online, and found he had already swindled twenty families in the town. The police were called. Swindle sounds like dwindle: when someone swindles you, your money dwindles to nothing. So, what verb means to cheat someone out of money?... Swindle.
swindle.example: Online scammers swindled a retired schoolteacher in Rajshahi by posing as bank officers and asking for her PIN.

gre.s: The so-called investment firm existed only to ____ elderly retirees, promising guaranteed returns before disappearing with their life savings.
gre.clue: disappearing with their life savings

terse.hook: TERSE: TERSE is a terse word, just five letters.
terse.story: Terse. Using few words; abrupt. Dina sent her boss a long, careful email explaining why the report would be two days late, with three apologies and a new plan. His reply came back in one word: "Fine." She stared at it for a full minute, unsure whether he was angry. Later she learned that every email he wrote was that terse. Terse once meant wiped clean and polished; a terse reply is wiped clean of every extra word. So, what word describes a reply that is short and curt?... Terse.
terse.example: Asked about the defeat, the coach gave a terse answer, 'We played badly,' and walked straight out of the press room.

gre.s: Expecting a warm thank-you for her months of work, the volunteer was stung by the director's ____ reply, which consisted of a single, unsigned line.
gre.clue: which consisted of a single, unsigned line

transitory.story: Transitory. Not permanent; lasting a short time. Every spring, the silk cotton trees along Morgan's village road burst into red blossoms. For two weeks the road looks as if it is on fire, and children collect the fallen flowers in their laps. Then the petals drop, and the trees turn plain and green again. His mother says beauty is always transitory. Transitory is related to transit: something transitory is just passing through. So, what word describes something brief and temporary?... Transitory.
transitory.example: Fame on social media is often transitory, as last month's viral singer from Khulna has already discovered.

gre.s: The economic boom proved ____: within two years, the new factories had closed and unemployment had returned to its former levels.
gre.clue: within two years, the new factories had closed

trifling.story: Trifling. Unimportant or trivial. Two brothers in Paula's neighbourhood stopped speaking for a year over a trifling matter: who had broken a plastic chair at a family picnic. The chair cost five dollars. When their mother finally sat them down, both were embarrassed by how trifling it seemed. They bought a new chair together that same afternoon. A trifle is a small thing of little value, and trifling describes anything that small. So, what word describes a matter too minor to fight over?... Trifling.
trifling.example: Compared with the cost of rebuilding the bridge, the repair bill seemed trifling, so the council approved it at once.

gre.s: Although the fine was ____, a mere ten dollars, the principle at stake led the activist to appeal all the way to the supreme court.
gre.clue: a mere ten dollars

unseemly.story: Unseemly. Not proper or appropriate; in bad taste. At a quiet prayer gathering after a neighbour's death, Tristan was shocked to see two guests arguing loudly about a land deal in the courtyard. Heads turned, the women inside fell silent, and an elder walked over to stop them. Shouting about money at such a time was deeply unseemly. Seemly is an old word for fitting and proper, so unseemly means not fitting the occasion. So, what word describes behaviour that is improper for the occasion?... Unseemly.
unseemly.example: Cheering loudly in the hospital corridor seemed unseemly to the nurses, even though the family had just heard good news.

gre.s: Many guests found the candidate's lavish victory party ____, since it took place just hours after deadly floods had devastated the region.
gre.clue: just hours after deadly floods had devastated the region

vivacious.story: Vivacious. Lively and full of energy, especially in personality. When Nadia joined the office, the quiet floor changed almost overnight. She learned everyone's name in a day, brought homemade cookies on Thursdays, and laughed so brightly that even the stern accountant smiled. Her vivacious spirit made Mondays bearable. Vivacious comes from the Latin vivere, to live, as in vivid and survive: a vivacious person is full of life. So, what word describes someone lively and spirited?... Vivacious.
vivacious.example: The vivacious tour guide kept forty tired schoolchildren laughing all the way around Lalbagh Fort.

gre.s: Unlike her reserved older sister, Shathi was ____, filling every room with laughter and chatter from the moment she arrived.
gre.clue: Unlike her reserved older sister

woeful.story: Woeful. Full of sorrow; very bad or deplorable. Kirk's college cricket team had practised for months, but in the final they were all out for thirty-one runs in just ten overs. The coach called it a woeful performance. Kirk himself looked woeful all evening, kicking stones on the long walk home while his friends stayed silent. Woeful simply means full of woe, and woe is deep sorrow. So, what word describes a performance that is shockingly bad?... Woeful.
woeful.example: The team's woeful defending allowed their opponents to score four goals in the first half alone.

gre.s: Although the school boasted of its modern facilities, inspectors found its science laboratories in ____ condition, with broken equipment and no working gas supply.
gre.clue: with broken equipment and no working gas supply

abhor.hook: AB-HOR: so HORrible that you back AWAY from it.
abhor.story: Abhor. To hate something deeply and find it disgusting. Ruby's grandfather was a gentle man who rarely raised his voice, but he abhorred cruelty to animals. When he saw boys throwing stones at a stray dog outside the town market, he marched over, took the stones from their hands, and made them bring the dog water. "I abhor cruelty," he told Ruby later. Abhor shares its Latin root with horror: you shudder and pull back from what you abhor. So, what verb means to hate something with disgust?... Abhor.
abhor.example: Akash abhors waste, so he carries leftover rice from every family feast to the night guards on his street.

gre.s: Although the novelist claimed to ____ violence, critics noted that her books dwell on it in loving, almost gleeful detail.
gre.clue: dwell on it in loving, almost gleeful detail

aghast.hook: AGHAST: as if you've seen a GHOST.
aghast.story: Aghast. Filled with horror or shock. When Ian opened his electricity bill one month, he was aghast. Instead of the usual eighty dollars, it said eight thousand. His mother sat down on the sofa, pale. The next morning he rushed to the office, where a clerk checked the meter and found a typing mistake: two extra zeros. Ian walked out grinning, no longer aghast. Hear ghost inside aghast: you look as if you have just seen a ghost. So, what word describes someone frozen with shock or horror?... Aghast.
aghast.example: The curator was aghast to learn that a cleaner had scrubbed the ancient paint off a priceless statue.

gre.s: Far from welcoming the proposal, the residents were ____ when they learned that the new highway would demolish the town's historic library and its surrounding park.
gre.clue: would demolish the town's historic library

agitate.hook: AGITATE: like a washing machine's AGITATOR, stirring things up.
agitate.story: Agitate. To make someone troubled or nervous; to campaign to arouse public concern. News that the river embankment near their village was cracking agitated Sydney's whole family. Her mother could not sleep. Then the villagers, led by a young teacher, began to agitate for repairs, marching to the district office every week with banners. After two months, workers finally arrived with sandbags. Think of the agitator in a washing machine, stirring the clothes around; to agitate is to stir people up. So, what verb means to stir up worry or public protest?... Agitate.
agitate.example: Loud thunder tends to agitate our old dog, who hides under the bed until the storm has passed.

gre.s: The doctor warned visitors not to ____ the patient with distressing news, since even mild anxiety might strain her weakened heart.
gre.clue: since even mild anxiety might strain her weakened heart

assuage.hook: ASSUAGE sounds like 'a massage': it soothes the pain.
assuage.story: Assuage. To make an unpleasant feeling less intense; to satisfy a need. Noah came home from his first day at a new school feeling lonely and homesick. His grandmother said nothing at first. She simply set down a warm bowl of rice with a fried egg and sat beside him while he ate. Slowly, his sadness eased. Her quiet company assuaged his loneliness, and the food assuaged his hunger. Assuage comes from the Latin for sweet, as in suave: to assuage pain is to sweeten it. So, what verb means to soothe a painful feeling?... Assuage.
assuage.example: A cup of sweet tea and a long chat with her aunt helped assuage Rima's worries about starting university in Sylhet.

gre.s: The airline offered free hotel rooms and meals in an attempt to ____ the anger of passengers stranded by the cancellation.
gre.clue: in an attempt to

bombastic.hook: BOMBASTIC: words that sound like a BOMB but carry nothing.
bombastic.story: Bombastic. Using pompous, inflated language with little meaning. At a small-town election rally, a candidate shouted into the microphone for an hour. He promised to turn the town into a golden paradise, to make every road shine like a mirror, and to lift the people to the stars. Felicity, standing at the back, whispered that he had not mentioned a single real plan. It was a bombastic speech. Bombast was once the cotton stuffing used to pad clothes; bombastic language is padded and puffed up. So, what word describes pompous, empty talk?... Bombastic.
bombastic.example: The student's bombastic essay used words like transcendent and epochal to describe an ordinary weekend picnic.

gre.s: Reviewers mocked the memoir's ____ prose, in which even a trip to the grocery store became an epic struggle described in grandiose, ornate language.
gre.clue: described in grandiose, ornate language

coalesce.hook: CO-ALESCE: COAL pieces fusing together in heat into one lump.
coalesce.story: Coalesce. To come together and form a single group or mass. After the floods in the hills, students from different universities began posting offers of help online. One group collected clothes, another bought rice, and a third found boats. Within a week, these small efforts coalesced into one large relief team of five hundred volunteers, led by a student named Brian. Co means together, and the Latin alescere means to grow: when things coalesce, they grow together into one. So, what verb means to merge into a single whole?... Coalesce.
coalesce.example: As the young solar system cooled, tiny grains of dust coalesced into rocks and, eventually, into the first planets.

gre.s: Over several centuries, the scattered tribes began to ____ into a single kingdom with a shared language and a common law.
gre.clue: into a single kingdom

convalescent.hook: CONVALESCENT: gaining back VALOR (strength) after illness.
convalescent.story: Convalescent. Recovering from illness. After a bad case of dengue, Marcus spent three weeks as a convalescent in his grandmother's village. He sat under the mango tree every morning, drank fresh coconut water, and took slow walks around the pond. Each day his legs felt a little stronger, and his appetite slowly returned. Con means fully, and the Latin valescere means to grow strong, as in valiant: a convalescent person is growing strong again. So, what word describes someone slowly recovering after an illness?... Convalescent.
convalescent.example: Convalescent soldiers in the old military hospital spent their afternoons playing chess on the sunny veranda.

gre.s: Though no longer in any danger, the ____ patient was still too weak to climb stairs, and her doctors advised another month of rest at home.
gre.clue: Though no longer in any danger

corporeal.story: Corporeal. Relating to the physical body; material rather than spiritual. Ruby's grandmother, a devout woman, often told her that the body is only a temporary house. "Food, clothes and money are corporeal needs," she said, folding her prayer mat. "The soul needs other things: kindness, prayer, patience." Ruby thought about that for a long time. Hunger is corporeal; hope is not. Corporeal comes from the Latin corpus, body, as in corpse and corporation, a body of people. So, what word describes things that belong to the physical body rather than the spirit?... Corporeal.
corporeal.example: Descartes argued that the mind is distinct from our corporeal existence and could, in principle, survive without it.

gre.s: The monks believed that ____ pleasures such as food and comfort were mere distractions; only by disciplining the body could they attend to the needs of the soul.
gre.clue: only by disciplining the body

decry.story: Decry. To publicly denounce or strongly criticise. When a developer began cutting down the old rain trees along a shady city road to widen it, citizens gathered with placards. Writers decried the plan in newspapers, students sang protest songs under the remaining trees, and Sherman, a retired teacher, decried it on television, his voice shaking. De means down, and cry means to call out: to decry something is to cry it down in public. So, what verb means to criticise something strongly in public?... Decry.
decry.example: Doctors in Dhaka have long decried the sale of antibiotics without prescriptions at neighbourhood pharmacies.

gre.s: Although the minister hailed the new law as a triumph for free speech, journalists were quick to ____ it as a thinly disguised tool of censorship.
gre.clue: a thinly disguised tool of censorship

dutiful.story: Dutiful. Conscientiously fulfilling one's duties. Every evening for six years, Tara has gone straight from her office to her father's bedside after his stroke. She measures his medicine, reads him the newspaper, and helps him with his exercises. Her friends say she is the most dutiful daughter they know. Tara just smiles and says she is giving back what he once gave her. Dutiful simply means full of duty, and a dutiful person carries that duty gladly. So, what word describes someone who faithfully does what they should?... Dutiful.
dutiful.example: Each morning the dutiful night watchman wrote a neat report in the logbook, even when nothing at all had happened.

gre.s: A ____ civil servant, she never missed a deadline in thirty years, though colleagues noted that she seemed to take little pleasure in her work.
gre.clue: never missed a deadline in thirty years

engender.hook: EN-GENDER: GENerates, GENes, birth. It gives birth to something.
engender.story: Engender. To cause or give rise to a feeling or situation. When the new principal of Rita's school began greeting every student at the gate by name, something changed. Children who had once arrived late now came early. Teachers smiled more. Her small daily kindness engendered a warmth that spread through the whole school. Engender shares the root gen, meaning birth, with generate and genes: to engender is to give birth to something. So, what verb means to cause a feeling or condition to arise?... Engender.
engender.example: The coach's habit of praising only the star players engendered resentment among the rest of the squad.

gre.s: Secretive layoffs, announced without explanation, inevitably ____ distrust among the employees who remain.
gre.clue: announced without explanation

exonerate.hook: EX-ONERATE: remove the ONUS (burden) of guilt.
exonerate.story: Exonerate. To officially clear someone from blame. When a gold necklace disappeared from a wedding house, the guests began whispering about Sean, a young cook. Sean kept working in silence, his eyes red. Then the bride's cousin found the necklace caught in the folds of a sari in the dressing room. The family publicly exonerated Sean and apologised to him. Ex means out, and onus means burden: to exonerate is to lift the burden of blame off someone. So, what verb means to clear someone of an accusation?... Exonerate.
exonerate.example: Historians later exonerated the admiral, showing that the fleet sank because of a sudden storm rather than his orders.

gre.s: The new DNA evidence did more than cast doubt on his conviction; it served to ____ him entirely, and the court ordered his release that same afternoon.
gre.clue: the court ordered his release that same afternoon

fallacious.hook: FALLACIOUS: built on a FALLACY, so it FALLS apart.
fallacious.story: Fallacious. Built on faulty logic or a false belief. Andrea's uncle insisted that because he had ridden his motorbike without a helmet for twenty years and never been hurt, helmets must be useless. Andrea, a medical student, gently explained that his argument was fallacious: one lucky man proves nothing about the thousands injured every year. Her uncle grumbled but had no answer. Fallacious comes from fallacy, a mistake in reasoning; a fallacious argument falls apart under a careful look. So, what word describes an argument built on faulty logic?... Fallacious.
fallacious.example: It is fallacious to assume that a medicine must be safe simply because it is made from herbs.

gre.s: The report's conclusion was ____, since it assumed that because two events occurred together, one must have caused the other.
gre.clue: assumed that because two events occurred together, one must have caused the other

fastidious.hook: FASTIDIOUS: FAST to notice every tiny flaw.
fastidious.story: Fastidious. Very attentive to detail; very concerned about accuracy and cleanliness; hard to please. Fred's roommate in the dorm was fastidious. He folded his shirts by colour, wiped his plate twice before eating, and once spent twenty minutes straightening the books on his shelf. When Fred left a single sock on the floor, he found it washed, folded and placed on his pillow. Fastidious comes from a Latin word for disgust: a fastidious person is quickly disgusted by any mess or mistake. So, what word describes someone extremely careful about detail and cleanliness?... Fastidious.
fastidious.example: The fastidious watchmaker in Old Dhaka spent an hour adjusting a single spring before he would return the clock.

gre.s: The ____ editor rejected the manuscript three times over minor inconsistencies in punctuation that most readers would never notice.
gre.clue: minor inconsistencies in punctuation that most readers would never notice

forestall.hook: FORE-STALL: act BEFOREhand to STALL it.
forestall.story: Forestall. To prevent or hinder something by acting in advance. Every year, before the monsoon, Natalie's father climbs onto their tin roof and checks every nail and seam. He seals the small holes with tar long before the first storm. By acting early, he forestalls the leaks that soak his neighbours' homes each July. Fore means before, as in forecast: to forestall a problem is to stop it before it arrives. So, what verb means to prevent something by acting ahead of time?... Forestall.
forestall.example: To forestall a rush at the counters, the stadium opened its online ticket sales a full week early.

gre.s: The company hoped to ____ a hostile takeover by buying back its own shares before the rival bid could be launched.
gre.clue: before the rival bid could be launched

glib.hook: GLIB: GLIdes off the tongue too easily.
glib.story: Glib. Fluent and smooth but insincere or shallow. When a new bridge in Owen's town cracked after only two years, the contractor appeared on television. He smiled, spoke quickly, and said that such things happen and everything would be fine. His answers were smooth, but none of them explained anything. Owen's mother shook her head at the glib reply. Glib sounds like glide: glib words glide off the tongue too easily, with no weight behind them. So, what word describes a quick, smooth answer that lacks sincerity?... Glib.
glib.example: The tutor warned that glib answers about poverty would not impress the examiners, who wanted evidence and careful argument.

gre.s: The spokesman's ____ answers, delivered smoothly and without a moment's hesitation, did little to reassure families who wanted a genuine explanation of the factory fire.
gre.clue: who wanted a genuine explanation

gloat.hook: GLOAT: like a GOAT bleating proudly at the loser.
gloat.story: Gloat. To take smug pleasure in one's success or another's misfortune. When Lizzie won a promotion over her office rival, one colleague, who had once gloated over Lizzie's own failure, expected her to celebrate loudly. Instead, Lizzie brought her rival a cup of tea and told him he deserved it too. Later her mother said she was proud. "Winning is fine," she said, "but never gloat." Gloat sounds like goat: picture a goat bleating proudly over a fallen rival. So, what verb means to take smug delight in someone else's loss?... Gloat.
gloat.example: My little brother gloated for days after beating me at carrom, reminding me of the score at every meal.

gre.s: Though the challenger had every reason to ____ over his opponent's humiliating defeat, he chose to praise her courage instead.
gre.clue: he chose to praise her courage instead

implacable.story: Implacable. Unable to be calmed or satisfied; relentless. Pavel's elderly neighbour had a long feud with the man next door over a mango tree whose branches hung over the wall. For years he refused every apology, every gift of mangoes, every offer to trim the branches. Even at his grandson's wedding, he would not shake hands. He was implacable. To placate is to calm someone, so an implacable person is one no one can placate. So, what word describes anger that nothing can soften?... Implacable.
implacable.example: The landlord remained implacable, rejecting every apology and insisting that the tenants leave by Friday.

gre.s: No concession seemed enough for the ____ critic, who greeted each revision of the policy with fresh and even fiercer objections.
gre.clue: greeted each revision of the policy with fresh and even fiercer objections

insipid.hook: IN-SIPID: when you SIP it, there's no taste IN it.
insipid.story: Insipid. Having little taste; boring and lacking any spark. Janet ordered a bowl of chicken soup at a fancy downtown café. It looked beautiful, but it was insipid: no salt, no spice, no flavour at all. She thought of her mother's soup, full of ginger and green chilli. Later, the film she watched was just as insipid, with no surprises and no feeling. In means not, and the Latin root means to taste, as in savour: insipid means without taste. So, what word describes food or a film that is dull and flavourless?... Insipid.
insipid.example: Critics found the singer's new album insipid, a collection of polite love songs without a single memorable tune.

gre.s: The reviewer praised the soup's vivid spices but dismissed the dessert as ____, a sugary pudding with no discernible flavor.
gre.clue: with no discernible flavor

magnanimous.story: Magnanimous. Big-hearted and quick to forgive, even toward rivals or the weak. After Mitch's school beat its old rivals in the football final, the other team's goalkeeper sat on the grass in tears. Mitch, the winning captain, walked over, helped him up, and invited the whole team to share the victory sweets. It was a magnanimous gesture, and the two schools have been friends ever since. Magna means great and animus means spirit: magnanimous means great-spirited. So, what word describes someone generous to a defeated rival?... Magnanimous.
magnanimous.example: The chess champion was magnanimous after her win, spending an hour showing her teenage opponent where he had gone wrong.

gre.s: In victory, the general proved ____, pardoning the defeated soldiers and allowing them to return home rather than seeking revenge.
gre.clue: pardoning the defeated soldiers

myopic.hook: MYOPIC: medically, nearsighted. Only sees what's close.
myopic.story: Myopic. Short-sighted; lacking foresight or wide perspective. A factory owner near the city river saved money by pouring waste straight into the water instead of building a treatment plant. For a few years, profits rose. Then the fish died, the neighbours went to court, and the factory was shut down. Tanya, a reporter, called it a myopic decision. Medically, myopic means nearsighted, seeing only what is close; a myopic plan sees only today's profit, not tomorrow's cost. So, what word describes a plan that ignores long-term consequences?... Myopic.
myopic.example: Cutting the school library budget to repaint the gates was a myopic choice that the town would regret for years.

gre.s: Environmentalists criticized the ____ policy, which boosted this year's revenues at the cost of devastating the region's fisheries for decades.
gre.clue: at the cost of devastating the region's fisheries for decades

pensive.hook: PENSIVE: from French 'penser', to think. Lost in thought.
pensive.story: Pensive. Quietly lost in serious thought, often a little sad. On the evening before he left to study in Germany, Aaron sat alone on the roof of his family's house. He watched the sun sink over the great river, listened to the evening call to prayer, and thought about everything he would miss. His mother found him there, pensive and silent, and sat beside him without a word. Pensive comes from the French penser, to think, and a pensive face is a thinking face. So, what word describes someone deep in quiet, slightly sad thought?... Pensive.
pensive.example: After reading his grandfather's wartime letters, Arif grew pensive and spent the evening alone by the river in Rajshahi.

gre.s: The usually cheerful host was unusually ____ that evening, staring out the window and answering questions only after long pauses.
gre.clue: staring out the window and answering questions only after long pauses

pithy.hook: PITHY: like the PITH, the dense core of a fruit — all substance.
pithy.story: Pithy. Brief but full of meaning; concise and forceful. When Shelby asked her grandfather for advice before her first job, she expected a long lecture. Instead he said just six words: "Arrive early. Listen more. Promise less." She wrote them on a card and kept it on her desk for years. It was the most pithy advice she ever received. The pith is the central core of a plant stem, and the pith of an argument is its essence: pithy words are all essence. So, what word describes a short, meaningful saying?... Pithy.
pithy.example: The professor's pithy comments in the margin, often just three or four words, taught me more than any long lecture.

gre.s: Unlike her long-winded opponent, the candidate was praised for her ____ answers, which captured complex ideas in a single memorable sentence.
gre.clue: captured complex ideas in a single memorable sentence

plucky.story: Plucky. Brave and determined in difficult circumstances. Twelve-year-old Miles lives on a river island in a great river, and every morning he rows a small boat across the river to reach school, even in strong currents. When the boat sprang a leak one monsoon, he bailed out the water with a mug and kept rowing. His teachers call him the pluckiest boy in the district. Pluck is an old word for courage, so a plucky person is full of courage. So, what word describes someone small but brave and determined?... Plucky.
plucky.example: A plucky ten-year-old chess player from Narayanganj held a grandmaster to a draw in the city tournament.

gre.s: Though heavily outmatched by the professional teams, the ____ amateur squad fought for every point and refused to concede even when defeat was certain.
gre.clue: refused to concede even when defeat was certain

regress.hook: RE-GRESS: going BACK (re), the opposite of progress.
regress.story: Regress. To return to an earlier, worse, or less developed state. Seth could read English fluently by the age of ten. Then his family moved to a remote area for two years, where he had no books and no one to practise with. When he returned to school in the city, his reading had regressed, and he stumbled over simple words. With his teacher's help, he caught up within months. Re means back and gress means step, as in progress: to regress is to step backward. So, what verb means to slip back to a worse state?... Regress.
regress.example: Teachers worry that children's reading skills regress over the long summer holiday if they never open a book.

gre.s: Without regular practice, stroke patients who have relearned to speak may ____, losing words they had recovered only a few months earlier.
gre.clue: losing words they had recovered only a few months earlier

reticent.hook: RETICENT: keeps words RETAINED, held back.
reticent.story: Reticent. Quiet and unwilling to share personal thoughts or feelings. At family gatherings, Penny's father sits in a corner, sipping tea while everyone else talks. When relatives ask about his work or his health, he smiles and says only, "All is well." He has always been reticent, even with his own children. Only years later did Penny learn that he had quietly paid school fees for three neighbours' children. Reticent shares a Latin root with tacit, meaning silent: a reticent person keeps silent about himself. So, what word describes someone who keeps his feelings to himself?... Reticent.
reticent.example: The normally reticent biologist became animated and talkative once the conversation turned to frogs.

gre.s: Usually ____ about her personal life, the actress surprised interviewers by speaking openly about her childhood.
gre.clue: surprised interviewers by speaking openly

scintillating.hook: SCINTILLATING: sparkles like a tiny spark (scintilla).
scintillating.story: Scintillating. Sparkling; brilliantly lively and clever. At a city literary festival, Kendra listened to an old novelist talk about growing up in the narrow lanes of the old city. Every sentence sparkled with wit; the audience laughed one moment and fell silent the next. When she finished, the hall rose in applause. Kendra called it the most scintillating talk she had ever heard. Scintillating comes from the Latin scintilla, a spark: a scintillating talk throws off sparks of wit. So, what word describes conversation that sparkles with cleverness?... Scintillating.
scintillating.example: The final between the two chess prodigies was scintillating, full of daring sacrifices that left the commentators breathless.

gre.s: Guests looked forward to the novelist's dinner parties, where her ____ wit kept the conversation sparkling until dawn.
gre.clue: kept the conversation sparkling until dawn

skittish.hook: SKITTISH: like a SKITTERING kitten, jumps at every sound.
skittish.story: Skittish. Jumpy and quick to take fright; hard to predict. The new calf on Ellie's uncle's farm was skittish. Every time a rickshaw bell rang on the road, it leapt sideways and hid behind its mother. Ellie spent a week sitting quietly near the shed, holding out handfuls of grass, until one morning it came close enough to sniff her fingers. She held her breath. Skittish sounds like skitter, the way a nervous animal scurries away at every sound. So, what word describes an animal or person easily startled?... Skittish.
skittish.example: Investors grew skittish after the bank scandal, pulling their money out at the first hint of bad news.

gre.s: The horse was so ____ that the slightest rustle in the bushes would send it bolting across the field.
gre.clue: the slightest rustle in the bushes would send it bolting

tortuous.hook: TORTUOUS: twisted like a TORTOISE's winding path. Not torturous!
tortuous.story: Tortuous. Twisting and turning a lot; also overly complicated. The road from the coast up into the southeastern hills is famously tortuous, curving around one bend after another as it climbs. Halfway up, Tanya felt her stomach turn with every curve. Getting her passport renewed that month had been tortuous too: six offices and endless forms. Tortuous comes from the Latin for twist, as in contortion; do not confuse it with torturous, which means full of torture. So, what word describes a road or process full of twists?... Tortuous.
tortuous.example: The tortuous instructions for the new tax form left even the accountants in our office confused.

gre.s: The bill's ____ path through the legislature, marked by countless amendments, reversals, and committee delays, took nearly three years.
gre.clue: countless amendments, reversals, and committee delays

vanquish.story: Vanquish. To beat an opponent completely. In the inter-school chess final, a quiet girl named Summer faced the three-time champion. Move by move, she trapped his queen, then his rooks, until his king had nowhere left to run. The hall burst into applause. She had vanquished the champion in just thirty moves. Vanquish sounds like vanish: when you vanquish an enemy, they vanish from the contest. It also shares a Latin root with victory. So, what verb means to defeat someone completely?... Vanquish.
vanquish.example: Our school's debating team vanquished the defending champions in the final, winning the vote of every judge.

gre.s: Although the champion had seemed invincible for a decade, the young challenger managed to ____ him in just three rounds, leaving no doubt about who was superior.
gre.clue: leaving no doubt about who was superior

ameliorate.hook: AMELIORATE: 'meliorate' sounds like 'better' (meilleur in French). Make better.
ameliorate.story: Ameliorate. To make a bad situation better. Every afternoon, the road outside Tess's school turned into chaos: rickshaws, cars and children all tangled together in the heat. Then a group of parents began volunteering as crossing guards, and the school moved its closing time by fifteen minutes. The jam did not vanish, but the changes ameliorated it a great deal. Ameliorate comes from the Latin melior, meaning better, as in the French meilleur: to ameliorate is to make better. So, what verb means to improve a bad situation?... Ameliorate.
ameliorate.example: Planting trees along the busy roads of Gazipur could ameliorate the summer heat for thousands of factory workers.

gre.s: The new irrigation canals did much to ____ the effects of the drought, though they could not entirely prevent crop losses.
gre.clue: though they could not entirely prevent crop losses

antagonize.hook: ANTAGONIZE: turn someone into your ANTAGONIST (enemy).
antagonize.story: Antagonize. To cause someone to become hostile or annoyed. Rhett wanted his landlord to fix the water pump. Instead of asking politely, he sent angry messages at midnight and complained loudly on the stairs. The landlord, who had always been friendly, now refused even to answer. Rhett had antagonized the one person who could help him. In the end, his wife fixed things with a polite visit and a box of sweets. To antagonize someone is to turn them into your antagonist, the villain against you. So, what verb means to make someone hostile toward you?... Antagonize.
antagonize.example: The referee's arrogant manner antagonized both teams, and by halftime even the home fans were jeering him.

gre.s: Eager not to ____ the powerful landlords whose support he needed, the reformer softened his proposals until they offended no one.
gre.clue: until they offended no one

apogee.hook: APO-GEE: AWAY (apo) from Earth (geo), the farthest, highest point.
apogee.story: Apogee. The highest or most successful point; also, the point in an orbit farthest from Earth. Nora's grandfather played football in the city in the nineteen seventies. The apogee of his career came when he scored the winning goal in a derby before a packed stadium; he still keeps the yellowed newspaper clipping. In science class, Nora learned the other meaning: the moon's apogee is where it swings farthest from Earth. The prefix apo means away, and gee comes from the Greek for Earth, as in geography. So, what word means the high point, or the farthest point of an orbit?... Apogee.
apogee.example: Many scholars regard the reign of Shah Jahan, who built the Taj Mahal, as the apogee of Mughal architecture.

gre.s: Critics agree that the novelist's career reached its ____ with her third book; nothing she wrote afterward came close to its brilliance or its success.
gre.clue: nothing she wrote afterward came close

bawdy.story: Bawdy. Humorously rude and indecent. At a village folk play, a clown came on between the serious scenes and told bawdy jokes about husbands, wives and a runaway sarong. The men at the back roared, the aunties covered their mouths, and Henry's grandmother pretended not to hear, though her shoulders were shaking. The jokes were rude, but in a cheerful, old-fashioned way. Bawdy sounds like rowdy, and bawdy humour is rowdy and rude. So, what word describes humour that is rude but merry?... Bawdy.
bawdy.example: Chaucer's bawdy tales of millers and cheating wives still make university students blush and laugh.

gre.s: The comedian's ____ jokes, full of sexual innuendo, delighted the late-night crowd but would never have been permitted on family television.
gre.clue: full of sexual innuendo

conflagration.story: Conflagration. A large, destructive fire. One night in the old city, a fire that began in a building storing chemicals spread through the narrow lanes. Within minutes, buildings, cars and shops were burning, and the flames turned the sky orange. Julia watched from a distant rooftop, her hands pressed to her mouth. Firefighters fought the conflagration until dawn. Conflagration comes from the Latin flagrare, to burn, the same root as flagrant, which once meant blazing. So, what word means a huge, destructive fire?... Conflagration.
conflagration.example: The Great Fire of London in 1666 was a conflagration that destroyed more than thirteen thousand houses.

gre.s: What began as a small kitchen fire soon became a ____ that consumed half the town, as dry winds drove the flames from roof to roof.
gre.clue: consumed half the town

congenial.hook: CON-GENIAL: comes with a GENIAL, friendly feeling.
congenial.story: Congenial. Pleasant and friendly; well suited to one's taste or nature. When Reid moved to a hill town for his first job, he worried about living with strangers. But his new flatmates were congenial: they shared their tea, invited him on weekend trips to the tea gardens, and laughed at his terrible jokes. The quiet green town was congenial to him too, after the noise of the capital. Congenial contains genial, which means warm and friendly. So, what word describes people or a place that suits you and makes you feel at home?... Congenial.
congenial.example: Rahim found the quiet public library in Chattogram far more congenial for study than his family's noisy flat.

gre.s: Although the two scientists had been bitter rivals in print, they found each other surprisingly ____ in person, chatting amiably for hours.
gre.clue: chatting amiably for hours

delineate.story: Delineate. To describe or portray precisely; to mark the boundary of. When two brothers in Mark's village disagreed about where their land ended, a government surveyor arrived with a long measuring chain and an old map. He walked the field all afternoon and drove bamboo stakes into the mud to delineate the boundary. Then he delineated his reasons in a clear report that both brothers signed. Delineate contains line: to delineate is to draw the lines clearly. So, what verb means to mark out or describe something precisely?... Delineate.
delineate.example: The new contract clearly delineates who must pay for repairs, ending years of argument between the tenants and the owner.

gre.s: Because the old treaty failed to ____ the border precisely, both countries spent decades claiming the same narrow strip of riverbank.
gre.clue: both countries spent decades claiming the same narrow strip of riverbank

denigrate.story: Denigrate. To criticize unfairly; to belittle. Whenever Ava talked about studying fashion design, her uncle denigrated the idea. "Sewing is not a career," he said, "it is a hobby." He called her sketches childish in front of the family. Ava kept drawing anyway. Five years later, her uncle wore a suit she had designed to a wedding, and he praised it all evening. Denigrate comes from the Latin for to blacken: to denigrate someone is to blacken their name or their work. So, what verb means to unfairly belittle someone?... Denigrate.
denigrate.example: Some nineteenth-century critics denigrated photography as a mechanical trick, unworthy of being called an art.

gre.s: Rather than engage with the substance of her argument, her rivals chose to ____ her credentials, dismissing her as a mere amateur despite her decades of research.
gre.clue: dismissing her as a mere amateur

despotic.hook: DESPOTIC: a DESPOT, an all-powerful tyrant.
despotic.story: Despotic. Holding total power and often using it cruelly. In history class, Isaac read about despotic kings who could jail anyone for a single word of criticism, and whose subjects whispered even at home. That night he remembered the headmaster of his old school, who had banned talking in the corridors and punished boys for the wrong colour of socks. Even that small despotic rule had made the children miserable. A despot is an all-powerful ruler, and despotic describes the way a despot rules. So, what word describes a ruler with total, cruel power?... Despotic.
despotic.example: Under the despotic governor, newspapers were shut down and any farmer who complained about taxes risked prison.

gre.s: The new leader, who had promised a return to democracy, soon proved just as ____ as his predecessor, jailing critics and ruling by decree.
gre.clue: jailing critics and ruling by decree

diatribe.hook: DIATRIBE: a speech that would make a whole TRIBE DIE of embarrassment.
diatribe.story: Diatribe. A long, angry speech or piece of writing attacking someone. When the internet went off in the middle of the cricket final, Maddie's father called the helpline and delivered a diatribe that lasted twenty minutes. He attacked the company, its manager, its prices and even its music on hold. At last the operator said quietly, "Sir, your bill was not paid." The diatribe ended at once. Hear tribe inside diatribe: picture someone shouting angrily at a whole tribe for an hour. So, what word means a long, bitter verbal attack?... Diatribe.
diatribe.example: The retired colonel's letter to the editor was a diatribe against cyclists, whom he blamed for every traffic jam in town.

gre.s: What began as a measured critique of the policy soon devolved into a ____ against everyone who had ever supported it.
gre.clue: What began as a measured critique

droll.hook: DROLL: a DOLL that makes funny, dry jokes.
droll.story: Droll. Amusing in a dry, odd, or whimsical way. Shawn's grandfather never laughed at his own jokes. When the electricity went out during a storm, he lit a candle and said, without smiling, "Ah, at last, a romantic dinner, courtesy of the power company." Everyone burst out laughing, but his face stayed perfectly straight. His humour was always droll. Droll comes from the French drôle, meaning funny, and droll humour is quiet, dry and a little odd. So, what word describes dry, quirky humour?... Droll.
droll.example: The museum guide had a droll way of describing ancient tax collectors that kept the bored students giggling.

gre.s: The memoir's ____ observations, delivered with a perfectly straight face, had readers laughing at the most mundane details of office life.
gre.clue: had readers laughing

enchant.hook: EN-CHANT: like a magical CHANT that casts a spell.
enchant.story: Enchant. To fill with delight; to charm. On her first visit to a freshwater swamp forest in the hills, Rachel sat in a small wooden boat as it slid between trees standing in green water. Birds called overhead, and sunlight fell in pieces on the surface. She had never seen anything so lovely. The forest enchanted her completely. Enchant contains chant, like a magic song that casts a spell: when something enchants you, you are under its spell. So, what verb means to fill someone with delight, as if by magic?... Enchant.
enchant.example: The puppet show at Shilpakala Academy enchanted the children, who sat in complete silence for an hour.

gre.s: The village's winding lanes and flower-covered cottages never fail to ____ visitors, many of whom return year after year.
gre.clue: many of whom return year after year

eschew.hook: ESCHEW: sounds like a sneeze, 'ah-CHOO!' — you avoid it.
eschew.story: Eschew. To keep away from something on purpose. After his father's heart attack, Felix decided to change his own habits. He began to eschew sugar in his tea, fried snacks at the office, and late nights on his phone. At first it was hard to refuse his colleagues' samosas, but within a few months he felt lighter and stronger. Eschew sounds like a sneeze, ah choo: you turn away from a sneeze, and you eschew whatever you choose to avoid. So, what verb means to deliberately avoid something?... Eschew.
eschew.example: The young poet eschewed rhyme altogether, believing it made her verses sound like advertising jingles.

gre.s: The minimalist architect tended to ____ ornament of any kind, preferring bare concrete and plain glass.
gre.clue: preferring bare concrete and plain glass

feign.hook: FEIGN: sounds like FAKE + FAINT; fake a faint.
feign.story: Feign. To pretend to be affected by a feeling or state. On the morning of her maths test, Cindy lay in bed clutching her stomach and moaning softly. She was feigning illness. Her mother felt her forehead, found it cool, and said, "Then you will not want your favourite paratha for breakfast." Cindy sat up at once. Her feigned pain had vanished. Feign shares its Latin root with fiction: both mean to make something up. So, what verb means to pretend to feel something?... Feign.
feign.example: Mahin feigned surprise when his friends burst in with a cake, though he had overheard their plans a week earlier.

gre.s: Though secretly delighted by the news, the diplomat chose to ____ indifference so as not to reveal his government's hand.
gre.clue: so as not to reveal his government's hand

foolhardy.hook: FOOL-HARDY: a FOOL who's too HARDY for his own good.
foolhardy.story: Foolhardy. Recklessly bold or rash. Every monsoon, the news shows young men riding on the roofs of crowded trains, or taking selfies at the edge of rushing waterfalls. Aaron's cousin once tried to swim across the swollen river on a bet, and a fishing boat had to pull him out. His mother called it the most foolhardy thing he had ever done. Hardy means bold and tough, so foolhardy is the boldness of a fool. So, what word describes someone recklessly daring?... Foolhardy.
foolhardy.example: Selling the family shop to buy cryptocurrency on a stranger's tip was a foolhardy move that Kamal deeply regretted.

gre.s: Experienced mountaineers considered the attempt ____, since the climbers planned to ascend in midwinter without oxygen or guides.
gre.clue: in midwinter without oxygen or guides

impetuous.hook: IMPETUOUS: full of IMPETUS (sudden force), no brakes.
impetuous.story: Impetuous. Acting suddenly, on impulse, without thinking first. Walking through the city pet market, Natasha fell in love with a parrot that could say hello. Without asking her parents or her landlord, she bought it, a cage and a bag of seeds on the spot. That night the parrot screeched until dawn, and the landlord knocked on her door. It had been an impetuous purchase. Impetuous comes from impetus, a sudden force that pushes forward with no brakes. So, what word describes someone who acts on sudden impulse?... Impetuous.
impetuous.example: In an impetuous moment, the young batsman charged down the pitch to the very first ball and was stumped.

gre.s: The general's ____ decision to attack before reinforcements arrived, made in a moment of anger, cost him the battle.
gre.clue: made in a moment of anger

interminable.story: Interminable. Seemingly endless; tediously long. Hank's flight to Toronto had a twelve-hour stopover in a quiet airport. He walked every corridor, read every sign, and drank four cups of bad coffee, but the clock barely moved. The wait felt interminable. Then the second flight was delayed, and the interminable day grew even longer. In means not, and terminate means to end: interminable describes something that seems to have no end. So, what word describes a wait that seems to go on forever?... Interminable.
interminable.example: Stuck in an interminable traffic jam on the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway, Shirin finished an entire novel.

gre.s: Audiences who had expected a brisk thriller found the film ____: its three-hour running time was padded with lengthy scenes in which almost nothing happened.
gre.clue: padded with lengthy scenes in which almost nothing happened

levity.story: Levity. A joking attitude toward something that deserves seriousness. At the hospital where Lucy's father was having surgery, the family waited in silence. Then her young cousin began making jokes about the hospital food and the doctor's moustache. Her aunt gave him a sharp look. This was not the time for levity. Later, when the surgery went well, a little levity was finally welcome. Levity comes from the Latin levis, light, as in levitate: levity treats heavy things too lightly. So, what word means inappropriate lightness about something serious?... Levity.
levity.example: The judge warned that any further levity in the courtroom would be treated as contempt.

gre.s: The speaker's ____ seemed badly misjudged; his jokes about the earthquake offended an audience that had gathered to mourn its victims.
gre.clue: an audience that had gathered to mourn its victims

malfeasance.story: Malfeasance. Illegal or dishonest acts by someone in an official post. A government engineer in Russell's district approved a new school building made with half the steel the design required, and quietly pocketed the rest of the money. When cracks appeared within a year, investigators traced the paperwork back to him. He was charged with malfeasance and dismissed. Mal means bad, as in malpractice, and feasance comes from the French for doing: malfeasance is bad doing by an official. So, what word means wrongdoing by a public official?... Malfeasance.
malfeasance.example: Investigators found evidence of malfeasance at the port authority, where officials had been taking bribes to release cargo uninspected.

gre.s: Once celebrated as a reformer, the mayor left office in disgrace after an inquiry uncovered years of ____, including bribery and the theft of public funds.
gre.clue: including bribery and the theft of public funds

malign.hook: MAL = bad. To say bad things about someone.
malign.story: Malign. As a verb, to speak harmful untruths about someone. As an adjective, evil or harmful. When Tom opened a small bakery that quickly became popular, a rival shop owner began to malign him, telling customers that Tom used stale flour and dirty water. None of it was true. Tom invited everyone to watch him bake in his open kitchen, and the rumours died. Those who malign others often reveal their own malign intentions. Mal means bad: to malign someone is to speak badly of them. So, what verb means to spread harmful lies about someone?... Malign.
malign.example: Anonymous accounts maligned the young cricketer online, falsely claiming that he had taken money to lose matches.

gre.s: Although tabloids continue to ____ the senator as corrupt, every investigation into her finances has found nothing improper.
gre.clue: every investigation into her finances has found nothing improper

onetime.hook: ONETIME: ONE TIME in the past.
onetime.story: Onetime. Former. In a small tea shop, Megan met an old man who quietly mentioned that he was a onetime member of the national football team. Now he sells tea and biscuits, and few customers know his past. He showed her a faded photograph from his playing days, and his eyes shone. Do not confuse onetime with a one-time event that happens only once; a onetime champion was a champion once, in the past. So, what word means former, as in someone who once held a role?... Onetime.
onetime.example: Sabina, a onetime nurse, now runs a small bakery in Uttara that is famous for its mango cakes.

gre.s: The senator, a ____ ally of the president, has become one of his fiercest critics since their bitter public quarrel over the budget last year.
gre.clue: has become one of his fiercest critics

philistine.hook: PHILISTINE: thinks a museum is a waste of land.
philistine.story: Philistine. A person hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts. When the old art college building in Caleb's town was set to be demolished for a car park, one businessman laughed. "Paintings do not feed anyone," he said. "Give me parking." Caleb, an art student, felt hurt. To him the man was a philistine, blind to everything beautiful the building had nurtured. In the Bible, the Philistines were enemies of the Israelites, and nineteenth-century writers borrowed the name for people who scorn culture. So, what word describes someone who has no time for art?... Philistine.
philistine.example: Only a philistine would cover the wall of a centuries-old terracotta temple with advertising posters.

gre.s: Dismissing the museum as a waste of public money, the mayor revealed himself to be a ____, indifferent to the paintings and sculptures that had made the city famous.
gre.clue: indifferent to the paintings and sculptures

plodding.hook: PLODDING: the PLOD-PLOD sound of tired, heavy footsteps.
plodding.story: Plodding. Slow, heavy, and monotonous; working steadily but without inspiration. Paula's history textbook was plodding: page after page of dates and names, with no stories and no pictures. She fell asleep over it every night. Her classmate's plodding effort, though, paid off; he read slowly, ten pages a day, and never missed one. Plod is the sound of tired, heavy footsteps, plod, plod, plod, and plodding work moves at that same heavy pace. So, what word describes something slow, steady and dull?... Plodding.
plodding.example: The biography's plodding chapters on tax records nearly made me give up before reaching the exciting war years.

gre.s: Critics praised the film's acting but found its ____ pace exhausting, as scenes dragged on long after their point had been made.
gre.clue: scenes dragged on long after their point had been made

precipitous.hook: PRECIPITOUS: like a PRECIPICE, a sheer cliff.
precipitous.story: Precipitous. Dangerously steep; sudden and dramatic. On a trek up a remote mountain, Sabrina reached a narrow path along a precipitous slope, with a sheer drop to the jungle below. She pressed her back to the rock and inched forward. That same month, the price of tomatoes made a precipitous fall after a bumper harvest. Precipitous is linked to precipice, a sheer cliff; do not confuse it with precipitate, which describes a rash action. So, what word describes a slope or drop that is dangerously steep?... Precipitous.
precipitous.example: After the mill closed, the town's population suffered a precipitous fall, from forty thousand to barely ten thousand.

gre.s: The company's decline was ____: in a single quarter, its share price fell by ninety percent, wiping out a decade of steady growth.
gre.clue: in a single quarter

prosaic.hook: PROSAIC: like plain PROSE, not poetry.
prosaic.story: Prosaic. Ordinary and dull; lacking imagination. Trey asked his grandfather how he had met his grandmother, hoping for a love story full of monsoon rain and poetry. "We met at the post office," his grandfather said. "She was in the queue before me." That was all. It was a prosaic answer, but his grandmother smiled across the room as if it were the most beautiful story in the world. Prosaic comes from prose, plain writing rather than poetry. So, what word describes something ordinary and unpoetic?... Prosaic.
prosaic.example: The famous painter's daily routine turned out to be prosaic, with breakfast at seven, work until noon, and an afternoon nap.

gre.s: Fans expecting a dramatic explanation for the band's breakup were disappointed by the ____ truth: the members had simply grown tired of touring.
gre.clue: had simply grown tired of touring

quandary.story: Quandary. A state of uncertainty over what to do in a difficult situation. Shelby received two offers on the same day: a scholarship to study in Japan, and a good job at home near her ageing parents. Taking one meant losing the other. For a week she barely slept. She was in a real quandary. Finally, her mother told her to go, and promised to call every night. Quandary sounds like wander, and in a quandary your mind wanders back and forth, unable to choose. So, what word means being stuck between difficult choices?... Quandary.
quandary.example: The referee faced a quandary when the floodlights failed with the scores level and only two minutes left to play.

gre.s: The doctor faced a genuine ____: revealing the diagnosis might devastate the fragile patient, yet concealing it would violate her duty of honesty.
gre.clue: revealing the diagnosis might devastate the fragile patient, yet concealing it would violate

ravage.hook: RAVAGE: like a RAVENOUS SAVAGE destroying everything.
ravage.story: Ravage. To damage or destroy something badly over a wide area. In the spring of two thousand seventeen, flash floods ravaged the great northeastern wetlands. In a few days the water swallowed most of the rice harvest, months of work gone. Adam's uncle stood at the edge of his field and saw only grey water where golden paddy had been. Ravage sounds like savage: ravaging forces destroy savagely and widely. So, what verb means to cause widespread destruction?... Ravage.
ravage.example: Years of civil war had ravaged the country's roads, so aid trucks needed four days to cover two hundred kilometres.

gre.s: Unless farmers act quickly to control the locusts, the swarms will ____ the region's crops, leaving little to harvest and threatening famine.
gre.clue: leaving little to harvest

sanctimonious.hook: SANCTIMONIOUS: acts like a SAINT, but it's all for MONEY and show.
sanctimonious.story: Sanctimonious. Making a show of being morally superior to others. At a family gathering, Roxanne's uncle lectured everyone about honesty, saying young people today had no morals. He spoke loudly so the neighbours could hear. Roxanne knew that the same uncle had cheated his own brother out of a plot of land. His sanctimonious speech made her feel sick. Sanct means holy, as in sanctuary and saint: a sanctimonious person puts on a show of holiness. So, what word describes someone smugly preaching about their own goodness?... Sanctimonious.
sanctimonious.example: My cousin's sanctimonious posts about healthy eating would be easier to bear if he did not eat fuchka every evening.

gre.s: Voters grew tired of the senator's ____ speeches about honesty, particularly after he was caught concealing his own debts.
gre.clue: after he was caught concealing his own debts

scrupulous.hook: SCRUPULOUS: has SCRUPLES, a moral conscience.
scrupulous.story: Scrupulous. Very careful to do what is right; extremely attentive to detail. When a customer at Isaac's small grocery shop accidentally paid him twenty dollars too much, Isaac noticed only that evening. He walked two kilometres in the rain to return it. In the shop he is just as scrupulous, weighing every bag of rice twice. A scruple was once a tiny sharp stone, the kind that gets into your sandal; a scrupulous person feels every small wrong, like that stone. So, what word describes someone careful to be honest and exact?... Scrupulous.
scrupulous.example: Scrupulous record keeping let the laboratory trace every blood sample back to the exact patient and hour.

gre.s: The biographer was ____ about sources, refusing to include any anecdote that she could not verify with at least two documents.
gre.clue: refusing to include any anecdote that she could not verify

staid.hook: STAID: STAYED the same forever, never adventurous.
staid.story: Staid. Serious, respectable, and unadventurous. Nancy's father has worn the same grey trousers to the same bank office for twenty-five years. He eats dinner at nine, reads the same newspaper, and goes to bed at half past ten. So when he announced on his birthday that he wanted a motorbike trip to the southeastern hills, the family was stunned. Even the most staid man has a spark in him. Staid is an old spelling of stayed: a staid person has always stayed the same. So, what word describes someone serious, steady and never adventurous?... Staid.
staid.example: The staid old bank surprised its customers by hiring a rapper to star in its new advertising campaign.

gre.s: Once known for its ____ coverage of parliamentary procedure, the newspaper has lately reinvented itself with splashy headlines and celebrity gossip.
gre.clue: has lately reinvented itself with splashy headlines and celebrity gossip

acrimonious.hook: ACRIMONIOUS: ACRID, as bitter as acid.
acrimonious.story: Acrimonious. Angry and bitter in speech or debate. At a residents' meeting in a city apartment building, the question was simple: who would pay to fix the broken lift? Within ten minutes, neighbours who had shared holiday sweets for years were shouting across the room, pointing fingers and dragging up old complaints about parking. Little Isla watched from the stairs, shocked at how acrimonious grown-ups could be. The acrimonious meeting ended with slammed doors. Acrimonious shares its root with acrid, meaning sharp and bitter, like burning smoke. So, what word describes a debate full of bitter, angry words?... Acrimonious.
acrimonious.example: The acrimonious split between the band's two founders played out for months in newspaper interviews and courtrooms.

gre.s: What began as a friendly disagreement between the two scholars grew increasingly ____, until each was publicly accusing the other of fraud.
gre.clue: publicly accusing the other of fraud

astringent.hook: ASTRINGENT: like a STRINGENT, tight squeeze, harsh.
astringent.story: Astringent. Sharply severe or critical; also, making skin tissue tighten. After a shave, the old barber in Adam's neighbourhood rubs a block of alum on his cheek, and the skin stings and pulls tight. Alum is an astringent. Years later, Adam's thesis draft comes back from his supervisor with sharp remarks on every page. Careless. Vague. Unsupported. The comments sting just like that alum, yet every one is fair. Astringent sounds like stringent, meaning strict, and both come from a Latin verb meaning to bind tight. So, what word describes criticism so sharp it stings?... Astringent.
astringent.example: Her astringent comments on the committee's draft, though painful to hear, saved the project from several costly errors.

gre.s: The critic's ____ reviews, which spared neither famous names nor beginners, made her the most feared voice in the literary world.
gre.clue: spared neither famous names nor beginners

axiomatic.hook: AXIOM: a basic truth in math, needing no proof.
axiomatic.story: Axiomatic. Self-evident; accepted as true without proof. Mandy's grandmother never studied economics, but she has run the family kitchen for fifty years on a few firm rules. Buy fish early, before the best ones are gone. Never trust a seller who will not let you touch the vegetables. To her, these truths are axiomatic. If you asked her for proof, she would only shake her head. An axiom is a basic truth in geometry, accepted without proof. So, what word describes a truth so obvious that no one needs to prove it?... Axiomatic.
axiomatic.example: Among good cooks it is axiomatic that fresh ingredients matter more than any fancy technique.

gre.s: It was once considered ____ that the sun revolved around the earth, a truth so plain that no one thought to question it, yet the assumption proved entirely false.
gre.clue: so plain that no one thought to question it

capitulate.story: Capitulate. To surrender or give in after resisting. For a whole week, a thin grey kitten cried outside the gate of Laila's house. Every evening Laila begged to keep it, and every evening her father said no. Then came a night of heavy rain. Her father opened the door, looked at the shivering kitten, and carried it inside himself. After seven days of refusing, he had capitulated. Capitulate comes from the Latin for head, like capital, because terms of surrender were once written out under headings. So, what verb means to finally give in after holding out?... Capitulate.
capitulate.example: After three hours of pleading from the twins, their mother capitulated and bought them ice cream before dinner.

gre.s: After months of insisting that it would never negotiate, the management finally chose to ____ to the union's demands when the strike began to cripple production.
gre.clue: when the strike began to cripple production

chastise.hook: CHASTISE: CHASE them with words until they're CHASTE (corrected).
chastise.story: Chastise. To scold someone sharply for doing wrong. Roy took his father's motorbike out at midnight without asking and came back with a dented mudguard. At breakfast, his father did not shout. He spoke slowly and sharply about trust, about danger, about Roy's mother lying awake. Roy stared at his paratha, his ears burning. He had never been chastised so thoroughly. Chastise comes from the same Latin root as chaste, meaning pure, as if a good scolding cleans out the fault. So, what verb means to scold someone sharply for a wrong?... Chastise.
chastise.example: The captain chastised her players for arriving late to training, reminding them that discipline wins tournaments.

gre.s: Far from praising the minister's handling of the flood, the committee's report went out of its way to ____ him for delays that had cost lives.
gre.clue: Far from praising

chivalrous.hook: CHIVALROUS: like a medieval knight's CHIVALRY.
chivalrous.story: Chivalrous. Courteous, gallant and honourable, especially toward women. One rainy evening downtown, the street flooded knee-deep. An elderly woman and her granddaughter stood stranded at the edge, clutching their shopping bags. A young delivery rider parked his bicycle, carried their bags across, then came back and gave the old woman his arm, step by careful step. He would not take a single cent. It was a chivalrous act, and the people watching smiled. Chivalry was the code of medieval knights, and the word comes from the French for horseman. So, what word describes gallant, honourable courtesy?... Chivalrous.
chivalrous.example: In a chivalrous gesture, the champion helped his fallen opponent to his feet before raising his own arms in victory.

gre.s: In an age of cynicism, the soldier's ____ treatment of his captured enemies, whom he fed and sheltered, astonished his comrades.
gre.clue: whom he fed and sheltered

defame.story: Defame. To damage someone's reputation with false statements. Keith ran a small sweet shop in town, known for its creamy yogurt. A rival began spreading a rumour that Keith mixed chalk into his yoghurt. It was a lie, but customers drifted away, and Keith sat alone behind his counter. When the rival was caught and fined, everyone saw how cruelly he had tried to defame an honest man. Hidden inside defame is fame, your good name; to defame someone is to tear that name down. So, what verb means to ruin a reputation with false claims?... Defame.
defame.example: The newspaper paid heavy damages after a court ruled that it had defamed a Sylhet surgeon with invented accusations.

gre.s: The politician's opponents sought to ____ him by spreading fabricated stories of corruption, hoping voters would believe the lies before they could be disproved.
gre.clue: spreading fabricated stories of corruption

efficacious.story: Efficacious. Working well and producing the result that was wanted. When little Zach caught a stomach bug one hot June, his grandmother did not panic. She mixed a packet of oral saline into clean water and fed it to him spoon by spoon. By evening he was sitting up, asking for biscuits. Researchers in South Asia helped prove, decades ago, how efficacious this simple drink is, and it has saved millions of children around the world. Efficacious is a formal cousin of effective; both come from the Latin for to accomplish. So, what word describes a remedy that truly works?... Efficacious.
efficacious.example: Across much of Africa, cheap insecticide-treated bed nets rank among the most efficacious tools public health workers have against malaria.

gre.s: The manufacturer touted the supplement as highly ____, yet independent trials showed that it relieved symptoms no better than a sugar pill.
gre.clue: relieved symptoms no better than a sugar pill

embellish.hook: EMBELLISH: add BELLS to it, decorate.
embellish.story: Embellish. To decorate; also, to add details, often untrue, to make a story more exciting. Every winter, Seth's uncle tells the story of crossing the great river in a storm. First the waves were tall. The next year they were taller than the boat. By this winter, a crocodile was chasing them, and the children shrieked. Uncle embellishes his tale the way Seth's mother embellishes a patchwork quilt, stitch by stitch. Hidden in embellish is the French belle, beautiful: to embellish is to make something prettier. So, what verb means to decorate a story with added details?... Embellish.
embellish.example: The job candidate embellished his résumé, turning a two-week internship into a year of senior management experience.

gre.s: The journalist was dismissed when editors discovered her habit of choosing to ____ her reports with vivid quotations that no source had ever actually spoken.
gre.clue: vivid quotations that no source had ever actually spoken

encyclopedic.hook: ENCYCLOPEDIC: like an ENCYCLOPEDIA, knows everything.
encyclopedic.story: Encyclopedic. Wide-ranging and thorough, covering almost every part of a subject. In the crowded lanes of the book market, an old bookseller named Reuben has a stall stacked to the ceiling. Ask him for a used chemistry guide or a rare poetry collection, and he climbs his ladder and pulls it out in a minute, dust and all. Piper once tested him with three forgotten titles.
