gre.s: The mood at the reunion was ____, with old friends laughing and singing late into the night, utterly unlike the somber gathering the organizers had feared.
gre.clue: laughing and singing late into the night

manacle.hook: MAN-ACLE: shackles on a MAN's hands (manus).
manacle.story: Manacle. A metal cuff locked around a prisoner's wrist; as a verb, to bind or restrict. At a museum display about the old colonial jails, Laura stopped before a pair of rusted iron manacles. They looked heavy enough to bruise any wrist. Her grandfather, standing beside her, said quietly that debt can manacle a family just as tightly, for generations. Laura thought about that all the way home. Manacle comes from the Latin manus, meaning hand, as in manual: manacles are chains for the hands. So, what noun means a metal cuff that locks a prisoner's hands?... Manacle.
manacle.example: Old colonial records describe how rebel peasants were manacled together and marched to the district jail.

gre.s: Rather than liberating the workers, the new contracts seemed designed to ____ them, binding them to the company with debts they could never repay.
gre.clue: binding them to the company with debts they could never repay

mettlesome.hook: METTLESOME: full of METAL, tough spirit. To test your METTLE.
mettlesome.story: Mettlesome. Full of spirit and courage. In a village football final, the girls' team from Rachel's school faced players a head taller than them. Within ten minutes they were a goal down. Yet they kept running, tackling and calling to each other, and in the last minute their small striker, Sophie, curled the ball into the corner. The crowd poured onto the field. What a mettlesome team. Mettle was once simply another spelling of metal: a mettlesome person has a spirit as tough as iron. So, what word describes someone full of courage and fight?... Mettlesome.
mettlesome.example: The mettlesome horse refused to be led into the trailer and kept two stable hands busy for an hour.

gre.s: Although she was the smallest player on the team, she was also the most ____, diving for every ball and never backing down from a challenge.
gre.clue: never backing down from a challenge

nettlesome.hook: NETTLE is a stinging plant. NETTLESOME = stings and annoys.
nettlesome.story: Nettlesome. Causing annoyance or difficulty. At midnight, a single mosquito found Andy in his dorm bed. It whined beside his ear, vanished when he switched on the light, and returned the moment he lay down again. He slapped his own cheek twice. By three in the morning, that tiny insect had become the most nettlesome creature on earth. A nettle is a plant whose leaves sting the skin, so a nettlesome thing stings and irritates you, again and again. So, what word describes something small but persistently irritating?... Nettlesome.
nettlesome.example: Settling the nettlesome question of who would pay for the shared water tank took the building residents three meetings.

gre.s: The software update was meant to fix a ____ glitch that had irritated users for months, causing the screen to freeze at random.
gre.clue: that had irritated users for months

objurgation.hook: OBJURGATION: OBJECTION + a JURY's harsh verdict.
objurgation.story: Objurgation. A harsh scolding or rebuke. When Ross came home at two in the morning after racing motorbikes on the highway, his grandfather was waiting at the gate with a lantern. He spoke, slowly and sharply, for half an hour, about the boys who had died on that road and the mother who had stayed awake praying. Ross never forgot that objurgation. Objurgation comes from a Latin verb meaning to scold, and you can hear an urge in it: an objurgation urges you hard to change. So, what noun means a harsh, scolding rebuke?... Objurgation.
objurgation.example: The headmaster's public objurgation of the boys who had broken the window could be heard across the entire playground.

gre.s: Expecting a mild reprimand for his error, the junior clerk was stunned by the manager's ____, a furious tirade delivered in front of the entire staff.
gre.clue: a furious tirade delivered in front of the entire staff

ossify.hook: OSSIFY: turn to bone (os = bone, as in osteo).
ossify.story: Ossify. To harden into bone; also, to become rigid and unchanging. When Sheldon's grandfather founded the village library in the nineteen seventies, it buzzed with new ideas: night classes, film shows, debates. Fifty years later, the same committee members sit in the same chairs, approve the same old books, and reject every suggestion from the young. The library has ossified. Os means bone in Latin, as in osteoporosis: to ossify is to turn as hard and stiff as bone. So, what verb means to become rigid and set in one's ways?... Ossify.
ossify.example: Without fresh ideas from younger writers, literary magazines can ossify into clubs that publish the same few names forever.

gre.s: Without new members to challenge its assumptions, the once innovative movement began to ____, clinging rigidly to doctrines it had long ago stopped questioning.
gre.clue: clinging rigidly to doctrines

peccadillo.hook: PECCADILLO: a tiny sin, small as an armadillo.
peccadillo.story: Peccadillo. A small, unimportant sin or fault. Every holiday, Monica's grandmother hid a box of cream sweets at the back of the fridge for the guests. And every holiday, Monica's father crept into the kitchen at midnight and ate two. When the grandmother counted the box the next morning, she only rolled her eyes and smiled. It was a peccadillo, too small to punish. Peccadillo comes from the Latin peccare, to sin, the root of impeccable, meaning without sin: a peccadillo is just a tiny one. So, what noun means a small, forgivable fault?... Peccadillo.
peccadillo.example: My grandmother forgave our childhood peccadilloes, such as stealing pickles from her jars, with nothing more than a scolding look.

gre.s: Supporters dismissed the scandal as a mere ____, but investigators soon showed that the senator's misconduct was neither minor nor isolated.
gre.clue: dismissed the scandal as a mere

penurious.story: Penurious. Extremely poor; also, very stingy. When Rick first came to the city from a northern village, he was penurious. He slept on a mat in a crowded room in a riverside slum, ate rice with salt and a green chilli, and walked an hour to the factory to save the bus fare. Every spare dollar went home to his mother. Ten years later he owns a small tailoring shop, but he still remembers those penurious years. Penurious comes from penury, the Latin word for want and scarcity. So, what word describes someone living in extreme poverty?... Penurious.
penurious.example: As a penurious student in Kolkata, the future novelist often skipped dinner so that he could buy secondhand books.

gre.s: Despite his considerable fortune, the old collector was so ____ that he refused to heat his house in winter and haggled fiercely over the price of bread.
gre.clue: refused to heat his house in winter

pertinacious.hook: PERTINACIOUS: PER-TENACIOUS, tenacious through and through.
pertinacious.story: Pertinacious. Holding on firmly; stubbornly persistent. A young reporter named Tanya wanted one interview with the head of a company accused of polluting a river. His office refused. She emailed every week for six months, waited outside the gate on rainy mornings, and phoned his assistant so often that they began to swap recipes. At last the door opened. She had been pertinacious. Pertinacious contains tenacious, meaning holding fast, with per meaning thoroughly: a pertinacious person is thoroughly tenacious. So, what word describes someone who refuses to give up?... Pertinacious.
pertinacious.example: A pertinacious reporter filed request after request until the ministry finally released the hidden audit reports.

gre.s: The lawyer's ____ questioning, which continued long after the witness had begun to falter, eventually produced a confession.
gre.clue: continued long after the witness had begun to falter

premeditate.hook: PRE-MEDITATE: MEDITATE on it BEFORE doing it.
premeditate.story: Premeditate. To plan something in advance, often a crime. The robbery at a small-town jewellery shop looked sudden: masked men, a broken glass case, a getaway motorbike. But the police found that the thieves had rented a room opposite the shop two months earlier, timed the guard's tea breaks, and mapped every camera. Nothing about it was spontaneous. The crime was carefully premeditated. Pre means before, and meditate means to think: to premeditate is to think something out beforehand. So, what verb means to plan an act, especially a crime, in advance?... Premeditate.
premeditate.example: Nothing about Rina's surprise birthday party was spontaneous, since her friends had premeditated every detail over three weeks of secret messages.

gre.s: The prosecution argued that the defendant had taken weeks to ____ the crime, pointing to receipts for tools bought a month earlier.
gre.clue: pointing to receipts for tools bought a month earlier

raillery.hook: RAILLERY: friends RALLY around you with jokes.
raillery.story: Raillery. Light, friendly teasing. When Jordan walked into the tea stall with his first stylish haircut, short at the sides and stiff with gel, his friends burst into applause. One asked if he was going to a wedding, another asked whose wedding, and a third offered to carry his autograph book. Jordan laughed hardest of all. It was raillery among old friends, warm and without any sting. Raillery comes from a French verb meaning to tease, so raillery is teasing done with affection. So, what noun means good-humoured teasing?... Raillery.
raillery.example: The cousins' raillery about who had gained the most weight since last Eid kept the whole family laughing.

gre.s: The two old rivals enjoyed a long tradition of affectionate ____, trading gentle jokes about each other's age and failing memory whenever they met.
gre.clue: trading gentle jokes

recrudescent.story: Recrudescent. Breaking out again after a quiet period. For years, the quarrel between Sasha's father and his brother over their grandfather's pond seemed forgotten. They shared holiday meals and even laughed together. Then a new road was announced beside the pond, and its value tripled overnight. Within a week, the old dispute was recrudescent, angrier than ever. Recrudescent comes from a Latin word meaning to become raw again, related to crude: an old wound turns raw once more. So, what word describes a problem flaring up again after it seemed healed?... Recrudescent.
recrudescent.example: Health officers in Cox's Bazar grew alarmed at recrudescent cases of diphtheria, a disease the region had thought defeated years earlier.

gre.s: Just when historians had declared the old nationalist rivalries extinct, a ____ wave of ethnic hostility swept the region, reviving conflicts dormant for half a century.
gre.clue: reviving conflicts dormant for half a century

sedulous.hook: SEDULOUS: SEATED-ulous, seated at the desk all day, diligently working.
sedulous.story: Sedulous. Diligent and dedicated; working steadily and carefully. Every morning at five, before her family woke, Rosie sat at the kitchen table of their city flat with a cup of tea and her GRE word list. She reviewed thirty words, wrote each in a sentence, and tested herself again on the bus home from work. She did this for six months without missing a day. Her sedulous effort paid off. To remember sedulous, picture someone seated at a desk, hour after hour, never giving up. So, what word describes steady, diligent work?... Sedulous.
sedulous.example: The museum's sedulous restorers spent two years cleaning a single Mughal manuscript, one tiny brushstroke at a time.

gre.s: Only through ____ effort, poring over thousands of documents for more than a decade, did the historian reconstruct the lost trade route.
gre.clue: poring over thousands of documents for more than a decade

stinting.hook: STINTING: giving only a tiny STINT.
stinting.story: Stinting. Ungenerous; giving as little as possible. The owner of a student hostel in the city was famously stinting. He let the water pump run for only one hour a day, removed every second light bulb from the corridors, and served dal so thin that the students joked they could read through it. Asked for a study room fan, he offered a hand fan. To stint is to hold back, so a stinting person holds back everything, while a generous one gives without stint. So, what word describes someone mean and sparing in what they give?... Stinting.
stinting.example: The company's stinting approach to safety gear meant that workers shared a few helmets between entire shifts.

gre.s: Critics accused the government of being ____ with flood relief: families that had lost everything received barely a week's rations.
gre.clue: received barely a week's rations

upbraid.hook: UP-BRAID: grab someone's BRAID and pull them UP for a scolding.
upbraid.story: Upbraid. To scold someone sharply for something they did wrong. Ralph's football team arrived at training forty minutes late, laughing and eating spicy snacks. The coach blew his whistle and waited until they were silent. Then he upbraided them: they had lost two matches in a row, the season was slipping away, and they were treating it like a picnic. Not one player looked up. The next morning, everyone arrived early. Picture someone pulled up by the braid for a telling off: to upbraid is to reprimand. So, what verb means to scold someone sharply?... Upbraid.
upbraid.example: Nafisa's mother upbraided her for lending the family car to a friend who had no driving license.

gre.s: The editor would ____ any reporter who missed a deadline, sometimes in front of the entire newsroom.
gre.clue: sometimes in front of the entire newsroom
